lessons.la: Francisca nobilis matrona Romana, ab ineunte ætate illustria dedit virtutum exempla: etenim pueriles ludos et illecebras mundi respuens, solitudine et oratione magni. pere delectabatur. Undecim annos nata, virginitatem suam Deo consecrare, et monasterium ingredi proposuit: p, réntum tamen voluntati humiliter obtemperans, Laurentio de Pontianis, juveni eque di. viti ac nobili nupsit. In matrimonio arctioris vitæ propositum, quantum licuit, semper retinuit: a spectaculis, con. vítiis aliisque hujusmodi ob. lectaméntis abhorrens, lanea ac vulgari veste utens, et quid. quid a domesticis curis supererat temporis, orationi aut proximorum utilitati tribuens: in id vero maxima sollicitudine incumbens, ut matronas Romanas a pompis sæculi et ornatus vanitate revocaret. Quapropter domum Oblatarum, sub regula sancti Benedicti, congregationis Montis Oliveti, adhuc viro alligata, in Urbe instituit. Viri exsilium, bonorum jacturam, ac uni vérse domus mœrorem non modo constantissime toleravit: sed gratias agens cum beato Job, illud frequenter usurpabat: Dominus dedit, Dominus abstulit: sit nomen Domini benedictum.

ye defuncto, ad prædictam Oblatarum domum convolans, nudis pedibus, fune ad collum alligato, humi prostrata, multis cum lacrimis earum numero adscribi suppliciter postulavit. Voti compos facta, licet esset omnium mater, non alio tamen quam ar. cille vilissimæque feminæ, et immunditiæ vasculi titulo gloriabatur. Quam vilem sui existimationem et verbo declaravit et exemplo: sæpe enim e suburbana vinea revertens, et lignorum fascem proprio cáii impositum deferens, vel eisdem onustum agens per Urbem asellum, pauperibus subveniebat, in quos étiam largas eleemosynas erogabat: ægrotantesque in xenodochiis visitans, non corporali tantum cibo, sed salutaribus monitis recreabat. Corpus suum vigiliis, jejuniis, cilicio, ferreo cingulo, crebrisque flagellis in servitutem redigere jugiter satagebat. Cibum illi semel in die herba et legumina, aqua potum præbuit. Hos tamen corporis cruciatus aliquando confessarii mandato, a cujus ore nutuque pendebat, modice temperavit.
lessons.en: On her husband's death she (in 1437) betook herself immediately to the house of the Oblates, and, with her feet bare and a rope round her neck, threw herself down on the threshold, entreating the sisters with tears to receive her into their number. When she obtained her wish, although she was the mother of them all, she would be among them only as one that served, glorying rather to be called the most degraded of women and a vessel of uncleanness. Her lowly esteem of herself was shown both by her word and example. She passed often through the city from a vineyard in the country carrying a bundle of sticks on her head, or driving an ass laden with faggots; she succoured the needy, for whom she collected large alms, and visited the sick in the hospitals, ministering to them both food for the body and exhortations healthful for their souls. She strove continually to bring her body into subjection by watchings, fastings, haircloth, the wearing of an iron girdle, and the often use of a scourge. She never ate but once a day, and then only vegetables, and she took no drink but water. These severities she however sometimes relaxed, in obedience to her confessor, on whose word and wishes she framed her customs.

lessons.la: Iyyw mysteria, præsertim vero Christi Domini passionem, tanto mentis ardore, tantaque lacrimarum vi contemplabatur, ut præ doloris magnitudine pene confici videretur. Sæpe étiam cum oraret, maxime sumpto sanctissimæ Eucharistiæ sacramento, spiritu in Deum elevata, ac cælestium contemplatione rapta, immobilis permanebat. Quapropter humani generis hostis variis eam contumeliis ac verberibus a proposito dimovere conabatur: quem tamen illa imperterrita semper elusit; Angeli præsertim præsidio, cujus familiari consuetudine gloriosum de eo triumphum reportavit. Gratia curationum et prophetiæ dono enituit, quo et futura prædixit, et cordium secreta penetravit. Non semel aquæ, vel per rivum decurrentes, vel e cælo labentes, intactam prorsus, dum Deo vacaret, reliquerunt. Modica panis fragmenta, quæ vix tribus sororibus reficiendis fuíssent satis, sic ejus precibus Dominus multiplicavit, ut quindecim inde exsaturatis, tantum superfuerit, ut canistrum impleverit: et aliquando earumdem sororum, extra Urbem mense Januario ligna parantium, sitim recentis uvæ racemis ex vite in arbore pendentibus mirabiliter obtentis, abunde explévit. Denique meritis et miraculis clara, migravit ad Dominum, anno ætatis suæ quinquagesimo sexto. Quam Paulus quintus Pontifex Maximus in Sanctorum numerum retulit.
lessons.en: So great was her mental realisation of the things of God, and chiefly of the sufferings of the Lord Christ, and so abundant her tears in contemplating them, that she seemed sometimes about to sink under her grief. Often when she was engaged in prayer, and principally after she had received the Most Holy Sacrament of the Eucharist, her spirit became altogether lifted up to God, and she remained motionless, carried away by the thought of heavenly things. The enemy of man assailed her with diverse reproaches and buffetings to break her off her intent, but she feared him not, and with the help of an Angel whom God gave her to be her familiar friend, she won a noble victory over the tempter. God glorified her with the gifts of healing and of prophecy, whereby she foretold things to come, and saw the secrets of the hearts of men. More than once while her thoughts were busy in God she remained unwet by streams or rain. When there was left only bread enough for three sisters, the Lord at her prayers was pleased so to multiply it, that fifteen had enough, and the basket was filled again with the fragments. In the month of January also, when the sisters were gathering sticks in the country, and were thirsty, she satisfied them abundantly with bunches of fresh grapes from a tree. She departed to be with the Lord, famous for good works and miracles, in the fifty-sixth year of her age, (upon the 9th day of March, in the year of our Lord 1440.) The Supreme Pontiff Paul V. caused her to be numbered among the saints.

lessons.la: ETRUS nóbili família de JeP remía Panórmi natus, Bonóniam adoléscens missus est, ut utríque Juri óperam daret. Doctorátus insígnia in utráque facultáte mox consecutiúrus, ceeléstium amóre ductus, terréna cuncta despíciens, ea in urbe ingréssus est Órdinem Fratrum Przedicatórum. Patrem, id ægre feréntem sibíque ácrater obsisténtem, magna ánimi constántia, sed fusis potíssimum lácrimis et précibus ad Deum, tandem devícit. Religiósis exínde votis solémniter nuncupátis, ac theologíe divinarúmque litterárum stúdiis explétis, uni se devóvit proximórum zetérnze — salúti procurándae, totúsque fuit in sacris eórum confessiónibus excipiéndis atque ministério verbi Dei. Quo sane in múnere ex co témpore diligéntius et fervéntius ccepit laboráre, quo a sancto Vincéntio Ferrério, quem Bonónize tunc degéntem convénerat, cértior efféctus fuit stúdium hoc suum Dómino veheménter esse probátum.

Laud autem véritus ne, dum áliis preedicáret, réprobus ipse efficerétur, nunquam déstitit corpus suum castigáre atque redigere in servitútem. Zona quinque círculis férreis compácta ita lumbos constrínxit, ut nec post ejus óbitum, nisi exsiccáto cadáverc, evélli inde potúerit. Huic severióri córporis castigatióni jejúnia áédidit, vigílias aliásque carnis maceratiónes. Ádeo in eo vigébat pro Jesu Christi amóre patiéndi ardor, ut se minus illi accéptum esse ingemíscere, si vel zegritúdine ásiqua vel :erúmuis áliis frequéntius non tentarétur. Réliquae item, Qua hóminem perfectiónem sectáp. tem decent, virtútes in ill singulári prorsus modo enituérunt, ac præ céteris cultus assíduus reguláris disciplínæ. Quo factum est ut sǽpius No. vitiórum institutióni praepósitus, illos ad omnem sauctimóniam informáverit, aliísque auctor fúerit ut monástice vitz institátum suscíperent : quos inter mérito recensétur beátus Joánnes Liíccius, qui, Petro suadénte, Ordini nomen dedit.

N conóbiis, quorum prudéntia summa nec minóri zelo przefectúram gessit, Régule observántiam relígio sámque vivéndi normam, sícubi collápsam invénit, restitúere, ubi vero floréntem, tuéri et amplificáre, non tam dictis quam benefáctis, sédulo curávit. Illíus sanctitátis et doctrína& fama Eugénius Quartus permótus, concílio cecuménico a se Floréntize indícto, eum, ut interésset, vocávit. In hoc vero concílio ita se gessit, ut deínde in clerum Trinácriz univérsum commíssum ei fúerit ab eódem Summo Pontífice árduum reformatiónis opus, quod tamen pro ánimi sul modéstia nonnísi in Reguláres viros perficiéndum suscépit : et ut erat mitíssimus, benígne cum ómnibus agens felíciter absólvit. Post heec in coenóbium Panormitánum sanct Zi se recépit, ubi tandem méritis et labóribus plenus sanctíssime | excéssit. Signis, iisque przecláris, a Deo fuísse illusrátum — vétera produnt monuménta. Ejus cultum Pius Sextus Póntifex Máximus probávit, ac toti Fratrum Przedicatórum Ordini de beáto Petro Jeremía recitándi Officium, Missámque celebrándi fecit potestátem.

Innocéntius Sextus : Hujus Doctóris, inquit, doctrína pre céteris, excépta canónica, habet proprietátem verbórum, modum dicendórum, veritátem sententiárum : ita ut nunquam qui eam tenúerit, mveniátur a. veritátis trámite deviásse, et qui eam impugnáverit, semper fúerit de veritáte Suspéctus. Urbánus Quintus ad Tolosánam Académiam : Vólumus, ait, et tenóre przeséntium vobis injingimus ut beáti Thome doctrínam tamquam verídicam et cathólicam sectémini : eámque studeátis totis víribus ampliáre.

Quod et ántia, et líquido nuper in sacris Tridentini concílii decrétis appáruit. Clemens Octávus ad Neapolitános : Pie, ait, prudentérque cogitátis de novo Civitáti Patróno adsciscéndo, cive vestro, divínce voluntátis Angélico intérprete, vitæ sanctitáte et miráculis claro, Thoma Aquináte. Hic síquidem honor ejus virtútibus, cum admirábili doctrína conjúnctis, jure óprimo debétur. Ac doctrínæ quidem testis est ingens librórum númerus, quos ille brevíssimo témpore in omni fere disciplinárum génere, singulári órdine ac mira perspicuitáte sine ullo prorsus erróre conscrípsit.

Et Leo Décimus tértius, omnes suórum Przecessórum laudes una compléctens et preetergrédiens, de ipso hæc habet : Ratiónem, ut par est, a fide appríme distínguens, utrámque tamen amíce consócians, utriúsque tum jura conservávit, tum dignitáti consú luit, ita quidem ut rátio, ad humánum fastígium Thomæ pennis evécta,jam fere néqueat sublimius assúrgere; neque fides a ratióne fere possit plura aut validióra adjuménta przestolári quam quz jam est per Thomam consecúta. Et íterum sanctum Thomam in váriis scientiárum stúdiis tamquam exémplar cathólicis homínibus propónens atque Patrónum, ait : Preeclára lúmina ánimi et ingénii, quibus ad imitatiónem sui jure vocet álios, in eo sunt ómnia : doctrína ubérrima, incorrúpta, apte dispósita : obséquium fídei, et cum veritátibus divínitus tráditis mira consénSio : intégritas vitze cum splendóre- virtútum maximárum.

lessons.la: ATRITIUS Hibernórum A póstolus, sanctitáte insígnis, doctrína exímius, signis mirábilis fuit, natióne Trito, génere nóbilis, sancti Martini ex soróre nepos. Ab ineúnte ztáte lítteris incúbuit, adolcscénsque adhuc, a pirátis in Hibérniam abdúctus et vénditus, ibi servíre coáctus est. Exácto, summa cum patiéntia, ea in captivitáte sexénnio; repérto, cæli múnere,thesáuro, in prístinam se libertátem vindicávit, ad suósque revérsus, primum sancto Martíno avúnculo suo, a quo Cléricus factus est, demum sancto Germáno Autissiodorénsi Epíscopo sacris lítteris instituéndum se præbuit.

B his magístris a mundi illécebris ad rerum divinárum meditatiónem — cælestísque sapiéntiae stúdium plane translátus est. Divína interim visióne admónitus, Hibernórum conversiónem, quorum cecitátem et misériam Júgibus lácrimis deplorábat, ardentíssimo zelo cœpit deperire : Romámque proféctus, Cielestíno Primo Summo Pontífici pro eórum salúte per Evangélii praedicatiónem procuránda supplex factus, ipse ad apostólicum hoc munus a Ceelestíno delegátur, primus Hibérnice Epíscopus consecrátus.

TEC mora, in Hibérniam enávigans, divíno óperi, tanto fervóre tantáque grátia incúbuit, ut primum ipsos feeoe rócis gentis reges, ipsámque mox gentem, príncipum suórum exémpla certátim secútam, ad fidem convérterit, excussáque dǽmonis, miris ártibus et preestígiis illudéntis, tyránnide, divína virtúte poténtior Patrítius, Christi jugo verbis, exémplis, miráculis subjécerit : adeóque felíciter, ut quæ tot sceculis dæmonum sedes fúerat Hibérnia, Sanctórum póstmodum ínsula dicerétur. Tandem, postquam sexagínta annos per multos labóres múltaque prodígia Ecclésiam hanc sapiénter rexísset et in fide confirmásset, plenus annis et méritis plácida morte quiévit, anno Salútis quadringentésimo nonagésimo primo.

* IEYLLINA de Biscóssis, Papiíze ex honéstis piísque paréntibus orta, a puerítia religiónis opéribus ádeo inténta visa est, ut preces, quas quotiídie recitáre solébat, nunquam praetermíserit. Duodénnis visu orbáta, dídicit ex hac ipsa divína permissióne studiósius virtútum ómnium exercítio incúmbere. Nam a quibúsdam Soróribus Tértii Ordinis sancti Domínici excépta, atque eárum hábitum ac régulam amplexáta, ab iísdem sédula cura instrúcta fuit quómodo se in oratióne habéret, ac in cádem perseveráret; média quoque ab iídem accépit mentis ac consciéntize. puritátem servándi. Deínde, austerióris vitze cuúpida, ad abscónditum recéssum confúgit, in quo réliquo vitze témpore commoráta est.

Ac in solitúdine, véluti colúmba in cavérna macérize, l'assiónem contémplans Jesu Christi, dum illi máxime compaterétur, ejus ánima suavíssima devotióne et afféctu perfundebátur. Patiénti Sponso suo confórmis fíeri studens, peniténtize rigóribus se afflíxit : étenim duríssimo pane pro cibo utebátur : quotídie tam áspere se flagellábat, ut sanguis ad terram usque difflúeret : lácrimze illi panes erant die ac nocte, ac membra, | vigíliis, oratiónibus ac prostratiónibus defatigáta, Super lígneum tábulam brevíssimo somno recreábat. Ne tempus inániter absúmeret, cum | ui ei contíngeret, ejus sermónes circa ceeléstia júgiter vers. bántur : ex quo fiébat ut iii qui eam adíbant, spirituáliter recreáti ac melióres effécti Teverteréntur.

* Lt plane illitteráta esset beáta Sibyllína, in divínis tamen mire edócta appáruit, et de mýsticis rebus tanta facilitáte tantáque verbórum proprietáte loquebátur, ut in divi Augustíni Solilóquiis ac sancti Bernárdi Meditatiónibus mire versáta viderétur, De proximórum spiritáli salúte sollícita, nonnúllos, qui perditiónis viam mísere currébant, ad se accersítos, alíquibus Dei misericórdiam, áliis ejus justítiam ob óculos ponéndo, a vítiis excitávit, et ad pceniténtiam addúxit. Tandem, plena diérum et bonórum óperum, octogenária, ómnibus Ecclésige Sacraméntis refécta, ad czelos evolávit, décimo quarto Kaléndas Aprílis, Féria sexta, |- anno millésimo tercentésimo sexagósimo séptimo. Ejus córpore ad ecclésiam Fratrum Praedicatórum deláto, magna ad illud facta fuit concurréntium populórum frequéntia, Christo ccelésti ejus Sponso sanctitátem ipsíus signis manifestánte; unde públici eccleSiástici cultus ei tríbui ceepérunt honóres, in quibus, ad hzec usque témpora, Papíze et Álibi fidéles persevérant. Quibus rite probátis, Pius Nonus Póntifex Máximus, ex sacre Rítuum Congregatiónis. consúlto, cultum confirmávit, indulsitque ut in univérso Przedicatórum Ordine festum beátz Sibyllínae cum Offício et Missa celebrarétur. lessons.la: oskPH ínitur Ductus est in Ægýptum, emítque eum Putíphar eunúchus Pharaónis, princeps exércitus, vir Ægýptius, de manu Ismaëlitárum, a quibus perdúctus erat. Fuítque Dóminus cum eo, et erat vir in cunctis próspere agens: habitavítque in domo dómini sui, qui óptime nóverat Dóminum esse cum eo, ct ómnia, que géreret, ab eo dírigi in manu illíus. Invenítque Joseph grátiam coram dómino suo, et ministrábat ei: a quo præpósitus ómnibus gubernábat créditam sibi domum, et univérsa quæ ei trádita fúerant: benedixítque Dóminus dómui Ægýptii propter Joseph,
lessons.en: And Joseph was brought into Egypt, and Putiphar an eunuch of Pharao, chief captain of the army, an Egyptian, bought him of the Ismaelites, by whom he was brought. And the Lord was with him, and he was a prosperous man in all things: and he dwelt in his master’s house, Who knew very well that the Lord was with him, and made all that he did to prosper in his hand. And Joseph found favour in the sight of his master, and ministered to him: and being set over all by him, he governed the house committed to him, and all things that were delivered to him: And the Lord blessed the house of the Egyptian for Joseph’s sake, and multiplied all his substance, both at home, and in the fields.

resp.a: Fuit Dóminus cum Joseph, et dedit ei grátiam in conspéctu príncipis cárceris: Qui trádidit in manu illíus univérsos vinctos
v: Quidquid fiébat, sub ipso erat: Dóminus enim erat cum illo, et ómnia ópera ejus dirigébat.

head: Cap. 41.
lessons.la: Plácuit Pharaóni consílium Joseph, et cunctis minístris ejus: locutúsque est ad eos: Num inveníre potérimus talem virum, qui spíritu Dei plenus sit? Dixit ergo ad Joseph: Quia osténdit tibi Deus ómnia quæ locútus es, numquid sapientiórem et consímilem tui inveníre pótero? Tu eris super domum meam, et ad tui oris impérium cunctus pópulus obédiet: uno tantum regni sólio te præcédam.
lessons.en: The counsel pleased Pharao and all his servants. And he said to them: Can we find such another man, that is full of the spirit of God? He said therefore to Joseph: Seeing God hath shewn thee all that thou hast said, can I find one wiser and one like unto thee? Thou shalt be over my house, and at the commandment of thy mouth all the people shall obey: only in the kingly throne will I be above thee.

resp.a: Esuriénte terra Ægýpti, clamávit pópulus ad regem, aliménta petens. Quibus ille respóndit:
resp.b: Ite ad Joseph, et quidquid vobis díxerit, fácite.
v: Crescébat quotídie fames in omni terra, aperuítque Joseph univérsa hórrea, et vendébat Ægýptiis.

lessons.la: Dixítque rursus Phárao ad Joseph: Ecce, constítui te super univérsam terram Ægýpti. Tulítque ánulum de manu sua, et dedit eum in manu cjus: vestivítque eum stola býssina, et collo torquem áuream circumpósuit. Fecítque eum ascéndere super currum suum secúndum, clamánte præcóne, ut omnes coram eo genu flécterent, et præpósitum esse scirent univérsæ terræ Ægýpti. Dixit quoque rex ad Joseph: Ego sum Phárao: absque tuo império non movébit quisquam manum aut pedem in omni terra Ægýpti. HN.
lessons.en: And again Pharao said to Joseph: Behold, I have appointed thee over the whole land of Egypt. And he took his ring from his own hand, and gave it into his hand: and he put upon him a robe of silk, and put a chain of gold about his neck. And he made him go up into his second chariot, the crier proclaiming that all should bow their knee before him, and that they should know he was made governor over the whole land of Egypt. And the king said to Joseph: I am Pharao; without thy commandment no man shall move hand or foot in all the land of Egypt.

resp.a: Fecit me Dóminus quasi patrem regis, etdóminum univérsæ domus ejus: nolíte pavére;
resp.b: Pro salúte enim vestra misit me Deus ante vos in Ægýptum.
v: Veníte ad me, et ego dabo vobis ómnia bona Ægýpti, et comedétis medúllam terræ.

lessons.la: UiS et qualis homo fúerit beátus Joseph, cónice ex appellatióne, qua, licet dispensatória, méruit honorári ádeo, ut pater Dei ct dictus et créditus sit; cónice et ex próprio vocábulo, quod augméntum non dúbites interpretári. Simul et meménto magni illíus quondam Patriárchæ vénditi in Ægýpto; et scito ipsíus istum non solum vocábulum fuísse sortítum, sed et casti. móniam adéptum, innocéntiam assecútum et grátiam.
lessons.en: From the Sermons of St. Bernard, Abbot of Clairvaux. What and what manner of man the blessed Joseph was, we may gather from that title wherewith, albeit only as a deputy, God deemed him fit to be honoured he was both called, and supposed to be the Father of God. We may gather it from his very name, which, being interpreted, signifieth Increase. Remember likewise that great Patriarch who was sold into Egypt, and know that the Husband of Mary not only received his name, but inherited his purity, and was likened to him in innocence and in grace.

resp.a: Ascéndit Joseph a Gálea de civitáte Názareth in Judǽam, in civitátem David, quæ vocátur Béthlehem:
resp.b: fc quod esset de domo et família David.
v: Ut profiterétur cum María desponsáta sibi uxóre.

lessons.la: S! quidem ille Joseph, fratérna ex invídia vénditus et ductus in Ægýptum, Christi venditiónem præfigurávit: iste Joseph, Herodiánam invídiam fúgiens, Christum i Ægýptum portávit. Ille dómino suo fidem servans, dóminæ nóluit commiscéri: iste Dóminam suam, Dómini sui matrem, vírginem agnóscens et ipse cóntinens, fidéliter custodívit. Illi data est intellegéntia in mystériis somniórum: isti datum est cónscium fíeri atque partícipem cæléstium sacramentórum.
lessons.en: If then, that Joseph that was sold by his brethren through envy, and was brought down to Egypt, was a type of Christ sold by a disciple, and handed over to the Gentiles, the other Joseph flying from the envy of Herod carried Christ into Egypt. That first Joseph kept loyal to his master, and would not carnally know his master's wife; that second Joseph knew that the Lady, the Mother of his Lord, was a virgin, and he himself remained faithfully virgin toward her. To that first Joseph it was given to know dark things in interpreting of dreams; to the second Joseph it was given in sleep to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven.

resp.a: Surge, et áccipe Púerum et Matrem ejus, et fugein Ægýptum;
resp.b: Et esto ibi, usque dum dicam tibi.
v: Ut adim plerétur quod dictum est a Dómino per prophétam dicéntem: Ex Ægýpto vocávi Fílium meum.

lessons.la: t fruménta servávit non sibi, sed omni pópulo: iste Panem vivum e cælo servándum accépit tam sibi quam toti mundo. Non est dúbium, uim bonus et fidélis homo fúerit iste Joseph, cui Mater desponsáta est Salvatóris. Fidélis, inquam, servus, et prudens, quem constítuit Dóminus suæ Matris solátium, suæ carnis nutrítium, solum dénique in terris magni consílii coadjutórem fidelíssimum.
lessons.en: The first Joseph laid by bread, not for himself, but for all people; the second Joseph received into his keeping that Living Bread Which came down from heaven, not for him only, but for the whole world. We cannot doubt but that that Joseph was good and faithful to whom was espoused the Mother of the Saviour. Yea, I say, he was a faithful and wise servant, whom the Lord appointed to be the comfort of His own Mother, the keeper of His own Body, and the only and trusty helper in the Eternal Counsels.

resp.a: Cum indúcerent púerum Jesum paréntes ejus, ut fácerent secúndum consuetúdinem legis pro o,
resp.b: Accépit eum Símeon in ulnas suas, et benedíxit Deum.
v: Et erant Pater ejus et Mater mirántes super his, quæ dicebántur de illo.

head: Cap. l.
lessons.homily_head: Homilía sancti Hierónymi Presbýteri. (Lib. 1.Comm. incap. r. Matth.)
lessons.gospel: esset desponsáta Mater Jesu María Joseph, ántequam convenírent, invénta est habens de Spíritu Sancto. Et réliqua.
lessons.la: UARE non de símplici vírgine, sed de desponsáta concípitur? Primum, ut per generatiónem Joseph, orígo Maríæ monstrarétur: secúndo, ne lapidarétur a Judcis ut adúltera: tértio, ut in Ægýptum fúgiens habéret solátium. Martyr Ignátius étiam quartam áddidit causam, cur a desponsáta concéptus sit: Ut partus, ínquiens, ejus celarétur diábolo, dum eum putat non de vírgine, sed de uxóre generátum. RK. vii Dicit Mater Jesu ad illum Fili quid fecísti nobis sic? * Ecce Pater tuus et ego doléntes quærebámus te, et ait ad illos Quid est, quod me querebátis? nesciebátis quia in his, quæ Patris mei sunt, opórtet me esse? — Ecce Pater tuus et ego.

NTEQUAM convenírent, inE vénta est in útero habens de Spíritu Sancto. Non ab álio invénta est, nisi a Joseph, qui pene licéntia maritáli futúræ uxóris ómnia nóverat. Quod autem dícitur, Antequam convenírent, non séquitur ut póstea convénerint: sed Scriptúra quod factum non sit, osténdit.
lessons.en: Before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost. She was found, that is, by Joseph, but by no one else. He had already almost an husband's privilege to know all that concerned her. Before they came together. This doth not imply that they ever did come together the Scripture merely showeth the absolute fact that up to this time they had not done so.

resp.a: Descéndit Jesus cum eis, et venit Názareth:
resp.b: Et erat súbditus illis.
v: Proficiébat sapiéntia, et ætáte, et grátia apud Deum et hómines.

lessons.la: OSEPH autem vir ejus, cum Is justus, et nollet eam tradúcere, vóluit occúlte dimíttere eam. Si quis fornicáriæ conjúngitur, unum corpus effícitur, et in lege præcéptum est, non solum reos, sed et cónscios críminum obnóxios esse peccáti: quómodo ISrgh, cum crimen celáret uxóris, justus scríbitur? Sed hoc testimónium Maríæ est, quod Joseph sciens illíus castitátem, ct admírans quod evénerat, celat siléntio, cujus mystérium nesciébat.
lessons.en: Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a public example, was minded to put her away privily. If any man be joined to a fornicatress they become one body; and according to the law they that are privy to a crime are thereby guilty. How then can it be that Joseph is described as a just man, at the very time he was compounding the criminality of his espoused? It must have been that he knew her to be pure, and yet understood not the mystery of her pregnancy, but, while he wondered at that which had happened, was willing to hold his peace.

resp.a: Angelus Dómini appáruit Joseph, dicens: Joseph, fili David, noli timére accípere Maríam cónjugem tuam; quod enim in ea natum est, de Spíritu Sancto est
resp.b: páriet autem fílium, et vocábis nomen ejus Jesum.
v: Cum esset desponsáta Mater Jesu Maria Joseph, antequam convenírent, invénta est in útero habens de Spíritu Sancto

ant: X. t. Ibant paréntes Jesu per omnes annos in Jerúsalem in die solémni Paschæ.
Cum redírent, remánsit puer Jesus in Jerúsalem, et non cognovérunt paréntes cjus.
Non inveniéntes Jesum, regréssi sunt in Jerúsalem requiréntes eum; et post tríduum invenérunt illum in templo sedéntem in médio doctórum, audiéntem et interrogántem eos.
Dicit Mater ejus ad illum: Fili, quid fecísti nobis sic? Ecc. pater tuus, et ego doléntes quærebámus te.
Descéndit Jesus cum eis, et venit Názareth, et erat sip. ditus illis.

v2.magn: Ecce fidélis servus et prudens, quem constítuit Dóminus super famíliam suam. EMPORE Paschali, in festo S. Joseph fiat Officium ut pag. 985. notátum est.

lessons.la: Cap. UDITE fílii disciplínam patris, et atténdite ut sciátis prudéntiam. Donum bonumtri. buam vobis: legem meam ne derelinquátis. Nam et ego fílius fui patris mei, tenéllus et unigénitus coram matre mea. Et docébat me, atque dicébat: Suscípiat verba mea cor tuum: custódi præcépta mea, et vives.
lessons.en: Hear, ye children, the instruction of a father, and attend that you may know prudence. I will give you a good gift, forsake not my law. For I also was my father’s son, tender and as an only son in the sight of my mother: And he taught me, and said: Let thy heart receive my words, keep my commandments, and thou shalt live.

lessons.la: Pósside sapiéntiam, pósside prudéntiam: ne obliviscáris, neque declínes a verbis oris mei. Ne dimíttas eam, et custódiet te: dílige eam, et conservábit te. Princípium sapiéntiæ, pósside sapiéntiam, et in omni possessióne tua, acquíre prudéntiam: árripe illam, et exaltábit te: glorificáberis ab ea, cum eam fúeris amplexátus: dabit cápiti tuc augménta gratiárum, ct Co róna ínclyta próteget te.
lessons.en: Get wisdom, get prudence: forget not, neither decline from the words of my mouth. Forsake her not, and she shall keep thee: love her, and she shall preserve thee. The beginning of wisdom, get wisdom, and with all thy possession purchase prudence. Take hold on her, and she shall exalt thee: thou shalt be glorified by her, when thou shalt embrace her. She shall give to thy head increase of graces, and protect thee with a noble crown.

lessons.la: UDI fili mi, et súscipe verba mea, ut multiplicéntur tibi anni vite. Viam sapiéntiæ monstrábo tibi: ducam te Xf sémitas æquitátis: quas cum ingréssus fúeris, non arctabúntur gressus tui, et currens non habébis offendículum. Tene disciplínam, ne dimíttas ean: custódi illam, quia ipsa vita tua. Do m Xxii. Mártii. B. Ambrósii Sansedonii.

ENEDICTUS Núrsiæ nóbili B énére ortus, Romæ liítteris erudítus, ut totum se Jesu Christo daret, in altíssimam spelúncam penetrávit; in qua per triénnium ita delítuit, ut unus id sciret Románus mónachus, quo ad vitæ necessitátem minístro utebátur. Concupiscéntiæ motus, sibi a dæmone excitátos, in spinis volutátrs exstínxit. sanctitátis, ejus fama permóti mónachi quidam se illi instituéndos tradidére; qui ob vivéndi licéntiam ab ipso dúrius objurgáti, mortem ei venéno inférre studuérunt at crucis signo vas oblátum confrégit, et in solitúdinem secéssit.

Um multi ad eum quotídie discípuli convenírent, duódecim monastéria ædificávit, éaque sanctíssimis légibus communívit. Cassínum deínde migrans, Apóllinis, simulácrum commínuit, aram evértit lucos succéndit; prophético spíritu darus ventúra prædíxit: Quod ubi accépit Tótila Gothórum Téx, exploratúrus, an ita res esset, spathárium suum régio ornátu et comitátu præmísit, qui se regem simuláret. Quem ut ille vidit, Depóne, inquit, fili, quod geris; nam tuum non tst. Sed et Tótila ad eum acCédens se humi prostrávit cui ob scélera increpáto. advénum in Urbem, maris transmissiónem, et post novénnium Portem prædíxit.

* Eminéntem mortis suæ diem przedíxit Benedíctus : sepúlcrum, in quo condi vellet, sex diébus ántequam eo inferrétur, aperíri jussit : sextóque die in ecclésiam deférri vóluit ; ubi sumpta Eucharístia, sublátis in cælum óculis orans, inter manus discipulórum ánimam Deo réddidit. Hujus czeléstis glória duóbus mónachis in czelésti visióne osténsa est. Disciplínam monásticam in Occidénte pene collápsam restítuit, ac przecláris institútis religiónem mirífice propagávit : ex qua innúmera diversórum Órdinum áómina prodiére, quibus Ecclésia cathólica plúrimum illustráta fuit.

lessons.la: Cap. l. APIENTIAM ómnium antiquórum exquíret sápiens, et in prophétis vacábit. Narratiónem virórum nominatórum conservábit, et in versútias parabolárum simul introíbit. Occúlta proverbiórum exquíret, et in abscónditis parabolárum conversábitur. In médio magnatórum ministrábit, et in conspéctu prǽsidis apparébit. In terram alienigenárum géntium pertránsiet: bona enim et mala in homínibus tentábit.
lessons.en: The wise men will seek out the wisdom of all the ancients, and will be occupied in the prophets. He will keep the sayings of renowned men, and will enter withal into the subtilties of parables. He will search out the hidden meanings of proverbs, and will be conversant in the secrets of parables. He shall serve among great men, and: appear before the governor. He shall pass into strange countries: for he shall try good and evil among men.

lessons.la: R suum tradet ad vigilándum dilúculo ad Dóminum, qui fecit illum, et in conspéctu Altíssimi deprecábitur. Apériet os suum in oratióne, et pro delíctis suis deprecábitur. Si enim Dóminus magnus volúerit, spíritu intelligéntiæ replébit illum: et ipse tamquam imbres mittet elóquia sapiéntiæ suæ, et in oratióne confitébitur Dómino: et ipse díriget consílium ejus, et disciplínam, et in abscónditis suis consiliábitur.
lessons.en: He will give his heart to resort early to the Lord that made him, and he will pray in the sight of the most High. He will open his mouth in prayer, and will make supplication for his sins. For if it shall please the great Lord, he will fill him with the spirit of understanding: And he will pour forth the words of his wisdom as showers, and in his prayer he will confess to the Lord. And he shall direct his counsel, and his knowledge, and in his secrets shall he meditate.

lessons.la: PSE palam fáciet disciplínam doctríngs sue, et in lege testaménti Dómini gloriábitur. Collaudábunt multi sapiéntiam ejus, et usque in sǽculum non delébitur. Non recédet memória ejus, et nomen ejus requirétur a generatióne in generatiónem. Sapiéntiam ejus enarrábunt gentes, et laudem ejus enuntiábit ecclésia. Si permánserit, nomen derelínquet plus quam mille: etsi requiéverit, próderit illi.
lessons.en: He shall shew forth the discipline he hath learned, and shall glory in the law of the covenant of the Lord. Many shall praise his wisdom, and it shall never be forgotten. The memory of him shall not depart away, and his name shall be in request from generation to generation. Nations shall declare his wisdom, and the church shall shew forth his praise. If he continue, he shall leave a name above a thousand: and if he rest, it shall be to his advantage.

lessons.la: * MRBROSIUS Sansedónius Se- .X nis in Etrúria nobílibus Piísque paréntibus natus est. Adoléscens Przedicatórum Or. dinem ampléxus, atque ad stúdium — Parisiénse miss, dæmonem, sub eremítze Spécie ipsum a religióso stúdio de. hortántem, detéctis insígni superávit. Albérto Magno do. ctóre et sancto Thoma Aquináte condiscípulo, ita in lítteris profécit, ut eum, post theologíam in Académiis Parisitns et Coloniénsi summo appláus tráditam, Summus Póntifey Romam adscíverit, ad collápsa ibi sacræ doctrínæ stúdia re. stituénda. Pro gravíssimis Ecclésiae cathólicee negótiis a Summis Pontifícibus ad suprémos Fidéles Príncipes deléta. tus, ea felicissime gessit.

OHEMICAM sectam in váriis Germániz pártibus gras sántem profligávit. Romam factiónibus discissam pacávit, Summíque Pontíficis electiónem in plenam libertátem vindicávit. Európze Príncipes ad bellum advérsus Turcas pro Terra sancta recupera tióne, ínito inter se fcedere concitávit. In sacris concióni ; bus, majórum páriter ac popu ' lárium vítia, summa libertáte redarguébat, et ad pcenitén tiam fidéles efficáciter inflammábat. Concionántem illum sepius in áera sublátum, e colúmbam ejus auri assistén tem pópuli conspexére.

* JARPESSSSINA: in Deum at , próximum caritáti sum mam humilitátem conjúnxi doctorátus láurea ac Senéms, Ecclésize przesulátu recusátis Missæ sacrifícium tanto ánlm , sensu celebrábat, ut ómnibus ártubus ossibúsque concuterétur, et ubérrimis profúsis lácrimis, in éxtasim raperétur. Inoratióne assíduus, in virginitátis custódia vigil, in córporis castigatióne — sevérus, Dóminum proméruit. Conciónem Senis habens, in feneraitóres tanto zelo commótus est, ut fracta semel et. íterum péctoris vena, morti viam patefécerit : quam leetus suscétis Sacraméntis aspéxit, anno millésimo ducentésimo octuagésimo sexto. Apostólicum Virum Clemens Octávus Martyrológio Románo adscrípsit, Gregórius vero Quintus décimus festum ejus in univérso Predicatórum Ordine celebrándum constítuit.

v1.magn: Pro eo quod non credidísti verbis meis, inquit Angelus Gábriel, eris tacens, et non póteris loqui usque in diem nativitátis ejus.

mat.invit: Adorémus Regem Archangelórum: * Qui privilégio Annuntiatiónis Gabriélem illustrávit Archángelum.

head: Cap. a.
lessons.la: Actum est autem cum vidérem ego Dániel visiónem, * t quǽrerem intelligéntiam: Cce stetit in conspéctu meo Uem quasi spécies viri. Et audívi — vocem viri inter Ulai, et clamávit, et ait: Gábriel fac me intellígere istam visiónem. Et venit, et stetit juxta ubi ego stabam: cumque venísset, pavens córrui in fáciem meam, et ait ad me: Intéllige fili hóminis, quóniam in témpore finis complébitur vísio. Cumque loquerétur ad me, collápsus sum pronus in terram: et tétigit me, et státuit me in gradu meo, dixítque mihi: Ego osténdam tibi quæ futúra sunt in novíssimo maledictiónis: quóniam habet tempus finem suum.
lessons.en: And it came to pass when I Daniel saw the vision, and sought the meaning, that behold there stood before me as it were the appearance of a man. And I heard the voice of a man between Ulai: and he called, and said: Gabriel, make this man to understand the vision. And he came and stood near where I stood: and when he was come, I fell on my face trembling, and he said to me: Understand, O son of man, for in the time of the end the vision shall be fulfilled. And when he spoke to me I fell flat on the ground: and he touched me, and set me upright, And he said to me: I will shew thee what things are to come to pass in the end of the malediction: for the time hath its end.

resp.a: Sacram praséntis diéi solemnitátem álacri celebrémus devotióne: quóniam insígnis Archángelus Gábriel Christum annúntians
resp.b: Singuláre glóriæ præsídium cælo et univérso orbi áttulit.
v: Perácta prophética legatióne, cum venerándo triúmpho Angelórum cœtibus comitátur.

lessons.la: RIES, quem vidísti habére córnua, rex Medórum est atque Persárum. Porro hircus caprárum, rex Græcórum est, et cornu grande, quod erat inter óculos ejus, ipse est rex primus. Quod autem fracto illo surrexérunt quátuor pro eo: quátuor reges de gente ejus consúrgent, sed non in fortitúdine ejus. Et post renum eórum, cum créverint iniquitátes, consúrget rex ímpudens fácie, et intélligens propositiónes. Et roborábitur fortitúdo ejus, sed non in víribus suis: et supra quam credi potest, univérsa vastábit, et prosperábitur, et fáciet. Et interfíciet robústos, et pópulum sanctórum secúndum voluntátem suam, et dirigétur dolusin manu ejus: et cor suum magnificábit, et in cópia rerum ómnium occídet plúrimos: et contra príncipem príncipum consúrget, ct sine manu conterétur. Et vísio véspere et mane, quæ dicta est, vera est: tu ergo visiónem signa, quia post multos dies erit. Et ego Dániel lángui, et ægrotávi per dies: cumque surrexíssem, faciébam ópera regis, et stupébam ad visiónem, et non erat qui interpretarétur.
lessons.en: The ram, which thou sawest with horns, is the king of the Medes and Persians. And the he goat, is the king of the Greeks, and the great horn that was between his eyes, the same is the first king. But whereas when that was broken, there arose up four for it: four kings shall rise up of his nation, but not with his strength. And after their reign, when iniquities shall be grown up, there shall arise a king of a shameless face, and understanding dark sentences. And his power shall be strengthened, but not by his own force: and he shall lay all things waste, and shall prosper, and do more than can be believed. And he shall destroy the mighty, and the people of the saints, According to his will, and craft shall be successful in his hand: and his heart shall be puffed up, and in the abundance of all things he shall kill many: and he shall rise up against the prince of princes, and shall be broken without hand. And the vision of the evening and the morning, which was told, is true: thou therefore seal up the vision, because it shall come to pass after many days. And I Daniel languished, and was sick for some days: and when I was risen up, I did the king’s business, and I was astonished at the vision, and there was none that could interpret it.

resp.a: Iste est Gábriel, qui supra céteros cælórum Spíritus a Dómino est eléctus
resp.b: Beátus Archángelus, cui crédita sunt secréta cæléstia.
v: Iste est Gábriel, quem Pater c:zeléstis Fílio ánico únicum minístrum destinávit.

head: Cap. 9.
lessons.la: MQUE adhuc lóquerer, et orárem, et confitérer peccáta pópuli mei Israël, et prostérnerem preces meas in conspéctu Dei mei, pro monte sancto Dei mei: adhuc me loquénte in oratióne, ecce vir Gábriel, quem víderam in visióne a princípio, cito volans tétigit me in témpore sacrifícii vespertíni. Et dócuit me, ct locútus est mihi, dixítque: Dániel nunc egréssus sum ut docérem te, et intellígeres. Ab exórdio precum tuárum egréssus est sermo: ego autem veni ut indicárem tibi, quia vir desideriórum es: tu ergo animadvérte sermónem, et intéllige visiónem. Septuagínta hebdómades abbreviáta: sunt super pópulum tuum, et super urbem sanctam tuam, ut cy. summétur prævaricátio, e finem accípiat peccátum, e deleátur iníquitas, et addúcitur justítia sempitérna, et impleátur vísio et prophetía, et ungátur Sanctus sanctórum. Scito ergo, et animadvérte: Ab éxitu sermónis, ut íterum ædificétur Jerúsalem, usque ad Christum ducem, hebdómades septem, et hebdómades sexagínta duæ erunt: et Moris d ædificábitur platéa, et muri in angústia témporum. Et pos hebdómades sexagínta duas occidétur Christus: et non erit ejus pópulus, qui eum negatúrus est.
lessons.en: Now while I was yet speaking, and praying, and confessing my sins, and the sins of my people of Israel, and presenting my supplications in the sight of my God, for the holy mountain of my God: As I was yet speaking in prayer, behold the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, flying swiftly touched me at the time of the evening sacrifice. And he instructed me, and spoke to me, and said: O Daniel, I am now come forth to teach thee, and that thou mightest understand. From the beginning of thy prayers the word came forth: and I am come to shew it to thee, because thou art a man of desires: therefore do thou mark the word, and understand the vision. Seventy weeks are shortened upon thy people, and upon thy holy city, that transgression may be finished, and sin may have an end, and iniquity may be abolished; and everlasting justice may be brought; and vision and prophecy may be fulfilled; and the saint of saints may be anointed. Know thou therefore, and take notice: that from the going forth of the word, to build up Jerusalem again, unto Christ the prince, there shall be seven weeks, and sixty-two weeks: and the street shall be built again, and the walls in straitness of times. And after sixty-two weeks Christ shall be slain: and the people that shall deny him shall not be his. And a people with their leader that shall come, shall destroy the city and the sanctuary: and the end thereof shall be waste, and after the end of the war the appointed desolation.

resp.a: Quómodo fiet istud, respóndens ait María, quia virum non cognósco? Angelus Gábricl ad hac
resp.b: Spíritus Sanctus supervéniet in te, et virtus Altíssimi obumbrábit tibi.
v: Ideóque quod nascétur ex te Sanctum, vocábitur Fílius Dei

lessons.la: No ángelum Gabriélem de minóribus ess; qui quálibet ex causa crebra sóleant ad terras fungi legatióne. Quod ex ejus nómine palam intélligi datur, quod in. terpretátum— Fortitúdo Dii dícitur; et quia non ab álio áliquo forte excellentióre se ut ássolet spíritu, sed ab ipso Deo mitti perhibétur. Propter hoc ergo pósitum est, A Dco, Vel ídeo dictum est, A Deo, ne cui, vel beatórum spirítuum suum Deus, ántequam Vírgini, revelásse putétur consílium, excépto dumtáxat Archángelo Gabriéle; qui útique tantæ inter suos inveníri potúerit excelléntiæ, ut tali et nómine dignus haberétur et núntio. Nec discórdat nomen a núntio.

resp.a: Descéndit Angelus Gábriel ad Zacharíam, dicens: Áccipe púerum in senectúte tua
resp.b: Et habébit nomen Joán nes Baptísta.
v: Ne tímeas Zacharía, quóniam exaudíta est orátio tuæ et Elísabeth uxor tua páriet tibi fílium.

lessons.la: ll Er quippe virtútem Chri stum, quem mélius nun tiáre decébat quam hunc, quem símile nomen honórat? Nam quid est áliud fortitúdo, quam virtus? Non autem dedécens aut incóngruum videátur, Dóminum et núntium common censéri vocábulo; cum símilis in utróque appellatiónis, no? sit tamen utriúsque Sím! ls La wg Die Xxiv. Mártii. S. Gabriélis, Témpore Quadrag. causa. Aliter quippe Christus fortitúdo vel virtus Dei dícitur, áliter Angelus; Angelus enim tantum — nuncupatíve, Christus autem étiam substantíve. Christus Dei virtus et dícitur ct est, quæ forti armáto, qui suum átrium in pace custodíre solébat, fórtior supervéniens, ipsum suo bráchio debellávit: et sic ei vasa captivitátis poténter erípuit. Angelus vero fortitúdo Dei appellátus est, vel quod hujúsmodi merúerit, prærogatívam offícii, quo ejúsdem nuntiáret advéntum virtútis: vel quia vírginem natúra pávidam, símplicem, verecúndam, de miráculi novitáte ne expavésceret, confortáre debéret; quod et fecit, Ne tímeas, ínquiens, María, invenísti grátiam apud Deum.

resp.a: Gábriel Archángelus appáruit Zacharíæ dicens: Nascétur tibi fílius, nomen ejus Joánnes vocábitur:
resp.b: Et multi in nativitáte ejus gaudébunt.
v: Erit enim magnus coram Dómino, vinum et síceram non bibet.

lessons.la: gr et ipsíus Sponsum, hóminem útique nihilóminus húmilem ac timorátum, non irrationabíliter fórsitan idem Angelus confortásse créditur : quamquam tunc ab Evangélica non nominétur. Joseph, inquit, fili David, ne tímeas accípere Maríam cónjugem luam. Conveniénter ítaque Gábriel ad hoc opus elígitur : immo quia tale illi negótium Injúngitur, recte tali nómine designátur. Missus est ergo Gábriel Angelus a Deo. Quo ? In civitátem Galilzeze, cui nomen Názareth. Videámussi, ut ait Nathánael, a Názareth potest áliquit boni esse. Názareth interpretátur Flos. Vidéntur autem mihi quoddam semen fuísse divínze cognitiónis, tamquam e cælo jactátum in terras, allocutiónes et promissiónes factæ czelitus ad Patres, Abraham scílicet, Isaac et Jacob.

resp.a: Gaude María Virgo, cunctas hǽreses sola interemísti, quæ Gabriélis Archángeli dictis credidísti
resp.b: Dum Virgo Deum et hóminem genuísti: et post partum, Virgo, invioláta permansísti.
v: Gabriélem Archángelum scimus divínitus te esse affátum: úterum tuum de Spíritu sancto crédimus impraegnátum: erubéscat Judǽus infélix, qui dicit Christum ex Joseph sémine esse natum.

head: Cap. l.
lessons.homily_head: Homilía venerábilis Bedæ Presbýteri. (Expónit. in Luc. lib. t. cap. r.)
lessons.gospel: In illo témpore: Missus est Angelus Gabriel a Deo in civitatem Galilææ, cui nomen Nazareth, ad Virginem desponsatam viro, cui nomen erat Joseph, de domo David, et nomen Virginis Maria. Et réliqua.
lessons.la: XORDIUM . Redemptiónis nostra, fratres caríssimi, hodiérna nobis sancti Evangélii léctio comméndat; quæ Àngelum de cælis a Deo missum narrat ad Vírginem, ut novam in carne Nativitátem Fílii Dei praedicáret : per quam nos, abjécta vetustáte nóxia, renovári atque inter fílios Dei computári possímus.

resp.a: Missus est Gábriel Angelus ad Maríam Vírginem desponsátam Joseph, núntians ei verbum; et expavéscit Virgo de lúmine: ne tímeas, María, invenísti grátiam apud Dóminum: Ecce concípies, et páries,
resp.b: Et vocábitur Altíssimi Fílius.
v: Dabit ei Dóminus Deus sedem David, patris ejus, et regnábit in domo Jacob in ætérnum.

lessons.la: T ergo ad promíssze Salútis U mereámur dona pertíngere : primórdium ejus inténta curémus aure percípere. Missus est (inquit) Angelus Gábriel a Deo in civitátem Galilǽæ, cui nomen Názareth, ad Vírginem desponsátam viro, cui nomen erat Joseph. Aptum profécto humánze Restauratiónis princípium, ut Angelus a Deo mitterétur ad Vírginem, partu consecrándam divíno : quia prima perditiónis humánze fuit causa, cum serpens a diábolo mittebátur ad mulíerem, spíritu supérbiae decipiéndam : immo ipse in serpénte diábolus veniébat, qui genus humánum, decéptis primis paréntibus, immortalitátis gloria nudáret.

resp.a: Súscipe verbum, Vir o María, quod tibi a Dómino per Angelum Gabriélem transmíssum est: concípies et páries Deum páriter et hóminem,
resp.b: Ut benedícta dicáris inter omnes mulíeres.
v: Páries quidem fílium, et virginitátis non patiéris detriméntum: efficiéris grávida, et eris mater semper intácta.

lessons.la: DCIRCO Angeli privátis nomínibus censéntur: ut signétur per vocábula étiam in operatióne quid váleant. Neque étenim in illa sancta civitáte, quam de visióne omnipoténtis Dei plena sciéntia pérficit, idcírco própria nómina sortiúntur, ne eórum persónse sine nomínibus sciri non possint : sed cum ad nos áliquit ministratúri véniunt, apu étiam nómina a Es trahunt. Ad Maríam ergo Vir ginem Gábricl míttitur, qi Dei Fortitúdo nominátur. [lum quippe nuntiáre veniébat, Qui ad debellándas aéreas potest. tes húmilis apparére dignátus est. De quo per Psalmístam dícitur : Dóminus fortis, et potens in prǽlio. Et rursum: Dóminus Virtútum ipse est rex glóriae. Per Dei ergo Fortitúdinem nuntiándus erat, qui Vir. tútum Dóminus, et potens in prœlio contra potestátes aéreas ad bella veniébat.

resp.a: Ave, María, grátia plena, Dóminus tecum: inquit Angelus Gábriel
resp.b: Spíritus Sanctus supervéniet in te, It virtus Altíssimi obumbrábit tibi: quod enim ex te pascé! tur Sanctum, vocábitur Fílius Dei.
v: Quómodo fiet istud, quóniam virum non cognósco? Et respóndens Angelus, dixit ei.

laud.bened: Gábriel Archángele, qui ante Deum semper assístis, admítte preces nostras intra sacrárium exauditiónis, et repórta nobis antídotum divínæ reconciliatiónis.

head: Cap. 4.
lessons.la: A illi disciplínam patris, et atténdite ut sciátis prudéntiam. Donum bonum tríbuam vobis: legem meam ne derelinquátis. Nam et ego fílius fui patris mei, tenéllus et unigénitus coram matre mea. Et docébat me, atque dicébat: Suscípiat verba mea cor tuum: custódi præcépta mea, et vives.
lessons.en: Want is from the Lord in the house of the wicked: but the habitations of the just shall be blessed. Hear, ye children, the instruction of a father, and attend that you may know prudence. I will give you a good gift, forsake not my law. For I also was my father’s son, tender and as an only son in the sight of my mother: And he taught me, and said: Let thy heart receive my words, keep my commandments, and thou shalt live.

lessons.la: Dou Sapiéntiam, pósside prudéntiam: ne obliviscáris, neque declínes a verbis oris mei. Ne dimíttas eam, et custódiet te: dílige cam, et conservábit te. Princípium sapiéntiæ, pósside sapiéntiam, et in omni possessióne tua, ac quíre prudéntiam: árripe illam, et exaltábit te: glorificáberis ab ea, cum eam fúeris amplexátus: dabit cápiti tuo augménta gratiárum, et coróna ínclyta próteget te.
lessons.en: Get wisdom, get prudence: forget not, neither decline from the words of my mouth. Forsake her not, and she shall keep thee: love her, and she shall preserve thee. The beginning of wisdom, get wisdom, and with all thy possession purchase prudence. Take hold on her, and she shall exalt thee: thou shalt be glorified by her, when thou shalt embrace her. She shall give to thy head increase of graces, and protect thee with a noble crown.

lessons.la: vDI fili mi, et súscipe verba mea, ut multiplicéntur tibi anni vitæ. Viam sapiéntiæ monstrábo tibi: ducam te per sémitas æquitátis: quas cum ingréssus fúeris, non arctabúntur gressus tul, et currens non habébis offendículum. Tene disciplínam, ne dimíttas eam: custódi illam, quia ipsa est vita tua.
lessons.en: Hear, O my son, and receive my words, that years of life may be multiplied to thee. I will shew thee the way of wisdom, I will lead thee by the paths of equity: Which when thou shalt have entered, thy steps shall not be straitened, and when thou runnest thou shalt not meet a stumblingblock. Take hold on instruction, leave it not: keep it, because it is thy life.

lessons.la: RANCISCUS Paulæ, quod est Calábriæ óppidum, loco húmili natus est; quem paréntes, cum diu prole caruíssent, voto facto, beáti Francísci précibus suscepérunt. Is adoléscens divíno ardóre succénsus in erémum secéssit, ubi annis sex, victu ásperam, sed meditatiónibus cæléstibus suávem vitam duxit. Sed cum virtútum ejus fama lóngius manáret, multíque ad eum pietátis stúdio concúrrerent, fratérnæ caritátis causa ce solitúdine gréssus, ecclésiam prope Paulam ædificávit, ibíque prima sui órdinis fundaménta jecit.
lessons.en: This Francis was born of humble parents at Paola, a town in Calabria, (about the year of our Lord 1416.) His parents, who had long been childless, obtained him, after making a vow, by the prayers of blessed Francis. While he was yet a lad, the love of God moved him to withdraw into a desert place, where he lived for six years, hardly as to the body, but sumptuously in meditation on things heavenly. Nevertheless, when the fame of his holy life was noised abroad, and many betook themselves to him, that they might learn godliness, he was drawn out of the desert by love to his neighbour, and built a church near Paola, wherein he laid the first foundations of his Order.

lessons.la: E in eo mirífica loquéndi L. grátia: perpétuam virginitátem servávit: humilitátem sic cóluit, ut se ómnium mínimum díceret, suósque alúmnos Mínimos appellári volúcrit. nudis pédibus per glácies, nives, montes et acúta saxa, vepres spinásque absque laesióne incedébat. Rudi amíctu utebátur, humi cubábat. Cibi abstinéntia fuit admirábili: nam semel in die post solis occásum reficiebátur, et ad panem, et aqua potum, vix áliquid ejusmodi obsónii adhibébat, quo vesci in Quadragésima licet: quam consuetúdinem, ut fratres sui toto anni témpore retinérent, quarto eos voto astrínxit. Multa étiam futúra prophético spíritu prædíxit.

LURIMIS quoque miráculis servi sui sanctitátem Deus testári vóluit, quorum illud in primis célebre, quod a nautis rejéctus, Sicíliæ fretum strato super flúctibus pállio cum sócio transmísit. A Ludovíco undécimo Francórum rege expetítus, magnóque in honóre hábitus. est. Dénique annum círciter nonagésimum primum agens, vitǽque suæ finem jam próximum divína inspiratióne prospíciens, ómnibus ecclesiásticis. Sacraméntis et signo Crucis communítus, przelécta coram eo Domínica Passióne, die secúnda Aprílis, quæ fuit Parascéves, circa horam, qua Christus est passus, Turónis migrávit ad Dominum, anno salutis millésimo quingentésimo séptimo: Ejus corpus dies úndecim insepúltum, ita incorrúptum permánsit, ut suávem étiam odórem effláret. Ipsum vero Leo Papa décimus in Sanctórum númerum rétulit.

head: Cap. 7.
lessons.la: Uam pulchri sunt gressus tui in calceaméntis, fília príncipis! Quam pulchra es, et quam decóra caríssima, in delíciis! Statúra tua assimiláta est palmæ, et úbera tua botris. Dixi: Ascéndam in palmam, et apprehéndam fructus ejus: et erunt úbera tua sicut botri víneæ, et odor oris tui sicut malórum. Guttur tuum sicut vinum óptimum, dignum dilécto meo ad potándum, labiísque et déntibus illíus ad ruminándum. Ego dilécto meo, et ad me convérsio ejus. Veni dilécte mi, egrediámur in agrum, commorémur in villis. Mane surgámus ad víneas: videámus si flóruit vínea, si flores fructus partúriunt, si floruérunt mala púnica: ibi dabo tibi úbera mea. Mandrágoræ dedérunt odórem. In portis nostris ómnia poma: nova et vétera, dilécte mi, servávi tibi.
lessons.en: What shalt thou see in the Sulamitess but the companies of camps? How beautiful are thy steps in shoes, O prince’s daughter! The joints of thy thighs are like jewels, that are made by the hand of a skillful workman. How beautiful art thou, and how comely, my dearest, in delights! Thy stature is like to a palm tree, and thy breasts to clusters of grapes. I said: I will go up into the palm tree, and will take hold of the fruit thereof: and thy breasts shall be as the clusters of the vine: and the odour of thy mouth like apples. Thy throat like the best wine, worthy for my beloved to drink, and for his lips and his teeth to ruminate. I to my beloved, and his turning is towards me. Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field, let us abide in the villages. Let us get up early to the vineyards, let us see if the vineyard flourish, if the flowers be ready to bring forth fruits, if the pomegranates flourish: there will I give thee my breasts. The mandrakes give a smell. In our gates are all fruits: the new and the old, my beloved, I have kept for thee.

resp.a: Catharína Virgo Jesu Christo virginitátem | perpétuam dicávit
resp.b: Cujus sponsa sanctíssima íílico effécta est.
v: Maríam autem Vírginem adhuc puélla exorávit ut Fílii sui ancila fíeret.

head: Cap. a.
lessons.la: Diligéntibus Deum ómnia cooperántur in bonum, iis, qui secúndum propósitum vocáti sunt sancti. Nam quos præscívit, et prædestinávit confórmes fíeri imáginis Fílii sui, ut sit ipse primogénitus in multis frátribus. Quos autem prædestinávit, hos et vocávit: et quos vocávit, hos et justificávit: quos autem justificávit, illos et glorificávit. Quid ergo dicémus ad hæc? si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos? Quis ergo nos separábit a caritáte Christi? tribulátio? an angústia? an fames? an núditas? an perículum? an persecútio? an gládius? Sed in his ómnibus superámus propter eum, qui diléxit nos. Certus sum enim quia neque mors, neque vita, neque ángeli, neque principátus, neque virtútes, neque instántia, neque futúra, neque fortitúdo, neque altitúdo, neque profúndum, neque creatúra ália póterit nos separáre a caritáte Dei, qua est in Christo Jesu Dómino nostro.
lessons.en: And we know that to them that love God, all things work together unto good, to such as, according to his purpose, are called to be saints. For whom he foreknew, he also predestinated to be made conformable to the image of his Son; that he might be the firstborn amongst many brethren. And whom he predestinated, them he also called. And whom he called, them he also justified. And whom he justified, them he also glorified. What shall we then say to these things? If God be for us, who is against us? Who then shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall tribulation? or distress? or famine? or nakedness? or danger? or persecution? or the sword? But in all these things we overcome, because of him that hath loved us. For I am sure that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor might, Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

head: Cap. o.
lessons.la: M Autem absit gloriári, nisi in cruce Dómini nostri Jesu Christi: per quem mihi mundus crucifíxus est, et ego mundo. In Christo enim Jesu neque circumcísio áliquid valet, neque præpútium, se nova creatúra. Et quicúmque hanc régulam secúti fúerint, pax super illos, et misericórdia, et super Israël Dei. De cétero, nemo mihi moléstus sit: ego enim stígmata Dómini esu in córpore meo porto. Grátia Dómini nostri Jesu Christi, cum spíritu vestro, fratres. Amen.
lessons.en: But God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ; by whom the world is crucified to me, and I to the world. For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision, but a new creature. And whosoever shall follow this rule, peace on them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God. From henceforth let no man be troublesome to me; for I bear the marks of the Lord Jesus in my body. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brethren. Amen.

lessons.la: gus Enim quóniam si ter. réstris domus nostra hujus habitatiónis dissolvátur, quod ædificatiónem ex Deo hab. mus, domum non manufáctam, ætérnam in cælis. Nam et in hoc ingemíscimus, habitatiónem nostram, quæ de cælo est, superíndui cupiéntes: si tamen vestíti, non nudi inveniámur. Nam et qui sumus in hoc tabernáculo, ingemíscimus graváti: eo quod nólumus exspoliári, sed supervestíri, ut absorbeátur quod mortále est, a vita.
lessons.en: For we know, if our earthly house of this habitation be dissolved, that we have a building of God, a house not made with hands, eternal in heaven. For in this also we groan, desiring to be clothed upon with our habitation that is from heaven. Yet so that we be found clothed, not naked. For we also, who are in this tabernacle, do groan, being burthened; because we would not be unclothed, but clothed upon, that that which is mortal may be swallowed up by life.

Et ídeo conténdimus, sive abs énues, sive præséntes, placére illi. Omnes enim nos manifestári opórtet ante tribúnalChristi, ut réferat unusquísque pro pria córporis, prout gessit, sive bonum, sive malum.

lessons.la: Sciéntes ergo timórem Dómini, homínibus suadémus, Deo autem manifésti sumus. Spero autem et in consciéntiis vestris maniféstos nos esse. Noniterum commendámus nos vobis, sed occasiónem damus vobis gloriándi pro nobis: ut habeátis ad eos, qui in fácie gloriántur, et non in corde. Sive enim mente excédimus, Deo: sive sóbrii sumus, vobis. Cáritas enim Christi urget nos:
lessons.en: Knowing therefore the fear of the Lord, we use persuasion to men; but to God we are manifest. And I trust also that in your consciences we are manifest. We commend not ourselves again to you, but give you occasion to glory in our behalf; that you may have somewhat to answer them who glory in face, and not in heart. For whether we be transported in mind, it is to God; or whether we be sober, it is for you. For the charity of Christ presseth us: judging this, that if one died for all, then all were dead.

lessons.la: NCEN Tius, honesta stirpe Valentiæ in Hispania natus, ab ineunte ætate cor gessit senile. Qui dum caliginosi hujus sæculi labilem cursum pro ingenii sui modulo consideraret, religionis habitum in ordine Prædicatorum decimo octavo ætatis suæ anno suscepit; et emissa solemni professione, sacris litteris sedulo incumbens, theologiæ lauream summa cum laude consecutus est. Mox obtenta a superioribus licentia, verbum Dei prædicare, Judæorum perfidiam arguere, Saracenorum errores confutare tanta virtute et efficacia cœpit, ut ingentem ipsorum infidélium multitudinem ad Christi fidem perduxerit, et multa Christianorum millia a peccatis ad pœnitentiam, a vítiis ad virtutem revocarit. Electus enim a Deo, ut monita salutis in omnes gentes, tribus et linguas difunderet, et extremi tremendique judicii diem appropinquare ostenderet, omnium auditorum animos terrore concussos, atque a terrenis affectibus avulsos, ad Dei amórem excitabat. —
lessons.en: This Vincent was born of respectable parents, at Valencia in Spain, (upon the 23rd day of January, in the year of our Lord 1357.) Even as a child he had an heart like the heart of an old man. Considering, to the utmost of his young understanding, how fleeting is the course of this dark world, he, in the eighteenth year of his age, took the habit of a Friar in the Order of Preachers. After he had made his solemn profession, he devoted himself to sacred learning, and took the degree of Master in Divinity with much distinction. He soon after received permission from his superiors to preach the word of God, on which duty he entered with such power and success, striving against the unbelief of the Jews, and overthrowing the errors of the Saracens, that he brought an exceeding great multitude of unbelievers to believe in Christ, and turned many thousands of Christians from sin to sorrow, and from vice to virtue. He was a chosen vessel unto God to proclaim the tidings of salvation among all nations, and tribes, and tongues, crying out that the last day, that awful day of judgment, is at hand, smiting consternation into the minds of all, as many as heard him, weaning their love from a perishing world, and turning it to God.

lessons.la: N hoc autem apostolico múI hic vitæ ejus tenor perpetuus fuit quotidie Missam summo mane cum cantu celebravit. Quotidie ad populum concionem habuit; inviolabile semper jejunium, nisi urgens adesset necessitas, servavit; sancta et recta consilia nulli denegavit, carnes nunquam comedit, nec vestem lineam induit: populorum jurgia sedavit, dissidentia regna pace composuit: et cum vestis inconsutilis Ecclesiæ diro schismate scinderetur, ut uniretur, et unita servaretur, plurimum laboravit. Virtutibus omnibus claruit, suosque detractores et persecutores, in simplicitate et humilitate ambulans, cum mansuetudine recepit, et amplexus est.
lessons.en: While Vincent wrought the Apostolic work of preaching committed to him, he lived ever as follows j Every morning he sang a solemn Mass, and every day he preached in public. He fasted every day, unless prevented by some absolute necessity. He refused to no one his holy and just advice. He never ate meat, nor wore linen. He quieted public disturbances, and negotiated the peace of kingdoms. When the seamless garment of the Church was rent by an horrid schism, he worked his every nerve to unite it again, and keep it one. He was a burning and a shining light of all virtues, walking always in lowliness and simpleness, so that he meekly welcomed and embraced them which spake evil against him and persecuted him.

Senio tandem et morbo cor. féctus infatigabilis Evangelii præco, plurimis Europæ pro. vínciis cum ingenti animarum fructu peragratis, Venetiæ in Britannia minori prædicationis et vitæ cursum feliciter con. summávit, anno salutis millesimo quadringentesimo dé. cimo nono: quem Callistus tertius sanctorum numero adscrípsit.

Non ad duas quippe urbes, aut decem, aut vigínti, neque ad unam gentem vos mitto, sicut mittébam Prophétas : sed ad omnem terram prorsus ac mare, totúimque mundum, et hunc váriis criminibus oppréssum. N E ígitur putétis, inquit, ad lévia vos ducéndos esse certámina, neque exiguárum rerum vobis ineúndam esse ratiónem. Vos estis sal terræ. Quid ínitur? Ipsíne putrefácta medicáti sunt? lessons.la: NTONIUS Pavónius, szeculo décimo quarto Saviliáni in dicecési Taurinénsi nóbili ortus, ab adolescén54 mundánis rebus abdicátis, icatórum Órdinem amlexus est. Sacræ huic milítiæ adscríptus, ad sublimiórem inimi virtútem divinarúmque literárum cognitiónem comarándam omnes ánimi cogitaúónes curásque convértit, w deínceps zelo secúndum siéntiam prǽlia Dómini prceliári posset. Quam ob rem, vir factus, cum magna sanctitátis doctrinæque existimatióne floréret, non modo Savilianénsis cenóbii præses constitútus est, verum étiam fídei Quiesítor in Longobardía superióre atque Ligúria renuntiátus fuit. Hoc génere que religiónis munus, calamitósis ádeo tempóribus ipsi concréditum, innúmeras exercéndee. virtútis opportunitátes eídem áttulit, iisque ómnibus par semper est visus. Nam assíduo verbi ministério ignorántiam divínæ legis morúmque corruptélas, unde hǽreses oríri solent, «efficáciter — coércuit. Tum vero erróres représsit, heereticórum fraudes detéxit, tósque a dispergéndo Domiínico grege invícte prohíbuit.

LACUIT autem divínze Clcméntize ut vitze tam sancte atque utíliter actee copiósa mérita excellentióre martýrii laude cumularéntur, idque a beáto Viro divínitus przecóghitum przedictúmque narrátur. Nam anno millésimo trecentésimo septuagésimo quarto, Bricherásium olim Taurinénsis, nunc vero Pineroliénsis Kecésis óppidum advéntans, ut quos ibi ab hzeréticis decéautem tutándze propagandzeptos audíerat, ad cathólicam unitátem revocáret, tonsóris cujúsdam óperam exquírens, admónuit ut apte perpolíret hóminem ad núptias eo in loco celebrándas invitátum. Cumque ille objíceret nullas in vico núptias parári, Vir sanctus, Ne dúbites, inquit, quia vera loquor. * Jam próxima Domínica die, in quam Resurrectiónis Dómini Octáva incidébat, cum idem Beátus Missæ sacrum celebrásset in ecclésia dicti loci, ac Dei verbo e suggéstu propósito hzereticórum erróres arguísset : septem ex illis hzeréticis, malígno concitáti spíritu, diversísque armis accíncti benígnum salútis suze Médicum ab ecclésia egrediéntem invádunt, ac hílari ánimo martýrium obeúntem, immániter prope eam trucídant. Sic ille, in Agni sánguine dealbáta stola, ad czeléstes ipsíus Agni núptias introdúci méruit.

M5 exúviz, Saviliánum ad sui ccenóbii ecclésiam translátze, miráculis ádeo illustrátae perhibéntur, ut sequénte século de ipsis honorificéntius tumulándis deliberátum fúerit. Id vero solémniter prǽstitit beátus ipsíus succéssor Aimo Taparéllus, qui toto Savilianénsi pópulo spectánte, gloriósum Mártyris corpus humilióre — sepúlcro edúctum, ad aram quamdam illíus ecclésize pie éxtulit, inter festa Redemptóris Natalítia, anno millésimo quadringentésimo sexagésimo octávo. Exínde autem beáto Mártyri rcligiósum cultum fidéles adhibére non desiérunt : qui plura obtentórum beneficiórum monuménta ad ipsíus túmulum apposuísse, ejúsque opem, przesértim ad res depérditas inveniéndas, implorásse ferúntur. At incúnte século décimo nono, cum Religiósa claustra in magna rerum ómnium perturbatióne fcede violaréntur, ossa Maártyris profanatióni illus templi atque ccenóbii subdúcta sunt, ac Raconixium tandem ad ecclésiam restitúti Ordinis transláta. Quem cultum illústri Mártyri præstitum Pius Nonus Póntifex Máximus confirmávit, utque ejus festívitas in univérso Praedicatórum Ordine ac in Taurinénsi et Pineroliénsi dicecésibus próprio Offício et Missa celebrarétur indúlsit.

lessons.la: NTONIUS Rívulis, dicecésis Taurinénsis óppido, ho. néstis paréntibus natus, adoléscens Floréntize in ccenóbio sancti Marci, cui tunc sanctus Antonínus prǽerat, cooptátus est in Órdinem Przedicatórum. Cum Neápolim profectúrus e Sicília solvisset, a pirátis Tu. neténsibus captus atque in Africam abdiúctus, postquam gráviter eam aliquándiu tulit calamitátem, ad extrémum Jesu Christi fidem ejurávit. Quartum jam 'mensenm in eo cœno hzeréntem respéxit miséricors Deus, extulítque magnitúdine virtútis suze. Quare ille, abjécta nefária superstitióne, áliquot ménsibus ad próximum sese certámen exércuit voluntáriis afllictatiónibus córporis divinique Offícii recitatióne. Inde expiátus Pceniténtiae Eucharisti:teque sacris, vestibúsque Ordinis amíctus, Tunéti régulum e castris revérsum convénit, et in magna hóminum frequéntia, seípsum accúsans impietátis, unam religiónem christiánam, a qua defécerat, veram esse testátus, multa de Christo magnífice przedicávit.

EGULUS, cum magnis eum Ix. pollicitatiónibus — blandi: piísque frustra tentásset, ábripi rem, tectaque praeudicium tradi jussit. sed Vir Dei nefárium hóminem, tríduum ipsum se ad defectiónem sollicitántem, freit máxima ánimi fortitúdine. Intérea illátas sibi a bárbaris contumélias inflictásque plagas patientíssime pérfcrens, et submíssa sibi a Christiánis subsídia egénis distríbuens, ípseque pane solum et aqua vitam tólerans, ad morten sese parábat. * Quinto ad eo, quo in cárcerem conjéctus fúerat, die, cum eum judex ad se addúci fecísset, constantémque in senténtia manére animadvertísset, lapídibus Óbrui imperávit. Ítaque ad martýrii locum raptus, pósitis génibus, tensísque ad cælum mánibus, orans, vim in se conjectórum lápidum in cárcel sidi in immótus sustínuit, et Martyr decéssit quarto Idus Aprílis anno millésimo quadringentésimo sexagésimo.

XSTINCTI corpus cum bár4 bari cremáre conáti essent, mirabíliter ab igne intáctum, Genuénses, qui mercatúram Tunéti exercébant, prétio re-. cuperárunt : quod lotum, suavémque spirans odórem, deínceps Génuam missum, beátus Amadéus Tértius Sabáudiz Dux, anno millésimo quadringentésimo sexagésimo nono Rívulos transferéndum curávit. Cumque ad mortis fórtiter pro Christo óbitze glóriam benefícia accessissent, quibus se multi beáti Antónii méritis auctos fuísse profitebántur, confirmátus majórem in moum est propagatúsque reliBiósus hóminum erga ipsum cultus. Quem nunquam intermíssum Clemens Décimus tértius Póntifex Máximus probávit, Ordinique Przedicatórum , univérso Offícii in ejus honórem recitándi Misszeque cele- , brándze potestátem fecit.

lessons.la: Eo primus, Etruscus, eo tempore pra fuit Ecclésiæ, cum rex Hunnorum Attila, cognomento F lagéllum Dei, in Italiam invadens, Aquilejam triennii obsidione captam diripuit et incendit. Unde cum Romam ardenti furore raperetur, jamque copias, ubi Mincius in Padum influit, trajicere pararet, occurrit ei Leo, malorum Italiæ impendentium misericordia permotus: cujus divina eloquentia persuasum est Attilæ, ut regrederetur. Qui interrogatus a suis, quid esset quod præter consuetudinem tam humiliter Romani Pontificisimperáta faceret; respondit, se astantem quemdam alium, illo loquente, sacerdotali habitu veritum esse, sibi stricto gladio minitantem mortem, nisi Leoni obtemperaret. Quare in Pannoniam reversus est.
lessons.en: Leo was an Etruscan who ruled the Church at the time when Attila, king of the Huns, whose surname is the Scourge of God, invaded Italy, and after a siege of three years, took, sacked, and burnt Aquileia. Thence he was hurrying to Rome, on fire with anger, and his troops were already preparing to cross the Po, at the place where that river is joined by the Mincio, when he was met by Leo, moved with compassion at the thought of the ruin which hung over Italy. By his God-given eloquence, Attila was persuaded to turn back, and when he was afterwards asked by his servants why, contrary to his custom, he had so meekly yielded to the entreaties of the Bishop of Rome, he answered that he had been alarmed by a figure dressed like a Priest, which had appeared at the side of Leo while he was speaking, holding a drawn sword, and had made as though to kill the king unless he consented. And so he returned into Pannonia.

lessons.la: Eo autem Rome singulári ómnium lætítia excéptus, paulo post invadénti Urbem Genseríco, eádem eloquéntiæ vi et sanctitatis opinione persuásit, ut ab incendio, ignomíniis, ac cædibus abstinéret. Sed cum Ecclésiam a multis hærésibus oppugnari, maximéque a Nestoriánis et Eutychiánis exagitári vidéret; ad cam purgandam, et in fide catholica confirmandam, concíliumChalcedonénse indixit, ubi sexcentis triginta coactis episcopis, Eutyches et Dióscorus, et iterum Nestórius condemnáti sunt: ejusdemque concílii decréta sua auctoritate confirmavit.
lessons.en: While Leo went back to Rome, where he was received with rejoicing by all men. A while later, Genseric entered the city, but Leo, by the power of his eloquence and the authority of his holy life, persuaded him to abstain from fire, insult, and slaughter. When Leo beheld how the Church was assailed by many heresies, and in dire trouble through the Nestorians and Eutychians, to purify the same and establish her in the Catholic Faith, he called the Council of Chalcedon, where, in an assembly of six hundred and thirty Bishops Nestorius was again condemned, along with Eutyches and Dioscorus; the decrees of which Council were confirmed by the authority of Leo.

lessons.la: Is actis, sanctus Pontifex l se ad reficiendas et ædificandas ecclesias convertit. Cujus suasu Demetria, pia femina, sancti Stephani ecclesiam construxit in suo fundo via Latina, tertio ab Urbe milliario: ipse via Appia sub nó. mine sancti Cornelii alteram condidit. Multas præterea e sacras ædes, et sacra earum vasa restituit. In tribus basilicis, Petri, Pauli, et Constantiniana, cameras exstruxit: Edi. ficávit monasterium vicinum basilicæ sancti Petri: sepulcris Apostolorum custodes adhibuit, quos cubicularios appellavit. Statuit, ut in actione mysterii diceretur: Sanctum sacrificium, immaculatam hostiam. Sanxit, ne monacha be. nedíctum capitis velamen reciperet, nisi quadraginta annó. rum virginitatem probasset. His et aliis præclare gestis, cum multa sancte et luculenter scripsisset, tértio Idus Aprílis obdormivit in Domino. Sedit in pontificatu annos viginti menses decem, dies vigínti octo.

lessons.la: * ETRUS González, sanctus Tellus vulgo appellátus, Fromestz in Hispánia apud Paléntiam piis ac nobílibus paréntibus ortus est. Adolécscens, sub Epíscopi Palentíni avúnculi sui cura, ingénuis ártibus et philosophíze óperam dedit, ingénio ad preclára queque aptíssimo. Sed ejúsdem Ecclésize Canonicátu, et mox étiam Decanátus dignitáte auctus, honórum ac divitiárum illécebris juveniliter abréptus, sǽculi vanitáti paulo libérius indúlsit. Áccidit vero ut cum ipso Domínicee Nativitátis die, equo spléndide phaleráto zequálium comitátu totam urbem lasciviens circumcursáret, equo in profúndum lutum repénte prolápso, dejéctus ipse, multóque cceno inquinátus, spectántium risu sannísque excéptus sit. Quo insígni pudóre suffúsus, et mundi, cui placére studúerat, contuméliam réputans, se vicíssim, a quo spretus esset, spretúrum constítuit. Ígitur paulo post, magna ómnium admiratióne, in Przedicatórum Órdinem sese recépit : ubi véterem hóminem cum áctibus suis éruens, novúmque induens, exímize pósuit tirocínia sanctitátis.

lessons.homily_head: Sermo illi vivus et éfficax, quo audiéntium corda ádeo pervadébat, ut per eas quas apostólico zelo peragrávit Hispánize províncias, innúmeros fere peccatóres ad poeniténtiam addúxerit.
lessons.gospel: |, , D céteras autem virtútes, quibus brevi magnópere excéllut, caritátem — áttulit proximórum salútis cupidíssimam. Quare absolúto sacrárum litterárum stúdio, sancto Patre Domínico adimitándum sibi propósito, przedicatióni se totum dedit, nihil a Deo impénsius flágitans quam ut revocándis in viam salútis animábus pérditis idóneus efficerétur. Severíssimam, apostólico more, eo in múnere paupertátemexércuit. Quocúmque exciperétur hospítio, non inde prius exíbat quam íncolas omnes sacra exomológesi expiásset.
lessons.la: Ferdinándum regem, cognoménto Sanctum, in várias advérsus Mauros expeditiónes eúntem secútus, consíliis, exémplo et oratió. nibus mirífice juvit. Venústas féminas ejus amóre Captas, aliásque procacióres ad eum immíssas, ut pudicítiae ejus insídias strúerent, non solum strénue répulit, sed ad meliórem vitæ frugem convértit.

* INIO flúmini prope Ribadáviam longe rápido atque effúso, pública transeúntium utilitááte pontem amplíssimum fere miráculo impósuit, accíta ad óperis molitiónem ingénti structórum manu : quibus cum cibus aliquándo defíceret, evocátos quotquot iis reficiéndis suffícerent pisces, manúque prehénsos, iísdem præbuit. Sed et sócios labóre itíneris atque inédia fere deficjéntes pane et vino cǽlitus suppeditátis recreávit. Adhuc vivens, in szevíssima maris procéla a nautis invocátus, eísdem sese conspícuum exlibuísse fertur tempestatémque sedásse. Prophético spíritu futúra multa przenuntiávit,atque imprímis extrémum vitæ sue diem : quo adventánte, in Tudénsem sese urbem recépit ubi méritis et labóribus ple nus, sancto fine quiévit. Ejus corpus honorífico sepúlcro á Epíscopo Tudénsi cónditum est : unde miræ fragrántie óleum manásse tráditur, ae£r* salubérrimum. Ejus miracul rum fama ad remótas usque Américae regiónes pervagáta, ingénti populórum veneratióne invocári et coli ccepit, a nautis cumprímis, qui cjus opem in maris tempestátibus przesentíssimam expérti, eum sub invocatióne sancti Telmi in Tutelárem sibi adscivérunt. Illíus cultum continénter propagátum approbávit Benedíctus Décimus quartus, ejúsque festum cum Offício et Missa ab univérso Preedicatórum Ordine, nec non a Clero Palentíno et Tudénsi celebrári concéssit.
