lessons.la: Liis generatiónibus non est ágnitum fíliis hóminum, sícuti nunc revelátum est sanctis apóstolis ejus, et prophétis in Spíritu, gentes esse coherédes, et concorporáles, et compartícipes promissiónis ejus in Christo Jesu per Evangélium: cujus factus sum nni ster, secúndum donum grátie Dei, quæ data est mihi secúndum operatiónem virtútis cjus. R. j Ecce ego mitto vos sicut oves in médio lupórum, dicit Dóminus: * Estóte ergo pri déntes sicut. serpéntes, et símplices sicut coláúmbae. X. Tra dent enim vos in concíliis, et in synagógis suis flagellábunt vos, — Estóte ergo.

tui ómnium sanctórum ht mínimo data est grátia bach, in géntibus evangelizáre investigábiles divítias Christi, et illumináre omnes, quæ sit dispensátio sacraménti abscónditi a sǽculis in Deo, qui ómnia creávit: ut innotéscat principátibus, et potestátibus in cæléstibus per Ecclésiam, multifórmis sapiéntia Dei, secúndum præfinitiónem sæculórum, quam fecit in Christo Jesu Dómino nostro: in quo habémus fidúciam, et accéssum in confidéntia per fidem ejus. E. ii Tóllite jugum meum super vos dicit Dóminus, et díscite a me, quia mitis sum, et húmilis corde: * Jugum enim meum suáve est, et onus meum leve. Et inveniétis réquiem animábus vestris, — jugum enim meum.

Dionem Quod peto ne defieds in tribulatiónibus meis pro vobis: quæ est glória vestra. Hujus rei grátia flecto génua mea ad Patrem Dómini nostri Jesu Christi, ex quo omnis patérnitas in cælis, et in terra nominátur, ut det vobis secúndum divítias glóriæ suæ, virtúte corroborári per Spíritum cjus in interiórem hóminem, Christum habitáre per fidem in córdibus vestris: E. iii. Dum stetéritis ante reges et prǽsides, nolíte cogitáre quómodo, aut quid loquámini Dábitur enim vobis in illa hora, quid loquámini. Y. Non enim vos estis, qui loquímini, sed Spíritus Patris vestri, qui lóquitur in vobis. — Dábitur enim vobis, Gléria. Dábitur enim vobis.

Jacóbus, Zébida fílius, Joánnis Apóstoli germánus frater, Galilǽus, inter prinios Apóstolos vocátus cum fratre, relíctis patre ac rétibus, secútus est Dóminum, et ambo ab ipso Jesu Boanérges, id est, tonítrui fili, sunt appelláti. Is unus fuit ex tribus Apóstolis, quos Salvátor máxime diléxit, et testes esse vóluitsuze transfiguratiónis, et interésse miráculo cum archisynagógi fíliam a mórtuis excitávit, et adésse cum secéssit in montem Olivéti, Patrem oratúrus, ántequam a Judǽis comprehenderétur.
lessons.en: James, the Son of Zebedee and brother of the Apostle John, was a Galilean, and with his brother one of the first of His Apostles whom the Lord called, whileas they were in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets and they immediately left the ship, and their father, and followed Him. (Matth. iv. 21, 22.) And He surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder. (Mark iii. 17.) Peter, and James, and John, were the three Apostles whom the Saviour loved best; them He took and brought up into an high mountain apart, and was transfigured before them, (Matth. xvii. 1,2;) when He went to the house of the ruler of the synagogue to raise his daughter from the dead, He suffered no man to follow Him save Peter, and James, and John, (Mark v. 37;) and, at the last, just before the Jews took Him, when He cometh unto a place called Gethsemane, and saith unto the disciples: Sit ye here, while I go and pray yonder. He took with Him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee. (Matth. xxvi. 36, 37.)

lessons.la: Dor Jesu Christi ascénsum in cælum, in Judǽa et Samaría ejus divinitátem prǽdicans, plúrimos ad christiánam fidem perdúxit. Mox in Hispániam proféctus, ibi áliquos ad Christum convértit; ex quorum número septem póstea epíscopi a beáto Petro ordináti in Hispániam primi dirécti sunt. Deínde Jerosólymam revérsus, cum inter álios Hermógenem magum fídei veritáte imbuísset, Heródes Agríppa Cláudio imperatóre ad regnum elátus ut a Judǽis grátiam iníret, Jacóbum líbere Jesum Christum Deum confiténtem cápitis condemnávit. Quem cum is, ui eum dúxerat ad tribúnal, fórtiter martýrium subeúntem vidísset, statim se et ipse Christiánum esse proféssus est.
lessons.en: After that Jesus Christ was ascended into heaven, James preached how that He was God, and led many in Judaea and Samaria to the Christian Faith. A while afterward, he went to Spain, and there he brought some to Christ, of whom seven were afterwards ordained Bishops by Blessed Peter, and were the first such sent into that country. From Spain James went back to Jerusalem, where he taught the Faith to diverse persons, and, among others, to the Magician Hermogenes. Thereupon Herod Agrippa, who had been raised to the kingdom under the Emperor Claudius, to curry favour with the Jews, condemned James to death for his firm confession that Jesus Christ is God. The officer who led James to the judgment-seat, at sight of the courage wherewith he was ready to offer up his testimony, declared himself also to be a Christian.

resp.b: Modo coronántur, et accípiunt palmam.
v: Isti sunt qui venérunt ex magna tribulatióne, et lavérunt stolas suas in sánguine Agni.

lessons.la: D supplícium cum rapta réntur, pétiit ille a Jacóbo véniam; quem Jacóbus osculátus, Pax, inquit, tibi sit. Itaque utérque est secúri percússus, cum paulo ante Jacóbus paralýticum sanásset. Corpus ejus póstea Compostéllam translátum est, ubi summa celebritáte cólitur, conveniéntibus eo religiónis et voti causa ex toto terrárum orbe peregrínis. Memória ipsíus natális hodiérno die, qui translatiónis dies est, ab Ecclésia celebrátur, cum ipse circa festum Paschæ, primus Apostolórum Jerosólymis profúso sánguine testimónium esu Christo déderit. M Vos estis lux mundi, dicit Dóminus, * Qui In patiéntia vestra possidébitis ánimas vestras, et ego dispóno vobis sicut dispósuit mihi Pater meus regnum, ut edátis et bibátis super mensam meam in regno meo. — Qui in patiéntia vestra. Glória. Possidébitis ánimas vestras.

Quǽritur quómodo cálicem martýrii Zebedǽi, fílii, Jacóbus vidélicet et Joánnes, bíberint; cum Scriptúra narret Jacóbum tantum Apóstolum ab Heróde cápite truncátum, Joánnes autem própria morte vitam finíerit. Sed, si legámus ecclesiásticas histórias, in quibus fertur, quod et ipse propter martýrium sit missus in fervéntis ólei dólium, et inde ad suscipiéndam corónam Christi athléta procésserit, statímque relegátus in Patmos ínsulam sit; vidébimus martýrio ánimum non defuísse, et bibísse Joánnem cálicem confessiónis,

lessons.la: UGUSTINUS Bugélle, cum hzec Vercellénsis agri atque dicecésis illústre adhuc esset óppidum, nóbili stirpe de Fángiis szeculo décimo quinto ortus est. Adoléscens Praedicatórum Ordini, in pátrio sancti Domínici ccenóbio nuper exstrúcto, nomen dedit; ac tali ardóre ad acquiréndam sanctórum sciéntiam conténdit, ut brevi egrégiam rerum divinárum cognitiónem adéptus sit, atque ipsos evangélicze perfecliónis ápices attígerit. Ítaque licet ejus vita tamquam singuláre innocéntize exémplar celebrarétur, níhilo tamen sécius carnem suam vigíliis, aspérrimo cilício ac fere contínuo jejúnio constánter afflíxit. Hinc magnam ánimi patiéntiam consecútus est: éaque tunc máxime enítuit, cum ei summa úlcerum ora, quibus totum corpus aliquándo infestabátur, ferro preecideréntur : tantum enim cruciátum, nullo prorsus édito dolóris indício, mira tranquillitáte pértulit. Non minus przeclára ipsíus fuit humílitas. Caritátis autem ejus in Deum tanta vis éxstitit, ut semper oráre viderétur, nec solum mente in czelum éerécta, sed córpore ipso e terra frequénter cleváto. Sápius étiam inter orándum vim lacrimárum profundébat, máxime cum vel canónicas preces in choro persólveret, vel ad altáre sacris operarétur.

Es Deíparam Vírginem insígni quoque pietáte ac religióne fuit. Proximórum salútis cupidíssimus, in verbi ministério, excipiendisque pceniténtium confessiónibus, in consíliis feréndis, in visitatióne infirmórum indeféssam óperam pósuit, atque ádeo innúmeris méritis ánimos sibi Christi fidélium, ipsorúmque Ecclésie Pastórum devínxit. Ccenobiórum regímini váriis in locis przeféctus, prístinum ubíque reguláris observántize decus vel collápsum restítuit, vel restitútum asséruit. Multis, étiam extérius, colluctatiónibus a dzemónibus véexátus, nunquam cessit eórum insídiis atque furóri : immo tale in ipsos impérium divínitus obtínuit, uL fácile eos ab obséssis corpóribus depélleret. Tanta étiam grátia ab omnipoténti Deo ditátus est, ut sola oratióne vel attáctu salútem eegrótis haud raro impertiret. Áliis ínsuper adhuc vivens claruisse fertur miráculis,e quibus véterum monumentórum consénsu memórize próditum, quod in óppido Soncini infántem sine baptísmo — mórtuum — lugénti matri, ac mox prodigii admiratióne et gáudio stupénti, restitúerit vivunt.

STREMOS ingravescéntis cetátis annos, inter assídua ómnium virtútum exercítia, Venétis transégit in célebri olim arctióris disciplínæ ceenóbio sancti Domínici. Ihi extrémo tandem morbo corréptus, Ecclésize Sacraméntis devotíssime suscéptis, ad óbitum se comparávit. lessons.la: NTONIUS nóbili génere natus in óppido prope Vercéllas, quod a sancto Germáno nomen duxit, in Insúbrize fínibus, totum ab ineúnte zetáte oratióni ac litterárum stúdio se dédidit. Hinc ardentíssimo desidério flagrans Przedicatórum Ordini sese addicéndi, reluctántis patris oppositiónibus bona cum vénia superátis, | illum tandem Vercéllis ampléxus est. Eo suscépto Instituto, exsultávit ut gigas ad currén- | dam perfectiónis viam : tantóque ánimi fervóre humilitáti, suique ipsíus abnegatióni, tum étiam oratióni ac divinárum rerum stúdio sese devóvit, ut brevi et sanctitátis exémplum, et sacrárum scientiárum doctiíssimus eváserit, Paupertátem, obediéntiam ac regulárem disciplínam severíssime cóluit : castitátem vero tum solertíssima sénsuum custódia, tum assídua carnis maceratióne semper illibátam servávit.

Acris Ordínibus initiátus, promovéndze Dei glórize, iominúmque saláti, przedicatióne, consíliis, ac Sacraméntis Omnem navávit óperam : in quo quidem usque ad últimum Vite éxitum tanta prudéntia, lemitáte ac sollicitúdine se exércuit, ut nemo tam pérvicax esset, qui non mélior factus, aut tristis ab eo discéderet : ipsámque Novocómi civitátem, in qua tunc corrúpti mores irrépserant, ad bonam frugem revocávit. Quamvis autem honóres ac praefectúras summópere aversarétur, tamen Presidum jussu eas gérere coáctus est Novocómi, Savónze, Floréntize, atque Bonónize: et ubíque regulárem observántiam verbo et exémplo restítuit, Savóna proféctus, a pirátis capius fuit, ac mirífice liberátus.

T3356 prophetíze, sanitátum ac discretiónis spirítuum divínitus ditátus est, Floréntize muto a nativitáte loquélam impetrásse, plurésque undequáque zegrotántes a difúicillimis morbis sua tantum benedictióne sanásse fertur. Olim visus est sénsibus alienátus dúlcia cum Deípara habére collóquia, refulgénte divíno quodam splendóre cubículo, Novocómum revocátus, impendéntem suum óbitum preenuntiávit; morbóque corréptus inter astántium láácrimas placidíssime quiévit in Dómino, anno Reparatiónis millésimo quadringentésimo quinquaeésimo nono, annos natus quinque et sexagínta, Ejus funus ingénti pópuli accúrsu, et complúribus signis illustrátum fuit: Sacræ autem ejus exúviæ recónditze in ecclésia sancti J]oánnis prope Novocómum, unde die vigésima octáva Quintílis anni millésimi octingentésimi décimi ad parochiálem sancti Germáni ecclésiam solémni ritu translátze fuérunt. Beáti cultum ab illíus óbitu incéptum Pius Séptimus Póntifex Máximus rite approbávit, indulsitque ut in utráque dicecési, Novocoménsi scílicet ac Vercellénsi, nec non ab univérso Przedicatórum Ordine beáti Antónii memória cum Offício et Missa quinto Kaléndas Augústi, illíus translatiónis die, quotánnis recolátur.

lessons.la: Arrha Lázari soror, nobílibus et copiosis paréntibus nata, sed Christi hospítio MARTH. E Vírginis, LONG C UPC. e Eris clarior, post ejus ascénsum in cælum, cum fratre, sorore, et Marcella pedíssequa, ac Maximino, uno ex septuagínta duo. bus discípulis Christi Dómini, qui totam illam domum baptizaverat, multisque aliis Christiánis, comprehensa a udzeis, in navem sine velo ac remigio impónitur, vastissi. móque mari ad certum nay. frágium committitur. Sed pa. vis, Deo gubernante, salvis ómnibus, Massiliam appulsa est.

o miraculo et horum præ. dicatióne primum Massilienses, mox Aquenses ac finítimæ gentes in Christum credidérunt; Lazarusque Massiliensium Maximinus Aquensium — epíscopus creatur. Magdalena vero, assueta oratióni et pédibus Dómini, ut optima parte contemplandæ cæléstis beatitúdinis, quam elégerat, fruerétur, in vastam altíssimi montis spelúncam se cóntulit; ubi trigínta annos vixit, ab omni hóminum consuetúdine disjuncta, quotidiéque per id tempus ad audiendas cæléstium laudes in altum ab Angelis elata.
lessons.en: Through this miracle and the preaching of the Saints, the people of Marseilles first, and then those of Aix, and of the uttermost tribes, believed in Christ, and Lazarus was made Bishop of Marseilles, and Maximin Bishop of Aix. Mary Magdalene sat still at Jesus' Feet, being altogether given to prayer and the contemplation of heavenly blessedness, that that good part which she had chosen might not be taken away from her, withdrew herself to a great cave in an exceeding high mountain, where she lived for thirty years, utterly cut off from all conversation with men, and every day during that time carried up by Angels into the air, to listen to them that dwell in heaven praising God.

lessons.la: Arrha autem, mirábili vitæ sanctitáte et caritate, ómnium Massiliensium ánimis in sui amórem et admiratiónem adductis, in locum a viris remotum cum aliquot honestíssimis féminis se recepit; ubl summa cum laude pietátis et prudéntiæ diu vixit, ac demum, morte sua multo ante prædicta, miraculis clara migrávit ad Dóminum, quarto Kalendas IB— Adam Die XXIX. Júlii. In Oct. s. MARU E Magdalénæ, Augusti. Cujus corpus apud Tarascum magnam habet veneratiónem.

lessons.la: Arrha et Maria duæ soIVÀ róres erant, ambæ non solum carne, sed étiam religióne germanæ; ambæ Dómino cohzesérunt: ambæ Dómino in carne præsénti concorditer serviérunt. Suscépit eum Martha, sicut solent súscipi peregrini; sed tamen suscépit famula Dóminum, ægra Salvatórem, creatura Creatórem. Suscépit autem spíritu pascenda, in carne pascéndum. Voluit enim Dóminus formam servi accípere, et, accepta forma servi, in illa pasci a servis, dignatióne, non conditione. Nam et ista dignátio fuit, se præbére pascéndum. Lectio viii — ABEBAT carnem, in qua esuriret quidem, et sitiret; sed nescítis, quia in erémo esuriénti Angeli ministrábant? Ergo quod pasci vóluit, pascénti præstitit. Quid autem mirum, si et de sancto Elía præstitit víduæ, quem prius, corvo ministrante, pascebat? Numquid pascéndo defécerat, quando ad víduam mittebat? Nequaquam, sed religiosam víduam, per obsequium exhibitum servo suo, benedicere disponebat.

Sc ergo susceptus est Dóminus, tamquam hospes, qui in sua propria venit, et sui eum non recepérunt; sed quotquot recepérunt eum, dedit eis potestátem fílios Dei fíeri, adoptans servos et liberos fáciens, rédimens captivos et fáciens coheredes. Ne quis tamen vestrum fórsitan dicat: O beáti, qui Christum suscipere in domum propriam meruérunt! Noli dolére, noli murmurare quia tempóribus natus es, quando jam Dóminum non vides in carne. Non tibi ábstulit istam dignatiónem. Cum uni, inquit, ex minimis meis fecistis, mihi fecistis. in Láudibus Memória Ss. Felicis, Simplicii, Faustini et Beatrícis Mártyrum, Oratio. pus. quǽsumus Dómine: utsicut pópulus christiánus Mártyrum tuórum Felicis, Simplicii, Faustini et Beatrícis temporáli solemnitáte congáudet, ita perfruátur aet.

lessons.la: ANNES, sive Mameértus, Calaróg:ze in Hispánia ex nobilíssimis paréntibus Felíci de Guzman pietáte exímio, et beáta Joánna de Aza progé nitus,fratrem germánum hábuit divum Domínicum Predicatórum Ordinis Institutórem. Tantórum paréntum roborátus exémplis, morum sanctitáte et vite innocéntia elúxit. Sacre milítize manctpátus, ceeléstium contemplatióne mirum in modum przecélluit, atque sancti et contemplatóris nómine passim nuncupári consuévit.Sed animárum zelus quo lagrábat, ad majóra cum excitávit, ádco ut, quamquam illi recéssus delíciis affúerit, frequens tamen esset ad popirlum conciónibus instituéndum. In Aquitániam proféctus, get mánum suum Domínicum convénit, cum quo nullis térritus perículis, nullis fractus labóribus, eódem supérno Spíritu ductus, omne cóntulit stádium ad bzereticórum. Albigénsium conversiónem. Quam ut secúrus Obtinéret, piis précibus corporísque maceratióne usus est.

RJDICATORUM Ordine institúto, ex primis fuit, qui eúmdem ingréssus est, hábitu de manu ipsíus Fundatóris in convéntu Prulliáno circa annum millésimum — ducentésimum décimum sextum suscépto. Et ita. germánus secúndum carnem, fílius secúndum spíritum, ipsíus sanctitátis verus imitátor efféctus est. Ab eódem sancto Domiínico Parisios cum liis sex ejúsdem Ordinis alámnis missus, ibi conciónes ad pópulum hábuit, ex quibus fructus manárunt ubérrimi. Spíritu lenitátis, pacis ac suavitátis replétus, ómnium ánimos in se convértit, et Przedicatórum Órdinem amplificávit. Quaprópter mérito percélebris ccenóbii sancti Jacóábi tamquam institútor habétur, Parisiénsi convéntu erécto, Matrítum conténdit, ubi a sancto ejus germáno Przeféctus assignátus — sanctimoniálibus ccnóbii de Majorito, quod sancti Domínici póstea nomen hábuit, hoc munus summa zedificatióne adimplévit.

ALAROGAM przedicatiónis causa véniens, postquam diu in Ordine sincéro corde €t pura mente Deo famulátus uerat, innúmeris auctus mériis diem óbit suprémum, circa annum millésimum bis centésimum trigésimum, Ejus corpus apud mónachos Cisterciénses sancti Petri de Gúmiel summo honóre primum prope altáre tumulátum, dein translátum, in majóri altári collocátum fuit cum áliis Sanctórum Relíquiis, ubi étiam nunc cólitur. Plúrima ab eo patráta fuísse prodígia scriptóres testántur : quare sancto Viro, quem doctórem et ducem dum in humánis ágeret, et post mortem patrónum validíssimum expérti fúcrant fidéles, ecclesiástici cultus spécies omnes statim exhibére ccepérunt : quem ad hzc usque témpora propagátum Gregórius Décimus sextus Póntifex Máximus ex sacrórum Rítuum Congregatiónis consúlto approbávit, atque ut in univérso Przedicatórum Ordine de beáto Manne Officium recitári, ac Missa celebrári possit benígne indúlsit.

lessons.la: Grátius natióne Hispanus, nóbilis genere Loyolæ in Cantabria natus, primo catholici regis aulam, deínde milítiam secutus est. In propugnatióne Pampelonénsi accepto vulnere gráviter decumbens, ex fortuita piórum librórum lectióne, ad Christi Sanctorúmque sectanda vestígia mirabíliter exársit. Ad montem Serrátum profectus, ante aram beátæ Vírginis suspénsis armis, noctem éxcubans, sacræ milítiæ tirocinium pósuit. Inde, ut erat indútus sacco, traditis antea mendíco pretiósis vestibus, Manresam secessit; Eo in loco, emendicato pane et aqua víctitans, exceptisque diébus Dominicis, jejunans, aspera catena cilicióque carnem domans, humi cubans, et férreis se flagellis cruentans, per annum commorátus est, claris adeo illustratiónibus a Deo recreatus, ut póstea dicere sólitus sit: Si sacræ Litteræ non exstarent, se tamen pro fide mori parátum ex iis solum, qua sibi Manresæ patefécerat Dóminus. Quo témpore, homo litterárum plane rudis, rábilem illum compósuit exercitiórum librum, Sedis Apo. stólicae judício et ómnium utilitate comprobátum.
lessons.en: Ignatius was a Spaniard by nation, and was born of the noble Biscayan family of Loyola, (in the year of our Lord 1491.) He followed first the Court and then the army of the Most Catholic King. At the siege of Pampeluna (in the year 1521) he received a severe wound which laid him up with a long and dangerous illness. During this time he chanced to read some godly books, and conceived from them a burning desire to follow in the footsteps of Christ and His saints. He betook himself to Monserrat, and there entered himself for the heavenly warfare, by hanging up his weapons, and watching them for a night before the Altar of the Blessed Virgin. Thence he withdrew to Manresa, clad in sackcloth, for he had before given his costly raiment to a beggar. At Manresa he lived upon bread and water, begging the bread, and fasting every day except the Lord's Day. He mastered his flesh by the use of a sharp chain and hair-cloth, slept upon the ground, and lashed himself to bloodshedding with iron scourges. Thus he dwelt for a year, feasted by God with such clear lights, that he was used afterwards to say that even if the Holy Bible had not existed, he would have been ready to die for the faith only on the evidence of those things which the Lord had shown unto him at Manresa. It was at this time that, albeit a man of little education, he put together that wonderful book entitled Spiritual Exercises, whose worth hath been attested by the judgment of the Apostolic See, and by universal usefulness.

lessons.la: U: vero se ad animárum lucra rite formaret, sub. sídium litterárum, a grammi. tica inter púeros exorsus, adhibére státuit. Cumque nihil interim omitteret de studio alienæ salútis, mirum est quas ubíque locórum ærúmnas ac ludibria devoráverit, asperrima quæque, et víncula et verbera pene ad mortem usque perpéssus: quibus tamen longe plura pro Dómini sui glória semper expetebat. Lutetiæ Parisiórum adjunctis sibi ex illa academía variárum natiónum sociis novem, qui omnes artium magistériis et theologíæ gradibus insignes erant, ibidem in monte Mártyrum prima Societátis fundaménta jecit, Romam póstea proféctus, ibídem Órdinem suum constítuens, ad tria consueta quarto addito de Missiónibus voto, Sedi apostolicæ arctius adstrinxit; et Paulus tertius primo recepit confirmavítque, mox alii Pontifices ac Tridentina synodus probavére. Ipse autem, misso ad prædicándum Indis Evangélium sancto Francisco Xaverio, aliisque in alias mundi plagas ad religiónem propagandam disseminatis, éthnicæ superstitióni hæresique bellum indixit; eo successu continuátum, ut constans fúerit ómnium sensus, étiam pontificio confirmátus oraculo, Deum, sicut alios aliis tempóribus sanctos viros, ita Luthé— admi. ro ejusdemque témporis hæreticis Ignatium et institutam ab eo societátem objecisse.
lessons.en: To make himself of greater use for the profit of souls, he determined to improve himself by education, beginning by going through the rudiments among little boys. He left nothing untried that could help towards the salvation of others, and it was marvellous what pain and mockery he cheerfully accepted on all hands, suffering ill-usage also, imprisonment and stripes almost unto death; but he was willing to suffer them all much more for the greater glory of his Master. At Paris he took to him seven comrades from the members of that University, men of different nations, but who had all taken the Degree of Master of Arts and in Divinity. With these seven he laid the first foundations of the Society of Jesus in the crypt at Montmartre, (upon the 15th day of August, in the year of Christ 1534.) When he afterwards organised the same Society at Rome he bound it by the closest bonds to the Apostolic See, adding to the three accustomed vows of Poverty, Chastity, and Obedience, a fourth, concerning Missions. Paul III. was the first Pope to receive and confirm the Institute, but it has since been approved by other Popes and by the Council of Trent. Ignatius, to spread the Faith, sent holy Francis Xavier to preach the Gospel in the Indies, and others in other parts of the world, and the war, which he thus proclaimed against paganism and heresy, was waged with such success, that it was the general belief, confirmed by the utterance of the Pope, that even as God had in other times raised up holy men specially to meet the needs of their day, so He had raised up against Luther and the heretics of that age, Ignatius and the Society which he had founded.

lessons.la: Ep in primis inter Cathóli s cos instaurare pietátem curæ fuit. Templórum nitor, catechismi traditio, conciónum ac sacramentórum frequéntia ab ipso increméntum accepére. Ipse, apertis ubíque locórum ad juventútem erudiéndam in litteris ac pietáte gymnasiis, eréctis Romæ Germanórum collegio, male nuptárum et periclitántium puellárum cœnobiis, utriusque sexus tam orphanórum quam catechumenórum dómibus, aliisque pietátis opéribus, indeféssus lucrandis Deo ánimis instábat; audítus aliquándo dicere, si optio darétur, malle se beatitúdinis incertum vivere, et interim Deo inservire et proximórum saluti, quam certum ejusdem glóriæ statim mori. ln dæmones mirum exercuit impérium. Vultum ejus cælésti luce radiántem sanctus Philippus Nerius aliique conspexere. Denique, ætátis anno sexagesimo quinto, ad Dómini sui amplexum, cujus majórem glóriam in ore semper habúerat, semper in ómnibus quæsíerat, emigrávit. lessons.la: M Heródes rex manus, ut afflígeret quosdam de Ecclésia. Occídit autem Jacóbum fratrem Joánnis gládio. Videns autem quia placéret Judǽis, appósuit ut apprehénderet et Petrum. Erant autem dies Azymórum. Quem cum apprehendísset, misit in cárcerem, tradens quátuor quaterniónibus mílitum custodiéndum, volens post Pascha prodúcere eum pópulo. Et Petrus quidem servabátur in cárcere. Orátio autem fiébat sine intermissióne ab Ecclésia ad Deum pro eo.
lessons.en: And at the same time, Herod the king stretched forth his hands, to afflict some of the church. And he killed James, the brother of John, with the sword. And seeing that it pleased the Jews, he proceeded to take up Peter also. Now it was in the days of the Azymes. And when he had apprehended him, he cast him into prison, delivering him to four files of soldiers to be kept, intending, after the pasch, to bring him forth to the people. Peter therefore was kept in prison. But prayer was made without ceasing by the church unto God for him.

lessons.la: Ce Autem productúrus eum esset Heródes, in ipsa no. duos mílites, vinctus caténis duábus: et custódes ante óstium custodiébant cárcerem. Et ecce ángelus Dómini ástitit, et lumen refúlsit in habitáculo: percussóque látere Petri, excitávit eum, dicens: caténæ de mánibus ejus. Dixit autem ángelus ad eum: Præcíngere, et cálcea te cáligas tuas. Et fecit sic. Et dixit illi: Circúmda tibi vestiméntum tuum, et séquere me. E. ii Si díligis me Simon Petre, pasce oves meas. Démine tu nosti quia amo te * et ánimam meam pono pro te. Si oportúerit me mori tecum, non te negábo. — Et ánimam meam pono pro te.

Transeúntes autem primam et secúndam custódiam, venérunt ad portam férream, quæ ducit ad civitátem: que ultro apérta est eis. Et exeúntes processérunt vicum unum: et contínuo discéssit ángelus ab eo. And passing through the first and the second ward, they came to the iron gate that leadeth to the city, which of itself opened to them. And going out, they passed on through one street: and immediately the angel departed from him. And Peter coming to himself, said: Now I know in very deed, that the Lord hath sent his angel, and hath delivered me out of the hand of Herod, and from all the expectation of the people of the Jews.

lessons.la: Um ígitur Póntifex Románam caténam cum ea, quæ Jerosólymis alláta fúerat, contulísset, factum est ut illæ inter se sic connecteréntur, ut non duæ, sed una caténa ab eódem artífice confécta esse viderétur. Quo miráculo tantus honor sacris illis vínculis habéri cœpit, ut proptérea hoc nómine sancti Petri ad víncula ecclésia, título Eudóxiæ, dedicáta sit in Exquíliis, ejúsque memóriæ dies festus institútus Kaléndis Augústi.
lessons.en: When then the Pope put together the Roman chain and that which had been brought from Jerusalem, it came to pass that they got so entangled the one with the other that they seemed no longer two but one chain. From this wonder these holy fetters began to receive such honour, that Eudoxia's Church of St. Peter on the Esquiline Mount was dedicated under the name of St. Peter in Chains, and a Feast - Day instituted upon the first day of August in memory of it.

lessons.la: UO ex témpore honos, qui eo die profánis Gentílium celebritátibus — tríbui — sólitus erat, Petri vínculis habéri cœpit, qua tacta ægros sanábant et dǽmones ejiciébant. Quo in génere, anno salútis humánæ nongentésimo saxa ésimo nono áccidit, ut quidam comes, Othónis imperatóris familiáris, occupátus ab immúndo spíritu, seípsum déntibus dilaniáret. Quare is jussu imperatóris ad Joánnem Pontíficem dúcitur, qui ut sacra caténa cómitis collum áttigit, erúmpens nefárius spíritus hóminem líberum relíquit; ac deínceps in Urbe sanctórum vinculórum relígio propagáta est.
lessons.en: From that time forth the honour which before had used to be paid to the profane festivity of the Gentiles, (held in memory of the dedication of the temple of Mars, and of the birth of Claudius,) began to be turned to the Chains of Peter, whose very touch healed the sick, and drove out devils. Among other such cases there befell in the year of man's Redemption 969, that of a certain Count, a servant of the Emperor Otho, who was possessed by an unclean spirit, and tore himself with his own teeth. This man the Emperor ordered to be taken to Pope John, and as soon as he had touched the Count's neck with the hallowed chains, the foul spirit came out of him, and left him free. And thenceforward the reverence for these holy chains greatly increased in the City.

lessons.la: Cap. l, Omne stultam fecit Deus sapiéntiam hujus mundi? Nam quia in Dei sapiéntia non cognóvit mundus per sapiéntiam Deum: plácuit Deo per stultítiam prædicatiónis salvos fácere credéntes. Quóniam et Judǽi signa petunt, et Græci sapiéntiam quærunt: nos autem prædicámus Christum cru cifíxum: Judǽis quidem scándalum, géntibus autem stultítiam, ipsis autem vocátis Judǽis, atque Græcis, Christum Dei virtútem, et Dei sapiéntiam: quia quod stultum est Dei, sapiéntius est homínibus: et quod infírmum est Dei, fórtius est homínibus.
lessons.en: Where is the wise? Where is the scribe? Where is the disputer of this world? Hath not God made foolish the wisdom of this world? For seeing that in the wisdom of God the world, by wisdom, knew not God, it pleased God, by the foolishness of our preaching, to save them that believe. For both the Jews require signs, and the Greeks seek after wisdom: But we preach Christ crucified, unto the Jews indeed a stumblingblock, and unto the Gentiles foolishness: But unto them that are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God. For the foolishness of God is wiser than men; and the weakness of God is stronger than men.

lessons.la: Cap. Agéntes administratiónem, juxta quod misericórdiam consecúti sumus, non defícimus, sed abdicámus occúlta dedécoris, non ambulántes in astútia, neque adulterántes verbum Dei, sed in manifestatióne veritátis commendántes nosmetípsos ad omnem consciéntiam hóminum coram Deo. Quod si étiam opértum est Evangélium nostrum: in iis, qui péreunt, est opértum: in quibus Deus hujus sǽculi excæcávit mentes infidélium, ut non fúlgeat illis illuminátio Evangélii glóriæ Christi, qui est imágo Dei.
lessons.en: Therefore, seeing we have this ministration, according as we have obtained mercy, we faint not; But we renounce the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor adulterating the word of God; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man’s conscience, in the sight of God. And if our gospel be also hid, it is hid to them that are lost, In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of unbelievers, that the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God, should not shine unto them.

lessons.la: On enim nosmetípsos przeNem sed Jesum Christum Dóminum nostrum: nos autem servos vestros per Jesum: quóniam Deus, qui dixit de ténebris lucem splendéscere, ipse illúxit in córdibus nostris ad illuminatiónem sciéntiæ claritátis Dei, in fácie Christi Jesu. Habémus autem thesáurum istum in vasis fictílibus: ut sublímitas sit virtútis Dei, et non ex nobis. In ómnibus tribulatiónem pátimur, sed non angustiámur: aporiámur, sed non destitúimur: persecutiónem pátimur, sed non derelínquimur: dejícimur, sed non perímus: semper mortificatiónem Jesu in córpore nostro circumferéntes, ut et vita Jesu manifestétur in corpóribus nostris.
lessons.en: For we preach not ourselves, but Jesus Christ our Lord; and ourselves your servants through Jesus. For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God, in the face of Christ Jesus. But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency may be of the power of God, and not of us. In all things we suffer tribulation, but are not distressed; we are straitened, but are not destitute; We suffer persecution, but are not forsaken; we are cast down, but we perish not: Always bearing about in our body the mortification of Jesus, that the life also of Jesus may be made manifest in our bodies.

Itaque, si sal infatuátum fúerit, in quo saliétur? Id est, si vos, per quos condiéndi sunt quodámmodo pópuli, metu persecutiónum — temporálium amiséritis regna cælórum; qui erunt hómines, per quos a vobis error auferátur, cum vos elégerit Deus, per quos errórem áuferat ceterórum? Ek. vii Felix vitis, de cujus súrculo tantum germen redúndat sǽculo, * Cæli vinum proinans pópulo vitáli póculo. Ex ubertáte pálmitum mundi. jam cinxit áóbitum. — Celi vinum.

RGO ad níhilum valet sal infatuátum, nisi ut mittátur foras et conculcétur ab homínibus. Non ítaque calcátur ab homínibus qui pátitur persecutiónem; sed qui, persecutiónem timéndo, infatuátur. Calcári enim non potest nisi inférior; sed inférior non est, qui, quamvis córpore multa in terra sustíneat, corde tamen fixus in cælo est. lessons.la: Liberio summo Pontifice, Joánnes patricius Romanus et uxor pari nobilitate, cum liberos non suscepíssent, quos bonórum herédes relínquerent, suam hereditátem sanctíssimæ Virgini Dei Matri vovérunt, ab ea summis precibus assidue peténtes, ut in quod pium opus eam pecúniam potíssimum erogari vellet áli. quo modo significaret. Quorum preces et vota, ex animo facta, beáta Virgo Maria, benígne áudiens, miraculo comprobávit.
lessons.en: In the time of Pope Liberius, there lived at Rome a certain nobleman named John and a noble lady his wife, who had no children to whom to leave their substance. Then they vowed that they would make the most holy Virgin Mother of God their heiress, and earnestly besought her in some way to make known to them upon what godly work she would that the money should be spent. The Blessed Virgin Mary graciously listened to their prayers and heart-felt earnestness, and by a miracle assured them of her will.

lessons.la: UARE solemni sacerdotum et pópuli supplicatióne ad collem venit nive coopertum, et in eo locum ecclésiæ signávit, qua Joánnis et uxórb ejus pecúnia exstructa est, póstea a Xysto tertio restituta. Variis nomínibus primum es! appellata, basilica Liberii, sancta Maria ad Præsepe; sed, cum multæ jam essent in Urbe ecclésiæ sub nómine sanctæ Maríæ Vírginis, ut basilica ne novitate miraculi ac dignitate ceteris ejusdem nóminis basilicis præstaret, vocabuli étiam excelléntia significarétur, ecclésia sancte Maríæ majoris dicta est. Cujus dedicatiónis memória ex nive, quæ hac die mirabíliter cécidit, anniversaria celebritate cólitur.
lessons.en: Therefore he came in a solemn procession of Priests and people to the snow-clad hill, and traced upon that spot the plan of a Church which was built with the money of John and his wife. It was afterwards rebuilt by Sixtus III. At the beginning it was called by diverse names, sometimes the Liberian Basilica, sometimes the Church of St. Mary-at-the-Manger. Howbeit, since there are in Rome many Churches called after the Holy Virgin Mary, and this Church doth excel them all, both in honour, and because of the strange sign wherewith it was dedicated, it hath come to be called the Church of St. Mary, the Greater. The memory of the dedication thereof is kept every year by a Feast-day that taketh name from the wonderful fall of snow which on this day took place.

lessons.la: RATRES, magis satágite ut per bona ópera certam vestram vocatiónem, et electiónem faciátis: hæc enim faciéntes, non peccábitis aliquándo. Sic enim abundánter ministrábitur vobis intróitus in ætérnum regnum Dómini nostri, et Salvatóris Jesu Christi. Propter quod incípiam vos semper commonére dc his: et quidem sciéntes et confirmátos vos in præsénti veritáte. Justum autem árbitror quámdiu sum in hoc tabernáculo, suscitáre vos in commonitióne: certus quod velox est deposítio tabernáculi mei secúndum quod et Dóminus noster Jesus Christus significávit mihi.
lessons.en: Wherefore, brethren, labour the more, that by good works you may make sure your calling and election. For doing these things, you shall not sin at any time. For so an entrance shall be ministered to you abundantly into the everlasting kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. For which cause I will begin to put you always in remembrance of these things: though indeed you know them, and are confirmed in the present truth. But I think it meet as long as I am in this tabernacle, to stir you up by putting you in remembrance. Being assured that the laying away of this my tabernacle is at hand, according as our Lord Jesus Christ also hath signified to me.

lessons.la: Du Autem óperam et frequénter habére vos post óbitum meum, ut horum memóriam faciátis. Non enim doctas fábulas secúti notam fécimus vobis Dómini nostri Jesu Christi virtútem, et præséntiam: sed speculatóres facti illíus magnitúdinis. Accípiens enim a Deo Patre honórem, et glóriam, voce delápsa ad eum hujuscémodi a magnífica glória: Hic est Fílius meus diléctus, in quo mihi complácui, ipsum audíte.
lessons.en: And I will endeavour, that you frequently have after my decease, whereby you may keep a memory of these things. For we have not by following artificial fables, made known to you the power, and presence of our Lord Jesus Christ; but we were eyewitnesses of his greatness. For he received from God the Father, honour and glory: this voice coming down to him from the excellent glory: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.

lessons.la: premit Dóminus coram eléctis téstibus glóriam suam, r et commúnem illam cum céteris córporis formam tanto splendóre claríficat, ut et fácies ejus solis fulgóri símilis, et vestítus candóri nívium esset æquális. In qua transfiguratióne illud quidem principáliter agebátur, ut de córdibus discipulórum crucis scándalum tollerétur; nec conturbáret eórum fidem voluntáriæ humílitas passiónis, quibus reveláta esset abscónditæ excelléntia dignitátis. Sed non minóre providéntia spes sanctæ Ecclésiæ fundabátur, ut totum Christi corpus agnósceret quali esset commutatióne donándum, ut ejus sibi honóris consórtium membra promítterent, qui in cápite præfulsísset.
lessons.en: From the Sermons of Pope St. Leo (the Great) The Lord taketh chosen witnesses, and in their presence, revealeth His glory. That form of body which He had in common with other men, He so transfigured with light, that His Face did shine as the sun, and His raiment became exceeding white as snow. Of this metamorphosis the chief work was to remove from the hearts of the disciples the stumbling at the Cross. Before their eyes was unveiled the splendour of His hidden majesty, that the lowliness of His freely-chosen suffering might not confound their faith. But none the less was there here laid by the Providence of God a solid foundation for the hope of the Holy Church, whereby the whole body of Christ should know with what a change it is yet to be honoured. The members of that body whose Head hath already been transfigured in light may promise themselves a share in His glory.

lessons.la: Cajetánus, nóbili Thienæa gente Vicéntiæ ortus, statim a matre Deíparæ Vírgini oblátus est. Mira a téneris annis morum innocéntia in eo eluxit, adeo ut Sanctus ab ómnibus nuncuparétur. Juris utrísque láuream Patavii adéptus, Romam proféctus est; ubi, inter prælátos a Júlio secúndo collocátus, et Sacerds. tio initiátus, tanto divini amoris stu succénsus est, relícta aula se totum Deo mancipaverit. Nosocomíis próprio ere fundátis, étiam morbo pestilénti laborántibus, suis ipse mánibus inserviébat. Pro. ximórum salúti assidua cura incumbébat, dictus proptérea Venátor animárum.
lessons.en: Cajetan was born at Vicenza, (in the year 1480,) of the noble family of the lords of Tiene, and was forthwith dedicated by his mother to the Virgin Mother of God. From his childhood such wonderful innocence shone in him that all called him the Saint. He took the degree of Doctor in Civil and Canon Law at Padua, and afterwards went to Rome, where Julius II. gave him a place among the Prelates. Having taken Priest's Orders, he became so full of the fire of the love of God, that he left the Court, that he might be free to work entirely for God. He founded hospitals at his own expense, and nursed the sick, even such as were suffering from the plague, with his own hands. He laboured with such constant earnestness for the salvation of his neighbours that he got the name of the Hunter of souls.

lessons.la: Collapsam ecclesiasticórum disciplínam ad for. mam Apostólicæ vitæ instaurare desiderans, ordinem le. ricórum regulárium instituit, qui, abdicáta rerum ómnium terrenárum sollicitúdine, nec réditus possiderent nec vitæ subsidia a fidelibus péterent, sed solis eleemosynis sponte oblátis víverent. Itaque, approbante Cleménte septimo, ad aram maximam basilicæ Vaticanæ una cum Joánne Petro Caráfa, episcopo Theatino, qui póstea Paulus quartus Pontifex maximus fuit, et aliis duobus exímiæ pietátis viris, vota solemnia emisit. In Urbis direptióne a milítibus crudelíssime vexátus ut pecúniam próderet, quam dudum in cælestes thesáuros manus páuperum deportaverant, verbera, torménta et carceres invicta patiéntia sustinuit. n suscepto vitæ instituto constantíssime perseverávit, soli divinæ providéntiæ inhærens, quam sibi nunquam de fuísse aliquándo miracula com probárunt.

D Vini cultus studium, nit rem domus Dei, sacrórum rituum observantiam et san ctíssimae Eucharfstize frequenúórem usum maxime promovit. Hæresum monstra et látebras non semel detéxit ac profligávit. Oratiónem ad octo passim horas jugibus lácrimis protrahebat: sæpe in éxtasim raptus ac prophétis dono illustris Romæ, nocte Natalítia ad præsepe Dómini infántem Jesum accípere meruit a Deípara in ulnas suas. Corpus íntegras noctes intérdum verberatiónibus affligebat; nec unquam adduci pótuit ut vitæ asperitátem emolliret, testátus in cínere et cilício velle se mori. Dénique, ex animi dolóre concepto morbo, quod offéndi plebis seditióne Deum vidéret, cælésti visióne recreatus, Neapoli migrávit in cælum; ibique corpus ejus in ecclésia sancti Pauli magna religióne cólitur. Quem, multis miraculis in vita et post mortem gloriosum, Clemens décimus, Pontifex maximus, Sanctórum número adscripsit.
lessons.en: He was a great advancer of care in the worship of God, of splendour in the house of God, of exactness in the holy ceremonies, and of the often receiving of the most holy Eucharist. The hideous forms and dark convolutions of heresy he more than once unmasked and abolished. He would remain in prayer with abundance of tears as much as eight hours at a time. He was often thrown into trances, and was celebrated for the gift of prophecy. One Christmas night at Rome, when he was praying before the Lord's manger, he was deemed worthy that the Mother of God should lay the Child Jesus in his arms. He sometimes spent the whole night in whipping himself, nor could he ever be persuaded to soften the hardness of his life, but witnessed that he was fain to die in sackcloth and ashes. In the end he fell ill with grief at the offence against God, which the people of Naples committed by rebelling (against the establishment of the Inquisition.) Refreshed by a vision from heaven, he departed thither (on the 7th day of August, 1547.) His body lieth at Naples in the Church of St. Paul, where it is held in great reverence. Pope Clement X., finding him to have been illustrious for miracles, both during his life and after his death, enrolled his name among those of the Saints.

lessons.la: UGUSTINUS Tragúrii in Dalmátia, sub Spalaténsi Archiepiscopátu, paréntibus nobilitáte, ac orthodóxze Fídei pietáte illústribus, natus est. Adoléscens, ut totum se Deo mancipáret, szeculári património dimísso, sacræ Preedicatórum famílie nomen dedit : ibíque in sectándis sancti Domínici, quem sibi patrem elégerat, vestígiis ádeo incúbuit, ut adhuc júvenis tamquam reguláris observántize exémplar ómnibus proponerétur. Exácto úrocinio, Parísios una cum fratre. Jacóbo Ursini studiórum causa missus, sanctum Thomam Aquinátem magístrum hábuit :Sub quo miruy est quantum in quer pie táte ceterísque virtútibus ue. fécerit. Pre.

Ip pátriam revérsus, Superig. rum jussu przedicatióni di. víni verbi addíctus est. Máximo interim salátis animárum st. dio inardéscens, nihil unquam omísit, quo infidéles ad fidem peccatóres ad poeniténtiam revocáret. In oratióne as. Quus, cui incúmbens plures noctes ducébat insómnes, illud sancti Doctóris Augustíni frequénter usurpábat: Recte novit vívere, qui recte novit oráre. Ne vero sub módio, virtútum cjus lucérna delitésceret, a Benedícto Undécimo ad Zagabriénsem Episcopátum promótus fuit. Quo in múnere, humilitátis, patiéntiae, misericórdiz erga páuperes laude, et przecípue indeféssis in custodiéndo grege sibi commísso labóribus ádeo enítuit, ut Robértus rex Neápolis, audíta ejus fama, summis précibus a Joánne Vigésimo secúndo impetrárit pastórem illum przefici Ecckésie Lucerínze, ut eam a Saracenórum erróribus, quibus infécta fúerat, expurgáret.

D Lucerinam Ecclésiam proféctus, novæ sponse sue máculas a Saracenórum labe expurgatúrus, mirum quas zerúmnas, quos labóres. perpéssus sit : donec oratiónis fervóre, przedicatiónis efficácia, morum sanctitáte, univérsum ovíle suum, cathólicum vidére merúerit. Utque illud a quólibet futúro inquinaménto sefváret immúne, Deíparæ Vírginis poténti patrocínio submisit totaih dioecésim, ac præcípue urbem Luceríinam, quam, mutáto nómine, civitátem sanctæ Maríe appellári vóluit : qua nomenclatúra nostris étiam tempéribus dicta cívitas decorátur. Tandem méritis plenus, et miraculórum fama illústris, ánimam réddidit Creatóri, die tértia Augústi circa annum Salútis millésimum — trecentésimum vigésimum tértium, cetátis vero suze septuagésimum : cujus corpus in ecclésia, quam suo Ordini zedificáverat, hononce cónditum, tot prodígiis a Deo insignítum ferunt, ut paucis post ejus óbitum annis, Cárolus dux Calábrize súpplices déderit lítteras Joánni Vigésimo secúndo Pontífici Máximo, ut Augustínum Beatórum fastis adscribere dignarétur. Clemens vero Undécimus, ut in toto Preedicatórum Ordine ejus festum cum Offício et Missa de Communi uníus Confessóris Pontíficis celebrarétur benígne concéssit.

Ipso duce et magístro, tantum in sémita virtútis et religiósze perfectiónis profécit, ut missis ab eódem sancto Fundatóre ad propagándum per Etrúriam Órdinem duódecim probatíssimis viris, Joánnem, etsi junióris actátis tunc fuísse mérito cónjicí possit, przefécerit. Sanctíssimi Patris przecéptis obtémperans, cum sóciis conténdit Floréntiam versus : ac Rípulis, tértio ferme ab ea lápide, primum cónstitit in domo, a pio cive Florentinoillisparáta,prope sacéllum, quod éxstrui is ipse curáverat. [nde Virsanctus quotídie in urbem véniens, jugi verbi Dei przedicatióne ac morum innocéntia arctíssime sibi devínxit ánimos Florentinórum, PRJAED. l p o— e qui pérditos in viam salútis redíre, réliquos autem in bono confírmari illíus hortaméntis atque mónitis perspiciébant. Verum qui rem civitátis públicam tunc moderabántur, animadverténtes incómmodum eídem esse quod síngulis diébus summo mane Floréntiam pérgere, et véspere ad hospítium Ripulitánum remeáre debéret, de loco, in quo intra urbis incdenia una cum ' sóciis dégere posset, ei providéndo cogitárunt. Ítaque primum ad sancti Pancrátii, dein ad sancti Pauli, ac demum ad sanctz? Maríze Novélle seu Vineárum, rite fuit eis domicílium; constitútum.

It in loco piórum largitiónibus sacra zede amplificáta, constructóque ccenóbio, novi Przedicatóres Florénti; vívere coepérunt arctióri legum sui Ordinis observántia, Exémplo suo cunctis Joánnes preíbat. Assídua cibt potiúsque abstinéntia, despiciéntia et castigatióne sui, quotidiáno oratiónis stúdio, rerum divinárum contemplatióne, quam ad plures horas (noctu przesértim) ducébat, fervénti devotióne, ac czremoniárum —observatióne diligentíssima dum Sacris operarétur, ceterísque virtútibus, qua: hóminem cumprimis decent aliórum regímini przeféctum, ad sui imitatiónem atque puriórem reguláris disciplínæ cultum sodáles magnópere excitábat. Córporis animique cástitas potíssimum in eo excélluit : qua sane quantum przestáret, miro prorsus modo Deus vóluit esse perspícuum. Síquidem cum ab impudica mulíere frustra tentátus, relátam de immúndo spíritu ab se victóriam Singulári humilitáte celáre niterétur, dæmon ipse, Deo ita jubénte, per os energúmeni rem totam palam fecit, ne. ns se líberum hóminem aliquándo dimissúrum, nisi is, qui inter flammas innóxius permánse. rat, se inde expélleret; vocató. que Dei Fámulo, ad ipsíus nutum, ægrum multum discérpens, íllico discéssit, His alifs. que ab eo przecláre gestis, erá. tia quoque curatiónum, qua ferunt a Deo fuísse donátum, factum est ut plures pietáte, nobilitáte géneris, doctrínze fama ecclesiasticisque dignittibus fulgéntes viri ab illo in Órdinem récipi postulárent, reque ipsa fúerint recépti: quos inter unus sánguine christiánam fidem sancívit, duo autem conspícuis fuérunt deínde Itálize Ecclésiis przepósiti.

[Astánte Óbitu sancti Domínici, Bonóniam perréxit, ut Parénti óprimo fílii obsequéntis atque amantíssimi extréma exhibéret offícia. Floréntiam inde redux, in hzréticos Patarénos, exitiálem Manichzeórum sóbolem, Ecclésie &que ac reipúblicze statum perturbántes, cum id a Gregório Nono Románo Pontífice ipsi fuísset demandátum, insúrgens, córum audáciam fregit, atque contuméliis ac probris, quibus illum ab incépto deterrére conabántur, fórtiter tolerátis, cathólicam fidem egrégie tutátus est, Ejúsdem Pontíficis jussu opus reformatiónis apud mónachos sancti Anthími Clusing dicecésis strénue promóvit. In zedibus Ripulárum, ubi primo suo in Etrúriam advéntu conséderat, sacrárum vírginum collégium instítuit sub sui Ordinis régula. Innúmeris demum pro Eccksie bono fideíque increménto perfúnctum labóribus, post administrátam ad plures annos ingénti cum suórum, tum cívium proÍéctu ccenóbii sanctæ Maríæ Novélle praefectúram, dies úlima excépit : quam letus aspéxit, fratrésque, quos dénuo óbitu ántia monúerat, ad vitze sanctimóniam atque ad vota sua Deo fidéliter reddénda cohortátus, Sacris Ecclésize expiátus, Sanctíssime excéssit, Ad ejus sepúlcrum frequens ccpit fíeri concúrsus populórum, illíus opem implorántium, seque eam adéptos profiténtium, ac eídem cultum deferéntium Beatórum. head: Cap. 5r.
lessons.la: ONFITEBOR tibi Dómine rex, et collaudábo te Deum salvatórem meum. Confitébor nómini tuo: quóniam ódii et protéctor factus es miti liberásti corpus meum a per. ditióne, a láqueo linguæ iníqua, et a lábiis operántium mendácium, et in conspéctu astántium factus es mihi adjútor. Et liberásti me secúndum multitúdinem misericórdia: nóminis tui a rugiéntibus, præ. parátis ad escam, de mánibus quæréntium ánimam meam, et de portis tribulatiónum quæ circumdedérunt me: a pressúra flammæ, quæ circúmdedit me, et in médio ignis non sum æstuátus: de altitúdine ventris ínferi, et a lingua coinquináta, et a verbo mendácii, a rege iníquo, et a lingua injústa: i Levíta Lauréntius bonum opus operátus est qui per signum Crucis cæcos illuminávit, * Et thesáuros Ecclésim dedit paupéribus. Dispérsit, dedit paupéribus justítia ejus manet in sǽculum séculi. — Et thesáuros Ecclésiæ.

Laudábit usque ad mortem ánima mea Dóminum, t vita mea appropínquans erat in inférno deórsum. Circumdedérunt me úndique, et non erat qui adjuváret. Respíciens eram ad adjutórium hóminum, et non erat. Memorátus sunt misericórdiæ tuæ Dómine, et operatiónis tuæ, quæ a sǽculo sunt: quóniam éruis sustinéntes te Dómine, et líberas eos de mánibus géntium. — H. ii Quo progréderis sine fílio pater? quo Sacérdos sam cte sine diácono próperas? * Tu nunquam sine minístro Sacri ficium offérre consuéverns. Quid in me ergo displícuit aternitáti tuæ? numquid decérem me probásti? Experire certe utrum idóneum minístrum clégeris, cui commisísti Domínici sánguinis dispensatiónem. — Tu nunquam.

Exaltásti super terram habitatiónem meam, et pro morte defluénte deprecátus sum. Invocávi Dóminum patrem Dómini mei, ut non derelínquat me in die tribulatiónis mec, et in témpore superbórum sine adjutório. Laudábo nomen tuum assídue, et collaudábo illud in confessióne, et exaudíta est orátio mea. Et liberásti me de perditióne, et eripuísti me de témpore iníquo. Proptérea confitébor, et laudem dicam tibi, et benedícam nómini Dómini. R. iii Noli me derelínquere, pater sancte, quia thesáuros tuos jam expéndi. * Non ego te désero fili, neque derelin quo: Sed majóra tibi debéntur pro fide Christi certámina. Nos quasi senes levióris Pugna cursum recípimus; te autem quasi júvenem manet gloriósior de tyránno triúmphus: post tríduum me sequérís Sacerdótem Levíta, — Non tgo te désero fili, Glória. Sed majóra tibi.

Beatissimi Laurentii Martyris, cujus natalem hodie celebramus, passionem nosse vos credo: et quanta in persecutione pertulerit, dilectionem vestram scire posse non dubito. Tanta enim ejus martyrii gloria exstitit, ut passione sua mundum illuminaverit universum. Illuminavit plane mundum Laurentius eo lumine, quo ipse accensus est, et flammis quas ipse pertulit, omnium Christianorum corda calefecit. Quis nolit ad horam uri Laurentii igne, ut æternum gehénna non patiatur incendium?

resp.a: Beátus Lauréntius clamávit et dixit: Deum meum colo, et ipsi soli sérvio;
resp.b: Et ídeo non tímeo torménta tua.
v: Mea nox obscúrum non habet, sed ómnia in luce claréscunt.

lessons.la: EATI igitur Laurentii exémB plo provocamur ad martyrium, accendimur ad fidem, incalescimus ad devotionem: et si nobis persecutoris flamma deest, fidei tamen flamma non deest. Non ardemus quidem corpore pro Christo, sed ardemus affectu: non subjicit mihi persecutor ignem: sed suggerit mihi ignem desiderium Salvatoris. Quo igne succensi illi duo discipuli dixerunt: Nonne cor nostrum ardens erat in nobis, dum loqueretur in via, et aperiret nobis Scripturas? HR. w. Strinxérunt córporis membra pósita in cratícula subjiciéntibus prunas insúltat Levíta Christi. * Beáte Laurénti, Martyr Christi, intercéde pro nobis. Carnífices vero urgéntes ministrábant carbónes subter cratem férream, — Beáte Laurénti. Il igitur igne beatus Laull réntius accensus, flammarum non sentit incéndia: et dum Christi ardet desiderio, persecutoris pœnam non sentit. In quantum enim In illo fídei ardor fervet, in tantum supplícii flamma frigéscit. Corporáli enim beátus Lauréntius labórat incéndio sed divínus Salvatóris ardor materiálem tyránni restiínxit ardórem. Quamvis enim in favíllam membra Solvántur, fídei tamen fortitúdo non sólvitur. Córporis quidem detriméntum sústinet, sed lucrum salútis acquirit.

resp.b: In odórem suavitátis.

lessons.la: Se Dóminus Jesus erat graL num mortificándum et multiplicándum; mortificándum infidelitate Judæórum, multiplicándum fide populórum. Jam vero exhortans nos ad passiónis suc sectanda vestígia, Qui amat, inquit, ánimam suam, perdet eam. Quod duobus modis potest. intélligi Qui amat, perdet; id est, si amas, perdes. Si cupis vitam tenére cum Christo, noli mortem timére pro Christo. Item alio modo: Qui amat ánimam suam, perdet eam; noli amare, ne perdas; noli amare in hac vita, ne perdas in æterna vita.

resp.b: Te Dóminum Jesum Christum — conféssus ^ sum.

lessons.la: H autem, quod posterius dixi, magis vidétur habére evangélicus sensus; séquitur enim: Et qui odit ánimam suam in hoc mundo, in vitam ætérnam custódit eam. Er N quod supra dictum est, Qui amat, subintellígitur n hoc mundo, ipse útique perdet; c qui eam odit, útique in hoc mundo, in vitam ætérnam ipse custódit eam. Magna et mira senténtia, quemádmodum sit hóminis n ánimam suam amor ut pereat, ódium nme pereat. Si male amáveris, tunc odísti; si bene óderis, tunc amásti. NK. viii Gáudeo plane, quia hóstia Christi éffici mérui: accusátus non negávi nomen sanctum ejus, interrogátus Christum conféssus sum, * Assátus grátias ago. Ego me óhtuli sacrifícium Deo in odórem suavitátis. — Assátus grátias ago.

Um ergo cause articulus venerit, ut hæc conditio proponatur, aut faciendum esse contra Dei præceptum, aut ex hac vita emigrandum; quorum duorum homo si cogatur álte! rum eligere, comminante mortem persecutore, ibi eligat Deo dilecto emori, quam offenso vivere. Ibi oderit in hoc mundo animam suam, ut in vitam ætérnam custodiat eam. —

Imminéntem ígitur tránsitum divína revelatióne cognóvit. Oránti enim et amóre divinórum ardéntius sstuánti ástitit pulchérrimus júvenls, humána spécie major, his eum verbis aHocútus : Veni dilécte, et in vera gáudia ingrédere.

Et cum vix prze lassitúdine membra subsisterent, incredíbili tamen devotiónis ardóre succénsus, in ecclésia totam noctem orans de more consúnmpsit, ac matutínis étiam précibus cum Frátribus intérfuit, Quibus finítis, gravi cápitis dolóre afféctus, in febrem íscidit, ex qua procul dúbio se moritúárum intelléxit. Rara fuit ejus in extrémo morbo patiéntia : nam fébribus extústus, semper vultu hilari ac jucóndo erat.

Dein accitis duódecim ex senióribus et przstantióribus Frátribus, Prióri convéntus Bononiénsis generáliter ómnia peccáta conféssus est, exomologesíque sacro ritu perácta, illts astántibus dixit : En, Fratres caríssimi, in hanc usque horam illibita mihi virgínitas singulári Dei múnere cónstitit : quam si vos étiam persáncte coluéritis, et vitze munditia et odóre claræ famæ mirum in modum in pópulis promovebímini.

In cujus oratióne ea vox audíta est: Ego vos semper custódiam. Saracéni autem partim se fugas mandárunt, partim, qui murum ascénderant, capti óculis, præcípites cecidérunt.

psA Virgo paulo post jejuI niis, oratiónibus vigiliisque confécta, cum duos et quadragínta annos summa cum laude monastérium gubernássel, múltaque edidísset mirácula; prídie Idus Augústi, sacra Eucharístia sumpta, ánimam Deoréddidit, Innocéntio Quarto Summo Pontífice : qui zegrotántem Vírginem invísit, eíque supplíciter peténti indulgéntiam peccatórum impertívit, Quam póstea Alexánder Quarum inter sanctas Vírgines rétulit.

Ip festo Vírginis preedicánda est virgínitas. Hoc in isto sermóne suscépimus. Ádjuvet Christus Vírginis Fílius, et Vírginum Sponsus : virgináli útero corporáliter natus, virZináli connúbio spirituáliter conjugátus. Cum ígitur univérsa Ecclésia virgo sit, sicut dicit Apóstolus, quanto digna sunt honóre membra, quse hæc tustódiunt étiam in ipsa carne, Qquize ipsa tota custódit in fide! Nulla ergo fecúnditas carnis sancte virginitáti, étiam carnis, comparári potest.

lessons.la: Hippolytus, a sancto Lauréntio baptizatus, domi sua, dum Eucharistiam sumeret, comprehénsus, et ad Valerianum imperatórem adductus, ab eo de suæ religiónis professióne interrogátus, líbere se Christianum proféssus est. Quam ob rem fustibus cæditur; quibus in verbéribus cum ejus fides constantior invenirétur, munéribus et honórum promissis tentátur. Quæ cum ómnia frustra diceréntur, præfecto occidendus traditur.

Qu domum Hippolyti veniens, ut ejus facultates publicaret, totam familiam christianam esse cognoscit; atque, iis a christiana fide frustra deterritis, primum plumbátis cæsa Concordia, Hippolyti nutríce, quæ ceteros confirmábat, réliquos extra portam Tiburtinam occídi jubet. Hippolytus, indómitis equis raptátus per loca tríbulis et cárduis cónsita, lacerato corpore, spíritum Deo réddidit, unáque cum réliquis a Justino presbytero ad agrum Veranum sepúltus est.

Ed cum idem Justínus corem Concórdim — inveníre non posset, miles quidam Porphýrius rogávit Irenæum cloacárium, ut corpus Concórdize in cloácam projéctum extráheret, Sperábat enim aurum et gemmas se in véstibus ejus repertúrum. Extrácto córpore, cum nihil miles reperísset eórum quæ putáverat, aufúgit. Irenæus vero, vocáto ad se Abúndio Christiáno, ambo corpus sanctæ Concórdiz ad Justínum Presbýterum detulérunt, quod ille juxta Hippólytum Sociósque sepelívit.

lessons.la: Et cap. w E est ista, quæ ascéndit per desértum sicut vírgula fumi ex aromátibus myrrhæ, et thuris, et univérsi púlveris pigmentárii? Quam pulchra es amíca mea, quam pulchra es! Oculi tui columbárum, absque ó, quod intrínsecus latet. Capílli tui sicut greges caprárum, quæ ascendérunt de monte Gálaad. Dentes tui sicut greges tonsárum, quæ ascendérunt de lavácro: omnes geméllis fétibus, et stérilis non est inter eas.
lessons.en: When I had a little passed by them, I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him: and I will not let him go, till I bring him into my mother’s house, and into the chamber of her that bore me. Who is she that goeth up by the desert, as a pillar of smoke of aromatical spices, of myrrh, and frankincense, and of all the powders of the perfumer? How beautiful art thou, my love, how beautiful art thou! thy eyes are doves’ eyes, besides what is hid within. Thy hair is as flocks of goats, which Come up from mount Galaad. Thy teeth as flocks of sheep, that are shorn which come up from the washing, all with twins, and there is none barren among them.

lessons.la: ICUT vitta coccínea lábia tua, et elóquium tuum dulce. Sicut fragmen mali púnici, ita genæ tuæ, absque eo quod intrínsecus latet. Sicut turris David collum tuum, quæ ædificáta est cum propugnáculis: mille clýpei pendent ex ea, omnis armatúra fórtium. Duo úbera tua, sicut duo hínnuli cápreæ gemélli, qui pascúntur in líliis. Donec aspíret dies, et inclinéntur umbræ, vadam ad montem myrrhæ, et ad collem thuris. Tota pulchra es amíca mea, et mácula non est in te.
lessons.en: Thy lips are as a scarlet lace: and thy speech sweet. Thy cheeks are as a piece of a pomegranate, besides that which lieth hid within. Thy neck, is as the tower of David, which is built with bulwarks: a thousand bucklers hang upon it, all the armour of valiant men. Thy two breasts like two young roes that are twins, which feed among the lilies. Till the day break, and the shadows retire, I will go to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense. Thou art all fair, O my love, and there is not a spot in thee.

Vulnerásti cor meum soror mea sponsa, vulnerásti cor meum in uno oculórum tuórum, et in uno crine colli tui. Quam pulchræ sunt mammæ tuæ soror mea sponsa! pulchrióra sunt úbera tua vino, et odor unguentórum tuórum super ómnia arómata.
lessons.en: Come from Libanus, my spouse, come from Libanus, come: thou shalt be crowned from the top of Amana, from the top of Sanir and Hermon, from the dens of the lions, from the mountains of the leopards. Thou hast wounded my heart, my sister, my spouse, thou hast wounded my heart with one of thy eyes, and with one hair of thy neck. How beautiful are thy breasts, my sister, my spouse! thy breasts are more beautiful than wine, and the sweet smell of thy ointments above all aromatical spices.

head: Cap. 3.
lessons.la: Et Cap. RATRES, ego me non árbitror comprehendísse. Unum autem: quæ quidem retro sunt oblivíscens, ad ea vero, quæ sunt prióra, exténdens meípsum, ad destinátum pérsequor, ad bravíum supérne vocatiónis Dei in Christo Jesu. Quicúmque ergo perfécti sumus, hoc sentiámus: et si quid áliter sápitis, et hoc vobis Deus revelábit. Verúmtamen ad quod pervénimus ut idem sapiámus, et in eádem permaneámus régula. I.
lessons.en: And may be found in him, not having my justice, which is of the law, but that which is of the faith of Christ Jesus, which is of God, justice in faith: Brethren, I do not count myself to have apprehended. But one thing I do: forgetting the things that are behind, and stretching forth myself to those that are before, I press towards the mark, to the prize of the supernal vocation of God in Christ Jesus. Let us therefore, as many as are perfect, be thus minded; and if in any thing you be otherwise minded, this also God will reveal to you. Nevertheless whereunto we are come, that we be of the same mind, let us also continue in the same rule.

Multi enim ámbulant, quos sæpe dicébam vobis nunc autem et flens dico inimícos crucis Christi: uorum finis intéritus: quorum Deus venter est: et glória in confusióne ipsórum, qui terréna sápiunt. Nostra autem conversátio in cælis est:
lessons.en: Be ye followers of me, brethren, and observe them who walk so as you have our model. For many walk, of whom I have told you often (and now tell you weeping), that they are enemies of the cross of Christ; Whose end is destruction; whose God is their belly; and whose glory is in their shame; who mind earthly things. But our conversation is in heaven; from whence also we look for the Saviour, our Lord Jesus Christ,

Itaque fratres mei caríssimi, et desideratíssimi, gáudium meum, et coróna mea: sic state in Dómino, caríssimi.
lessons.en: But our conversation is in heaven; from whence also we look for the Saviour, our Lord Jesus Christ, Who will reform the body of our lowness, made like to the body of his glory, according to the operation whereby also he is able to subdue all things unto himself. Therefore, my dearly beloved brethren, and most desired, my joy and my crown; so stand fast in the Lord, my dearly beloved.

lessons.la: Mília, Vercéllis nóbili génere orta, vel ab ipsis ztátis primórdiis pietátem in Deum et paréntes impénse cóluit. Patre defúncto, in eam, quam ántia iníerat, sancte ac innocénter vivéndi ratiónem alácrius incúmbere — ccepit. Quare ópibus, partitióne patérnz hereditátis sibi obveniéntibus, monastérium sancte Margaritae prope Vercéllas :edificávit, quo cum áliquat nobílibus puéllis se recépit, ut quod in votis jam habúerat, Deo sub Régula sancti Augustíni ac institútis Sorórum de Fceniténtia sancti Domínici libérius inservíret. Anno post, qui fuit zetátis suce décimus nonus, se per religiósam professiónem caelésti Sponso árcttus obstrinxit, vitam inde actúra, quam nec terrenárum rerum sollicitúdo, nec séculi blandiménta violárent.

My contémptum contémptui sui ipsíus, et perféctzte abnegatióni perpétuo federe sociávit. Ut puritátem, quam Deo dicáverat, ilibátam custodíret, crebris flagellatiónibus, cilício, ac jejúniis carnem júgiter aflli-: E£ens, eam spirítui servíre coégit. Tanta fuit humilitáte, ut nedum vilióra quæque domus ministéria laetíssima obíret, sed étiam, quamvis ómnium mater haberétur, nonnísi ægre addúci potúerit ut céteris praeésset. Quod sane munus singulári prudéntia ac zelo plúries gessit. Oratióni summópere addícta, una czeléstium mysteriórum contemplatióne — íntegros dies quandóque transégit. Hinc de ipsa preeclárum illud fertur ad Soróres mónitum : Sanctimoniálem, quæ in hoc orándi génere non fúerit valde exercitáta, ad instar esse ádvenze, urbem ad coeméndas merces ingrediéntis, ac nesciéntis cum quibus de hoc agat, vel quo prétio eas váleat comparáre.

RGINEM Deíparam, ceu matrem — amantíssimam, præcípuo pietátis afféctu venerabátur. Tanta autem in Domínicze Passiónis mystéria erat devotióne, ac ita illíus mentem cruciátuum, quos pértulit Christus, oblectábat contemplátio, ut eorúmdem se étiam partícipem fíeri veheménter optáret. Tandem cum annos octo et quinquagínta in monastério pie justéque exegísset, méritis ac virtútibus plena migrávit ad Sponsum die tértia Máii, vivificæ Crucis Inventióne solémni, anno millésimo tercentésimo quartodécimo, zetátis suce septuagésimo sexto. Cultum eídem delátum, ac przesértim post priórem illíus córporis translatiónem auctum propagatúmque, Clemens | Décimus — quartus Póntifex Máximus Apostólica auctoritáte probávit, atque ut festum beátae 7Emiliaa cum Offício et Missa décimo sexto Kaléndas Septémbris, quo die sacræ illíus Relíquize secúndo elátze sunt, ab univérso Fratrum Przdicatórum Ordine celebrarétur, benígne concéssit.

Nimírum p réntes ejus Joánnes et Líbera. longǽva :zetáte provécti et, ántia stériles, voto concépto ac frequentíssimis précibus fi lium hunc tandem ímpetra runt; quem nascóntem nov? miráculo rúbea cruce in péctore insignítum paréntes ipsi, vicináque omnes sunt admiráti. Exspectatiónem caeléstis augúrii Kachus non feféllit. Ecce enim adhuc infántulus, matérnz pietátis imitátor, quartae ac sextæ. Feriárum cujúsque bebdámadze jejúnio, quo fúerat concéptus, étiam nondum ratiónis compos vóluit enutríri. Mórtuo paulo post utróque parénte, amplíssimi patrimónii heres únicus, et civitátis ipsíus suprémus dóminus ac moderátor relíctus, qui infans jam viril abstinéntia sese matérno ab úbere depúlerat, fortióri rerum humanárum contémptu, vir factus pátriam bónaque ómnia et dignitátes patérnas nedum deséruit, sed contémpsit.Inde immortálem pátriam, própria contémpta, quzesitúrus, dum sciret ex Apóstolo permanéntem civitátem nos hic nullam habére, sed futúram inquírere, loca sanctióra, ct toto terrárum orbe sanctitátis vestígiis celebérrima, ccpit pedes invisere. Primum Aquampendéntem ltálize urbem áppulit, et ecce, hac in Civitáte primam erga infírmos exercéndz caritátis nactus occasiónem, beátus Rochus, cum tota fere cívitas pestiléntize morbo contabésceret, afflíctis contágii lue homínibus sublevándis totum se addíxit. Inde, civitáte a morbo tpidemíze liberáta, primum Gesénam, deínde Placéntiam *t vicínas Itálize urbes peraErivit, mira ubíque exércens Ópera caritátis, ac przesértim Supra humánas vires divína Virtúte et curatiónum — frequentióribus signis toto illo in orbe celebérrimus; inter quæ illud áscidit, quod Romam ad purpúrei senátus príncipem quemdam (Cardinálem dicunt) vocátus, eum peste laborántem, signo Crucis in fronte zegrotántis imprésso, prótinus sanávit; aliáque quamplúrima ínibi, e£ per totam ferme Itáliam sanitátum mirácula édidit sanctíssimus Peregrínus.

NIMVERO probatíssima et E gratissimi Deo et homínibus Viri necésse fuit ut patiéntiam probáret tentátio. Quam ob rem in Itália primum gravi febre et infixo divína permissióne sagíttze vúlnere percússus, omni ope humána destitútus, sub arbóre jácuit : cui, ut olim Christo ipsi, appáruit Angelus de czelo confórtans eum, eumdémque, per id tempus, canis, sumpto de mensa dómini pane quotidiáno, pavit; non instínctu naturáli, sed ejus jussu, qui Corvis ministrántibus Prophétas suos enutrívit, et sitiénti pópulo fontem aquæ e rupe duríssima edúxit. Inde in pátriam redeúntem novíssima, sed longe gravióre tentatióne Sanctum suum Dóminus mirificávit. Illum enim vili in hábitu, quem evangélicze paupertátis aemulatióne indúerat, deprehénsum cives Montepessuláni, tamquam pátria: proditórem aut exploratórem, in cárcerem detrúdunt.

IMs postrémus fuit, ac certe ad meritórum augméntum, gloriosissimus christiáni Antagonístz:e cum mundo et cum dæmone conflictus : dum illum, sibi jure hereditário débiti civitáátis Montispessulánae dominii contémptu, hunc vero per próprios cives et paréntes exasperántem advérsus Sanctum, mira tot injuriárum tolerántia súperat ac devínxit. Tandem longe misericordíssimus Deus, qui mílitem suum toto jam quinquénnio cum concupiscéntia mundi, et supérbia vite conflictántem e cæli spécula intuebátur, prius angélica visitatióne confortátum, solo edúxit ccelo donándum. Quem «ccuménici Constantiénsis concílii Patres, eláta ejus insolémni supplicatióne imágine, omnésque toto terrárum orbe pópuli christiáni, in pública pestiléntize clade ádeo propitium advocátum sunt expérti, ut tot miraculórum frequéntia,et unánimi orthodóxae Ecclésize consénsu firmáta ejus Ssanctitáte, et arce Confessóri sanctíssimo eréctze, et supplicatiónes públicze fúerint institútze : illúmque plebs christiána velut czelo jam beátum jure mérito venerétur.
