resp.b: Qui totum subdit suis orbem légibus.
v: Præstet no. bis grátiam Déitas beáta patris ac Nati paritérque Spíritus almi.

lessons.la: Bn Dei Génitrix et semper Virgo María, templum Dómini, sacrárium — Spíritus sancti, Virgo ante partum, Virgo in partu, Virgo post partum, przeséntis solemnitátis diéi expers nullo modo credénda est. Hzec est enim, quee Dei pópulum faciéndo monébat spérnere peritúri luxus sǽculi, ac lenocínia mortális vite declináre : carnis quoque pudicítiam | cum virginitátis honóre intra cordis hospítium observáre. Decébat eam, ómnium virtútum Regínam, fructum cunctis esse salútis perpétuz : et sóciam Angelórum, omnes suis informáre exémplis. Unde et innumerábilis utrísque sexus multitúdo ejus secúta est vestígia, relíctis nuptiárum cópulis. H.ij Felix namque es sacra Virgo María, et omni laude digníssima :* Quia ex te ortus est Sol justítize, Christus Deus noster. X. Ora pro pópulo, intérveni pro clero, intercéde pro devóto femíneo sexu : sentíant omnes tuum juvámen, quicúmque célebrant tuam solemnitátem. — Quia ex te ortus est Sol justítiæ Christus Deus noster. Benedictio. Spíritus sancti grátia illumináre dignétur sensus et corda nostra. Jy. Amen.

RINCIPIUM ac finis omnis creatúrze, supérna czelórum regna Spirítibus angélicis ad laudem et glóriam atque honórem sui nóminis ac majestátis, ín perpétuum miro ordine collocávit. Novem autem esse Angelórum órdines ad Dei judícia ac ministéria complénda, testánte sacro elóquio, cognóvimus : quorum Principátus atque Potestátes subtíliter ac mirabíliter Dei omnipoténtis nutu distinguúntur. talibúsque, a. primórdio incipiéntis vitze, beatórum Spirítuum distinctiónibus supérna celórum regna a Deo Conditóre in perpétuum mirabíliter collocáta subsístunt. His ómnibus, fratres caríssimi, tam decóris ac Deo diléctis Angelórum agmínibus, hujus diéi solemnitátem crédimus esse consecrátam.

resp.a: Te sanctum Dóminum in excélsis laudant omnes Angeli dicéntes: Te decet laus Et honor, Dómine
v: Chérubim quoque et Séraphim Sanctus proclámant, et omnis cǽlicus ordo, dicéntes.

lessons.la: OLEMNITAS hzec non solum Angelórum spirítibus, veTum Sanctis ómnibus, qui ab exórdio mundi creáti sunt, dedicáta consístit. Quorum primi fuérunt Patriárchze, — patres Prophetárum et Apostolórum., Hi Deo digni invénti sunt, fide przeclári, sapiéntes in Ópere, reparatóres orbis, justítia insignes, longánimes in Spe, obediéntes in przecéptis, Créduli ip. promissiónibus, susCeptóres Angelórum effécti, Hos séquitur eléctio ProphetáTum, cum quibus locútus est Cus, et osténdit illis secréta sua. Quorum álii in útero, álii in puerítia, álii in juventúte, álii in senectúte sanctificáti invénti sunt, fide pleni, devolióne summi, indústria solértes, excellénti ingénio prǽditi: in exercitatióne disciplínæ instrúcti, in sancta meditatióne assídui, metúque mortis intrépidi : verberántes tyránnos, peccáta pópuli plangéntes, multísque signis eftulsére. Hos séquitur Joánnes Baptísta, qui eódem Angelo, quo Christus, denuntiánte concéptus, exórdio baptísmatis primátum ténuit.

resp.a: Inter natos mulíerum non surréxit major Joánne Baptísta
resp.b: Qui viam Dómino praparávit in erémo.
v: Fuit homo missus a Deo, cui nomen erat Joánnes.

lessons.la: EQUITUR duodénus Apostol lórum númerus : quos ad componéndum novæ fídei fundaméntum, erigendúmque adhuc ténerze statum Ecclésize providéntia divína ex ómnibus, quos capiébat mundus, elégit : ut in omnem terram exíret sonus eórum. Hi vera: viti, id est Christo, támquam pálmites adhzesére : et eórum fructus in sempitérnum pérmanens non marcéscit, Hi sunt, quibus Iocútus est Dóminus dicens : Vos estis lux mundi, Et : Non potest cívitas abscóndi supra montem pósita: neque accéndunt lucérnam, et ponunt eam sub módio. Et íterum : Jam non dicam vos servos, sed aniícos : quia quzecúmque audívi a Patre meo, nota feci vobis.

resp.a: Qui sunt isti, qui ut nubes volant
resp.b: Et quasi colúmbae ad fenéstras suas?
v: Candidióres nive, nitidióres lacte, rubicundióres ébore antíquo.

lessons.la: Aresrous subjéctum est triumphále Mártyrum nomen : qui per divérsa tormentórum génera Christi Passiónem imitabántur. Álii namque ferro perémpti, álii flammis exústi, álii flagris verberáti, álii véctibus perforaáti, Álii cruciáti patíbulo, álii demérsi pélagi perículo, álii vivi decoriáti, áli1 vínculis mancipáti, álii linguis priváti, álii lapídibus óbruti, álii frígore afflícti, álii fame cruciáti : álii vero truncátis mánibus, sive céteris membris cæsis, spectáculum Angelis et homínibus facti, contumélias in pópulis nudi propter nomen Dómini portavérunt.

resp.a: Lavérunt stolas suas et cándidas eas fecérunt
resp.b: In sánguine Agni.
v: Isti sunt qui venérunt ex magna tribulatióne, et lavérunt stolas suas

lessons.la: Is quoque Sacerdétibus atque Doctóribus sive Confessóribus hujus festivitátem diéi non ignótam esse crédimus : qui corda fidélium imbribus irrigárunt czeléstibus, ut proférre immarcescíbilem bonórum óperum fructum possent. Hi talénta sibi crédita, cum usúra sine fraude amplificáre procuravérunt : quia bonum, quod didicére, subjectórum méntibus, arguéndo, | obsecrándo, increpándo, insérere nitebántur. Horum mens lucidíssima, manus vero plene munditia sunt : eo quod sacrosáncta mystéria celebrántes, hóstiam vivam Deo semetípsos offérre sine mácula pravi óperis non desístunt. Et licet persecutórum non sénserint gládium, tamen per vite méritum martýrio non priváántur.

resp.a: Sint lumbi vestri præcíncti, et lucernæ ardéntes n mánibus vestris
resp.b: Et vos símiles homínibus exspectántibus dóminum suum, gquan o revertátur a núptiis
v: Vi; iláte ergo, quia nescítis a hora Dóminus vester ventur us sit.

lessons.la: IKGINES quoque sacre ab V hujus diéi solemnitáte non sunt separátze, Hæ sunt enim, qui spreta liberórum propágine, sponso, qui in czelis est, perénni mente, actu, hábitu et gestu, sese applicáre maluérunt. Hæ sunt, quce oratiónibus instántes, jejúniis adhzeréntes, vigílias sacras amántes, eleemósynas sectántes, páuperes recreántes, nudos vestiéntes, infírmos visitántes, in tribulatióne gaudéntes, in verbis calúmnize vel contumélie patiéntes, in augménto sue perfectiónis húmiles, in damno rerum temporálium Deo grátias agóbant.

resp.b: Óleum recóndite in vasis vestris, dum sponsus advénerit.
v: Média nocte clamor factus est: Ecce, sponsus venit

Tráns- &pint cuncta, quce temporáliter stipe celebrántur. Curáte, qii his solemnitátibus intercSUIS, ne ab zetérna solemnitáte separémini. Quid enim prodest interésse festis hóminum, si deésse contíngat festis Angelórum?

resp.a: Concède nobis, Dómine, quæsumus, veniam delictorum: et intercedéntibusSanctis, quorum hódie solémnia celebramus, talem nobis tríbue devotionem
resp.b: Ut ad eórum perveníre mereámur societátem. EF. Adjuvent nos eorum mérita, quos própria impédiunt scélera: excuset intercessio, accusat quos áctio: et qui eis tribuisti cæléstis— palmam triúmphi, nobis véniam non déneges peccáti.

lessons.la: IMON, patre Rodúlpho, opuléntis ac nóbilis óppidi sancti Archángeli prope Críminum in Flamínia Cómite, sǽculo décimo tértio mediánte ortum hábuit, Quo témpore diræ factiónes, quibus a divinárum litterárum ac verze pietátis stúdio cives ope ac poténtia przeclarióres avellebántur, contentiónibus, dissidiis et armis illos implicábant, Inter heec fuit enutrítus Simon, donec sancti Spíritus afflátu cernens mundi glóriam, preter suam inanitátem, in perníciem — addúcere, illam spérnere, Deóque sibi esse serviéndum duxit in Ordine Przdicatórum, annos matus Septem et vigínti, Vividióra tunc erant exémpla sanctitátis et virtátum ómnium, quibus sanctus Petrus Martyr et Angélicus Doctor sanctus Thomás Aquínas ccenóbium sancti Catáldi civitátis Ariminénsis lonestáverant : quibus permótus, ibi Reliziónis hábitum suscípere státuit. Recógitans vero quod Dóminus Jesus, propósito sibi gáudio, sustínuit crucem confusióne contémpta; ut magis illi conformarétur, quamquam summo loco natus, et Epíscopi Ariminénsis ejúsdem Ordinis, nec non Archipresbyteri, qui eídem in EpiCopátu succéssit, nepos esset, objurgatiónibus et humanárum ratiónum posthábitis moméntis, inter láicos, quos Convérsos appéllant, ibídem adscríbi humíllime postulávit et obtínuit.

N sacro illo recéssu Abditus, I* totum christiánis virtútibus excoléndis dedit. Elúxit preesértim in ea summa vitz austéritas atque in Deum et hómines cáritas fla grantissima. Labóri semper inténtus, nunquam visus est Ótio vel sibi indulgére; sed aut oráre, meditár, aut mánuum vacáre opéribus. Excólere hortum, vérrere sordes, vilióra éxsequi múnera, nedum in delíciis habébat, sed tali sedulitáte, diligéntia animique demissióne ac lenitáte complébat, ut ómnium esset admiralióni et exémplo. Abstinéntia tanta fuit, ut sepe bíduum absque cibo transégerit, perque quinque annos Cincrália jejúnia pane tantum et aqua definiverit, donec id pro império Superiórum illi vétitum fúerit, ídeo quod ob cibi parcitátem prorsus inválidus et impotens ad offícia obeúnda eváderet. Corpus suum férrea caténa flagrísque eruentábat, et nuda tábula sibi, étiam seni morbóque afflicto, pro léctulo fuit. Animárum zelo succénsus, Crucem devotíssime amplexátus, sǽpius per civitátem excurrébat, christiána rudiménta púeros édocens, peccatóres árguens, protérvos íncrepans, eo succéssu, ut plures ad meliórem frugem fúcrint revocáti, Ab his opé ribus invídia furens humárni génceris hostis illum retráhere modis ónmibus frustra adnisus est : nam viva fidc muni tus, dæmonum insídias fórtiter vicit. t.

N oratióne autem assíduus, Deum étiam frequens pro infidélium et hzereticórum conversióne exorábat, idque tanto lacrimárum imbre perfúsus, ut quinquagésimo — séptimo ztátis anno cecus evaserit; quam calamitátem usque ad óbitum^hiláriter tulit. Nitórem domus Dei in wdítui offício, sacras vestes, altárium ornaménta, sacerdótibus humillime famulári máxime curans, pari sénsuum custódia et observántia erga diviníssimum Eucharístiæ sacraméntum sacrásque imágines, hac illac in ecclésia pro opportunitáte incedébat, ut vidéntes omnes ad devotiónem excitáret. Quamvis vero miraculórum et prophetize donis clarus, ea tamen erat humilitáte, ut vilem se eccatórem et indígnum cx íntimo cordis réputans, hóminum láudibus veheménter excruciarétur : atque ita supérnis visiónibus mirisque fulgóribus et fragrántiis in angústiis et infirmitáatibus, quibus frequénter premebátur, recreári promeruisse meméóriz próditur : donec. méritis et diérum longitúdine plenus, devotíssime suscéptis Ecclésim Sacraméntis, in Dómino quiévit die tértia Novémbris anni millésimi tercentésimi décimi noni : facto sábito ad ejus venerándum corpus tanto pópuli conCúrsu, ut per bíduum tumulári nequiverat. Quanta autem veneratióne felíces illas exúvize per quingéntos annos fúerint decorátz, constat ex illárum multiplícibus translatiónibus. Cives tandem Sancti Archángeli solemnióri pompa in sacéllo ecclésize collegiátae illas reposuérunt, anno millésimo octingentésimo décimo séptimo, ibíque honorífice condúntur. Quibus permótus Pius Séptimus Póntifex Máximus, ut de beáto Simóne Officium et Missa in univérso Przedicatórum Ordine ac in tota dicecési Ariminénsi celebrári possit, ex sacræ Rítuum Congregatiónis consúlto, benígne concéssit.

Cárolus, Mediolani nobili Borrom: eórum família natus, quanta futurus esset sanctitáte conspicuus, divina lux super pariéntis matris cubiculum noctu coruscans przsignávit. a Pio quarto avunculo suo Cardinális primum, et Mox Mediolanénsis archiepíscopus creatus, plárimam operam adhibuit, ut, juxta sacrosanctum Tridentinum concílium, ecclésiam sibi commissam compóneret; atque, ut depravatos plebis suæ mores reformaret, seípsum exímiæ sanctitátis præbuit exemplar. In profligandis hæreticis e partibus Rhætórum et Helvetiórum, quorum plurimos ad christianam fidem convértit, maxime laborávit. Verbi Dei prædicatiónem, gravíssimis licet curis Occupátus, nunquam intermisit.

Uritano principatu véndito, prétium univérsum, ad quadragínta aureórum millia, una die in páuperes erogáávit: et íterum viginti millia, sibi legata, distríbuit. Cum pestis Mediolani srassarétur, domesticam supellectilem, nec relícto sibi lectulo, in eosdem alendos cóntulit, eoque morbo laborántes sédulo invisens, sacraménta propriis mánibus administrábat, Multas ecclésias, monastéria, collégia ædificávit. Ecclesiásticæ libertátis fuit acerrimus propugnator. Disciplína vero restituénda: sollícitus, a seditiosis, dum oratióni insísteret, torménti bellici glóbulo percússus, divina virtúte servátur illæsus.

Nocturnis vigiliis, asperrimo cilício, assiduis flagellis corpus domábat. lessons.la: Ártibus, Limæ in América meridionáti ex nobílibus paréntibus Joánne de Porres et Anna Velásquez, VR IET27] fua aCsz mo Die V, Novémbris. E. Martini De Porres. 949 anno reparátae Salútis millésimo quingentésimo[sexagésimo) nono, ortum hábuit. Ab ineúnte ztáte, miro morum candóre futúrzie exímiæ sanctitátis indícia præbuit. Virtútes enim modéstiae, humilitátis ac in páuperes liberalitátis puerítiam ejus ómnibus admirábilem reddidérunt, Adoléscens vero, júgiter cum eo erga próximos prasértim zegrótos adolévit commiserátio : ideóque arti chirúrgicee omne impéndit stádium, ut absque ullo emoluménto sanitátem impertiret, quod ei sæpíssime pro voto cessit. Cáritas Dei ut magis magísque in corde suo diffunderétur, mundi honóres et oblectaménta abhórrens, patérnze domus oblítus, Tértium sancti Patriárchze | Domínici | Órdinem amplécti, ac inter láicos operários recenséri eníxe postulávit : quod ei ex senténtia páriter succéssit. Absolúáto tirOcínio summa ómnium admiratióne, ac solémnibus votis nuncupátis, quis enarráre póterit quo stádio, qua solértia emnígenas, qua Religiósum Perféctum constítuunt, virtútes cólere et prósequi conténderit? Humilitátem ádeo diligébat, ut vilióra et abjectióra quæque coenóbii offícia semper in delíciis habúerit obíre, peccatórem máximum se appellári, flexísque génibus pedes tórum deosculári, qui maledíctis eum oneráre audébant.

UAMVIS ab spontánea vel Q levi ánimze mácula remótus, nunquam désiit assíduis Jjúniis carnem suam excruciáre, cilíciis et caténis férreis diro modo cruentáre : ut rectíssime ásseri possit quod mortificatiónem [esu in suo córpore circumférret, Tanto in divínum humán:e Salátis Reparatórem cestuábat amóre, ut aliquándo visus sit ante imáginem Jesu Christi e cruce pendéntis précibus inténtus, sublátus a terra ad eum evoláre, tamquam plaga láteris ejus adhuc sánguinem scaturisset, admótis lábiis eam súgere, et máxima aviditáte satiári voluísset. Nil iegitur mirum si ex hoc perénni divíni amóris fonte inebriátus,' non nisi de czeléstibus loquerétur, quibus et suum et aliórum corda inflammáre ardentíssime exopiúbat. Martýrii palmæ cupidíssimus, Japóni et Sinárum impéria pétere in optátis habébat, ut inter hostiles ethnicórum manus, profúso sánguine, Christi hóstia éffici mererétur. Hac vero inexplébili in Deum caritáte síngulos cujúsque conditiónis hómines complectebátur, et máxime zegroótos, et praesértim moriéntes, quibus ómnia consolatiónis offícia ex corde przestáre studébat. Cum vero pátriz Suze tam miránda caritátis arguménta przebéret, uno eodémque témpore compassívi amóris igne incénsus erga míseros captívos in Africa degéntes, miro prorsus prodígio sǽpius illic adésse visus est, ut eos confortáret, providéret, eorúmque captivilátis caténas dissólveret. Áccidit ut cum unus ex illis génere Hispánus, postquam, Martíno auxiliánte, libertátem recuperávit Túlize Caesáreze, non post multum —€——X iso Die V1. Nov. De. Hierónymi, Valentini Et Soc, témporis spátium Lima eum vidísset, grati ánimi sensu commótus, ceu insígnem suum liberatórem salutáverit, et accéptum benefícium, Martíno reluctánte, ómnibus praedicáre non destíterit.

EHEMENTER angebátur gothos vidére puérulos aliósque líberos — paréntibus orbátos máximis óbrui malis; quibus reparándis, Lima, ut ad pietátem et honestátem institueréntur, percélebre collégium excitándum curávit. Eo quoque procéssit ejus humanitátis sensus, ut vel bruta ipsa animália suam óperam salutárem curámque continénter fúerint expérta, Deus vero tam excelléntem Servi sui caritátem supérnis donis mirum in modum exornáre sibi complácuit. Divino hinc húimine collustrátus et futúra przedíxit, et córdium abscóndita cognóvit, et dæmonum artes furentésque ímpetus detéxit ac profligávit, Et licet rudis et ignárus, gravíssimas theológicas questiónes sic dirimébat, ut vel ipsi doctíssimi viri admiraréntur, ejúsque sapiéntiam divínitus haustum celebrárent. Dignus przetérea a Deo rédditus, ut cum cælítibus collóquia habéret, multis coruscáret miráculis, et tandem extrémum :etérng suze retributiónis diem appropinquáre cognósceret, quem plúries et clare maniféstum fecit. Morbo ítaque diútino corréptus, ut omnes ccenábii Religióst moriénti adéssent eníxe postulávit, a quibus de cunctis | ao eo accéptis offénsis véniam pétiit. Defixis dein in Crucifíxi imágine óculis, quam pra mánibus tenébat, ad ea verba Evangeélii, quod astántes reci. tábant, Verbum caro factum est, imágine Crucifíxi in péctore depósita, seréna fronte hilaríque vultu, innocéntem ánimam réddidit Creatóri, an. no millésimo sexcentésimo tri- £ésimo nono, tértio Nonas Novémbris, anno zetátis sum sexagésimo. Multis vivens e post óbitum miráculis cláruit, Quibus rite áínitis ac probátis, Gregórius Décimus sextus Póntifex Máximus illum Beatórum albo accénsuit, ejúsque festum cum Offício ct Missa in univérso — Przedicatórum Ordine et Limána dicecési celebrári corcéssit.

lessons.la: x Frátribus Ordinis Przedicatórum, qui Evangélium Tunquinénsi pópulo nuntiáverant, Christi fidem próprio sánguine obsignáre primi meruérunt Franciscus Gil de Féderich et. Matthǽus. Alónso Leziniána. Hi, relícta Hispánia, ubi nati erant, ad Philippinas Ínsulas una migrántes, inde ad Tunquinum missi sunt. Quo cum appulíssent, spreto vitee discrímine, verbum vitæ dissemináre et regnum Dei amplificáre non desiérunt, donec ab ímpiis satcellitibus in cárcerem conjécti, nonníhil apostólicum officium intermíttere coácti fuérunt. Quantum tamen per eustódum tolerántiam lícuit, sacraménta ministráre, Christiános ad virtútem hortári, afflíctos solári nitebántur. Franciscus tandem cápitis damnátus est. Matthéum vero, etsi non eádem senténtia mulctátus, obtestátus est, útpote ejúsdem fídei assecla, velle se Francísco adJúngi cumque &o obtruncári : cunis voti compos factus est. Ambo ínitur crucem manu geStántes, ad supplícii locum ducti, ibi, Christi fidem iteráto proféssi, ceterósque adhortáti ut eídem sincére adhzaerérent, gládio interfécti sunt, undécimo Kaléndas Februárii, anno millésimo septingentésimo quadragésimo quinto.

USTRIS sex a tam gloriósa confessióne nondum exáctis, iliam de christiáni nóminis hóstibus victóriam retulérunt Hyacínthus Castaúéda, et Vincéntius Liem a Pace, indízena, Praedicatórum família páriter alúmni. Horum alter Hyacínthus, cum annis quinque apostólico múnere in Tunquíno functus esset, tandem comprehénsus, ac bíduo cibi potúsque expers, præsidi sístitur, atque in cáveam arundíneam ádeo exíguam trúditur ut neque stando locus esset, neque cubándi. Vincéntium, brevi póstea deprehénsum, in cáveam non absímilem conjiciunt nefárii satéllites. Hyacínthus déniqueextrémo supplício damnátur. Póterat Vincéntius mortem effúgere, cum, persecutiónis edícto, a capitáli paena immuúnes essent indigenze, sed eníxe flagitávit ut illíus consors fíeret in martýrio, cujus consors fúerat im apostolátu. Sicque generosi fídei confessóres, quómodo in vita dilexérunt se, ita et in morte non sunt separáti, Passi sunt séptimo Idus Novémbris, anno nullésimo septingentésimo septuagésimo tértio.

RJECLARAS illas Mártyrum Tunquinénsium primítias, quas seculum duodevicésimum Christo obtúlerat, véluti semen pretiósum excépit szeculo sequénti ingens Mártyrum messis. Quos inter, vitze sanctitáte non minus quam episcopális dignitátis decóre splendent Hierónymus Hermosílla et Valentinus Bérrio-Ochóa, Hispáni, atque Vicárii Apostólici per Tunquínum constitúti. Et Hierónymus quidem, postquam Przedicatórum Órdinem ingréssus fúerat et in "Tunquinum trajécerat, trigínta ámélius annos víneam illam Dominicam indefésso labóre excóluit, plúries ad necem quæsítus, donec tandem una cum fidéli fámulo suo atque Catechísta Tosépho Khang indígena, in satéllituni manus íscidit, mox in cárcerem relegándus. Valentínus porro, vir plane apostólici péctoris quamvis cetáte júnior, paucis post diébus in eódem loco captus est simul cum Petro Almató, Sacerdóte, pari animárum stúádio vehementíssime accénso. Qui omnes, post fidem strénue ante júdices confirmátam,anno millésimo octingentésimo sexagésimo primo, cápitis obtruncatióne martýrii palmam sunt consecúti, anno vero millésimo nongentésimo sexto a Pio Papa Décimo beatórum C:elitum albo eódem Decréto, quo prióres illi Mártyres Tunquinénses, sunt adscrípti.

lessons.la: U es Deus omnípotens, T quem trinum in persónis, et unum in substántia Deitátis cólimus et adorámus : Patrem. ingénitum, Fílium de Patre unigénitum, Spíritum sanctum de utróque procedéntem et in utróque permanéniem : sanctam et indivíduam Trinitátem. Te deprecámur, supplicámus et orámus : auge fidem, auge spem, auge caritátem. Fac nos per ipsam grátiam tuam, semper et in fide stábiles et in ópere efficáces : ut per fidem rectam et condiígna fídei ópera, ad vitam, te miseránte, perveniámus :etérnam : ut ibl vidéntes glóriam tuam sícuti est, adorémus majestátem tuam, quos dignos féceris vidére imménsam pulchritádinem tuam.

lessons.la: ANCTA María Vírginum piís. S sima, súscipe vota servuló. rum assídua : lapsos érige, errántes córrige, treméntes corróbora, pusillánimes con. fórta : ut tibi semper refer. mus laudes, quam Dei summi cólimus Genitricem. Suscípiat, benigníssima, Génitus tuus captivórum gémitus, clamóres peregrinórum, suspíria júvenum, vota vírginum, laménta viduárum, preces ómnium tua sancta suffrágia —deposcéntium : quz cunctis szeculis lumen verum effudísti Dóminum ]esum Christum. Virgo sancta, Virgo eloriósa, Mater Christi simul et Sponsa, non dedignéris opem ferre animábus, quas vides amóre Dei czléstis Sponsi flagráre, atque ejus núptias sitibúndo corde desideráre.

lessons.la: Ómine, quóties bene ágimus, gaudent Angeli, et tristántur dæmones : quóties a bono deviámus, diábolum ketificámus, et Angelos tuos suo gáudio defraudámus. Gáudium est enim eis super uno peccatóre poeniténtiam agénte; sed diábolo super uno justo peniténtiam deserénte. Da ígitur, da Pater eis semper gaudére de nobis; ut et tu semper per eos laudéris in nobis : et nos cum eis in unum ovíle tuum adducámur; ut confteámur nómini sancto tuo, Creátor hóminum et angelórum.

resp.a: Te sanctum Dóminum in excélsis laudant omnes Angeli dicéntes
resp.b: Te decet laus Et honor, Dómine.

lessons.la: difficile nobis non est, l quod a Sanctis geritur, imitari, cum sine præcedenti exemplo ab antiquis talia gesta conspicimus: ut non ipsi aliorum æmuli redderentur, sed æmulandæ virtutis seipsos nobis præberent exemplum: ut dum nos ex ipsis, et ex nobis alii proficiunt, sic Christus in suis semper servis in Ecclesia sancta laudetur. Unde ab origine mundi innocens Abel occiditur, Henoch Deo placens transfertur, justus Noë invenitur, Abraham fidelis probatur, Moyses mansuetus dignoscitur, Jesus castus, David lenis, Elias acceptus, Daniel sanctus, tres pueri victores redduntur.
lessons.en: It ought not to be hard for us to copy others, when we see what they of old time did without any examples before them, so that in them who copied not others, but set example for others to copy, and in us who copy them, and in them which take example by us, Christ may be glorified in His holy Church. Thus from the very beginning of the world there have been the harmless Abel who was slain, Enoch who walked with God, and was seen no more, for God took him, Noah who was found righteous, Abraham who was tried and found faithful, Moses who was the meekest of men, Joshua who was chaste, David who was gentle, Elijah who was accepted, Daniel who was holy, and the three Children who were victorious.

lessons.la: ERAGRARUNT piscatóres orP bem terrárum, et infírmum eum inveniéntes, ad sanitátem reduxérunt : et in ruína pósitum, ad stabilitátem revocavérunt : non scuta movéntes, non arcus tendéntes, non sagíttas mitténtes, non pecúniam largiéntes, non in eloquéntia confidéntes. Pecúnia indigéntes, sed regnum caelórum possidéntes : non habéntes humána solátia, habéntes autem Dóminum secum. Ego enim, inquit, vobíscum sum usque ad consummatiónem sǽculi. Peragrárunt univérsum orbem oves simul cum lupis : et vulnerátze a béstiis non sunt oves, sed magis lupi ad óvium mansuetúdinem sunt convérsi.

resp.a: Qui sunt isti, qui ut nubes volant
resp.b: Et quasi colúmbæ ad fenéstras suas?

lessons.la: UIBUS ergo vos láudibus prædicem fortíssimi Mártyres? Tolerástis, usque ad consummatiónem glórize, duríssimam quzstiónem, nec cessístis supplíciis, sed vobis pótius supplícia cessérunt. O quale fuit illud spectáculum Dómino, quam sublíme, quam magnum, quam accéptum! Quam letus illic Christus fuit ! quam libens in tálibus Servis suis pugnávit, et vicit! Prceliatóres atque assertóres sui nóminis eréxit, corroborávit, animávit, Et qui pro nobis mortem semel vicil, semper vincit in nobis, Hic est amon fídei nostre, qua congrédimur, qua vincimus, qua coronamur.

lessons.la: UI sunt isti, qui ut nubes volant, et quasi colúmba: ad fenéstras suas? Recte sancli Confessóres, quorum in praesénti memóriam ágimus, Nubes appelláti sunt : quia et verbis pluunt, et miráculis ac exémplis corúscant. Qui voláre quoque ut nubes dicúntur: quia in terra vivéntes, extra terram fuit omne quod egérunt. Unde et per quamdam Nubem dícitur : In carne ambulántes, non secúndum carnem militámus, Prióres enim patres conjúgiis utebántur, fílios procreábant, substántias possidébunt, curis rei familiáris intendébant. Istos autem prophétis jam spíritu prǽvidens substántias desérere, conjúgia non appétere, fílios non procreáre, nihil in terra qucrere, nihil possidére : non eos per terram velut hómines ambulántes, sed ut Nubes volántes nóminat.

resp.a: Sint lumbi vestri præcíncti, et lucernæ ardéntes in mánibus vestris
resp.b: Et vos símiles homínibus exspectántibus dóminum suum, quando revertátur a núptiis
v: Vigiláte ergo, quia nescítis qua hora Dóminus vester ventúrus sit.

lessons.la: Pur Deum femíneus étiam mílitat sexus. Multæ namque féminze ánimo viríli spiritálem milítiam gessérunt. Quædam enim interióris hóminis virtúte viros zequavérunt in agónibus Mártyrum : quædam étiam fertióres viris exstitérunt. Nam quibúsdam virórum ex ignávia mulíebri degencrántibus, illæ sexum infírmum viríli mente vicérunt, ac sic in testimónio virtútis, victrícem ponárum, viris labéntibus, constitórunt. Ex ipsis ergo sunt, quee angélicum sacræ virinitátis replent chorum. Ex ipsis et illæ sunt, quæ gloriósis præliis Confessórum et Mártyrum triúmphis corúscant.

Ibi hymnidici Angelórum chori. Ibi socíetas supernórum cívium, ibi dulcis solémnitas ómnium ab hac triste peregrinatióne ad tua E£áudia redeúntium. Ibi Prophetárum próvidus chorus, ibi duodénus Apostolórum númerus, ibi innumerabílium Mártyrum victor exércitus, ibi sanctórum Confessórum sacer convéntus, ibi veri et perfécti mónachi, ibi sanctæ mulíeres, quze voluptátes sǽculi et sexus infirmitátem vicérunt; ibi púeri et puéllae, qui annos suos sanctis móribus transcendérunt. Exsúltant omnes in própriis mansiónibus. Ii. ix.Concéde nobis, Dómine quǽsumus, véniam delictórum, et intercedéntibus — Sanctis, quorum hódie solémnia celebrámus, talem nobis tríbue devotiónem, * Ut ad eórum perveníre mereámur societátem. ℣. Dómine, qui operáti sunt justítiam, habitábunt in tabernáculo tuo, et requiéscent in monte sancto tuo. PREJAED, Hl.
Dóminus Sanctis suis notam fecit viam vitæ, et adimplévit eos lætítia cum vultu suo.
Hæc est generátio queréntium Dóminum, quzréntiim fáciem Dei Jacob.. X, Exsúltent justi in conspéctu Dei. E. Et delecténtur in lætítia. i.

lessons.la: Hómines dívites in virtúte, pulchritúdinis — stúdium habéntes, pacificántes in dómibus suis. Omnes isti in generatiónibus gentis suæ glóriam adépti sunt, et in diébus suis habéntur in láudibus. Qui de illis nati sunt, reliquérunt nomen narrándi laudes eórum: t sunt quorum non est memória: periérunt quasi qui non fúerint: et nati sunt quasi non nati, et fílii ipsórum cum ipsis. HK. ii Hæc est vera fratérnitas, quee nunquam pótuit violári certámine qui effúso sánguine secúti sunt, Dóminum * Contemnéntes aulam régiam Pervenérunt ad regna cæléstia. Ecce merces sanctórum copiósa est apud Deum, et vivent in ætérnum — Cantemnéntes aulam régiam.
lessons.en: Rich men in virtue, studying beautifulness: living at peace in their houses. All these have gained glory in their generations, and were praised in their days. They that were born of them have left a name behind them, that their praises might be related: And there are some, of whom there is no memorial: who are perished, as if they had never been: and are become as if they had never been born, and their children with them. But these were men of mercy, whose godly deeds have not failed: Their posterity are a holy inheritance, and their seed hath stood in the covenants. And their children for their sakes remain for ever: their seed and their glory shall not be forsaken.

lessons.la: Ed illi viri misericórdiæ sunt, quorum pietátes non defuérunt: cum sémine eórum pérmanent bona, heréditas sancta nepótes eórum, et in testaméntis stetit semen eónem, Sapiéntiam ipsórum nar rent pópuli, et laudem eórum núntiet ecclésia.

resp.a: Sacerdótes Dei, benedícite Dóminum
resp.b: Sancti et húmiles corde, laudáte Deum.
v: Spíritus et ánimæ justórum hymnum dícite Deo nostro

lessons.la: jur Sanctorum merita religiosa caritate miratur, quique justorum glorias fttquénti laude colloquitur, eorum mores sanctos atque justitiam imitetur: quoniam quem delectat Sancti alicujus meritum, delectare debet par circa cultum Dei obsequium. Quare aut imitari debet, si laudat: aut laudare non debet, si imitari detrectat: ut qui alium laudat, laudabilem se reddat: et qui Sanctorum merita admiratur, mirabilis ipse vitæ sanctitate reddatur. Nam si propterea justos fidelesque diligimus, quod in ipsis justitiam fidemque — suspicimus, possumus nos quoque esse quod sunt, si faciamus ipsi quod faciunt.
lessons.en: From the Sermons of St. John Chrysostom, (Patriarch of Constantinople.) He that wondereth with reverential love at the mighty deeds of the holy, he that hath oftentimes on his tongue praises for the glory of the righteous, let such an one copy their holy lives and their righteousness; for if any take pleasure in the work of a Saint, he ought to take pleasure in serving God as that Saint served Him. If he praiseth the Saint, he ought to imitate him, and if he is not ready to imitate him, he ought not to praise him. Let him that praiseth another make himself worthy of a like praise, and if he be in admiration of the Saints, let his own admirable life reflect the holiness of theirs. If we love the good and leal because they are good and leal, let us not forget that we can be what they are, by doing as they did.

resp.a: Isti sunt virisancti,quos elégit Dóminus in caritáte non sita, et dedit illis glóriam sempitérnam
resp.b: Quorum doctrína fulget Ecclésia, ut sole luna.
v: In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum, et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.

lessons.la: A? hanc igitur operum salutarium delectet nos pervenire palmam. Libenter ac prompte certemus, omnes in agone justitiæ Deo et Christo spectante curramus; et qui Século et mundo majores esse jam cœpimus, cursum nostrum nulla sæculi cupiditate tardemus. Si expeditos, si celeres in operis agone currentes dies nos ultimus invenerit, nusquam Dominus meritis nostris deerit remunerator.
lessons.en: From the Sermons of the Venerable Bede, Priest (at Jarrow.) Therefore, may it be our delight to go on unto this prize of good living. Freely and cheerfully let us strive in the race, running under the eyes of God and of Christ. We have already taken a station above floating and earthly things, and let us allow no love for things fleeting to hamper our running. If the last day shall find us lithe and speedful in the race of good living, we shall never have to complain that our Master is a scanty rewarder of our works.

resp.a: Propter testamentum Domini et leges paternas, Sancti Dei perstiterunt in amóre fraternitatis:
resp.b: Quia unus fuit spiritus in eis, et una fides.
v: Ecce quam bonum et quam jucundum habitare fratres in unum!

lessons.la: UAPROPTER, carissimi, Q mente integra, fide firma, virtute robusta, caritate perfecta, parati ad omnem voluntatem Dei simus, conservantes fortiter Dominica mandata, in simplicitate innocentiam, in caritate concordiam, modestiam in humilitate, diligentiam in administratione, vigilantiam in adjuvandis laborantibus, misericordiam in fovendis pauperibus, in defendenda veritate constantiam, in disciplinæ severitate censuram, ne aliquid ad exemplum bonorum factorum desit in nobis. Hæc sunt enim vestigia quæ nobis Sancti quique revertentes in patriam reliquerunt, ut illorum semitis inhærentes, sequeremur et In gáudia. KR. vi Hi, qui amícti sunt stolis albis, qui sunt? et unde venérunt? Hi sunt, qui lavérunt stolas suas, et dealbavérunt eas * in sánguine Agni. Ídeo sunt ante thronum Dei, et sérviunt ei die ac nocte in templo ejus. — In sánguine Agni. Glória. Insánguine Agni.

head: Cap. 31.
lessons.la: Infántia mea crevit mecum miserátio, et de útero matris mec egréssa est mecum: si despéxi pereúntem, eo quod non habúerit induméntum, et absque operiménto páuperem: si non benedixérunt mihi látera ejus, et de velléribus óvium meárum calefáctus est: si levávi super pupíllum manum — meam, étiam cum vidérem me in porta superiórem: húmerus meus a junctúra sua cadat, et bráchium meum cum suis óssibus confringátur.
lessons.en: (For from my infancy mercy grew up with me: and it came out with me from my mother’s womb:) If I have despised him that was perishing for want of clothing, and the poor man that had no covering: If his sides have not blessed me, and if he were not warmed with the fleece of my sheep: If I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, even when I saw myself superior in the gate: Let my shoulder fall from its joint, and let my arm with its bones be broken.

resp.a: Hic est Martínus, eléctus Dei Póntifex, cui Dóminus post Apóstolos tantam grátiam conférre dignátus est,
resp.b: Ut in virtúte Trinitátis Deíficæ mererétur fíeri trium mortuórum suscitátor magníficus.
v: Sanctæ Trinitátis fidem Martínus conféssus est.

lessons.la: Semper enim quasi tuméntes super me fluctus tímui Deum, et pondus ejus ferre non pótui. Si putávi aurum robur meum, ct obrízo dixi: Fidúcia mea. Si Izetátus sum super multis divítiis meis, et quia plúrima réperit manus mum.
lessons.en: For I have always feared God as waves swelling over me, and his weight I was not able to bear. If I have thought gold my strength, and have said to fine gold: My confidence: If I have rejoiced over my great riches, and because my hand had gotten much.

lessons.la: I gavísus sum ad ruínam ejus qui me óderat, et exsultávi quod invenísset eum malum. Non enim dedi ad peccándum guttur meum, ut expéterem maledícens ánimam ejus. Si non dixérunt viri tabernáculi mei: Quis det de cárnibus ejus ut saturémur? Foris non mansit peregrínus, óstium meum viatóri pátuit.
lessons.en: If I have been glad at the downfall of him that hated me, and have rejoiced that evil had found him. For I have not given my mouth to sin, by wishing a curse to his soul. If the men of my tabernacle have not said: Who will give us of his flesh that we may be filled? The stranger did not stay without, my door was open to the traveller.

Lucérna enim fides est, juxta quod scriptum est: Lucérna pédibus meis verbum tuum, Dómine. Verbum enim Dei fides nostra est; Verbum Dei lux est; Lucérna est fides: Erat Lux vera, qua illúminat omnem hóminem veniéntem in hunc mundum. Lucérna autem lucére non potest, nisi aliúnde lumen accéperit.

Nemo ergo fidem sub lege constítuat; lex enim intra mensúram est, ultra mensúram grátia; lex obúmbrat, grátia claríficat. Et ídeo nemo fidem suam intra mensúram legis inchidat, sed ad Ecclésiam cónferat, in qua septifórmis Spíritus relúcet grátia, quam Princeps ille sacerdótum fulgóre supérnæ divinitátis illúminat, ne eam legis umbra restínguat.

Illa autem Jerúsalem quæ in cælo est, in qua mílitat fides nostra, in illo altíssimo ómnium locáta monte, hoc est in Christo, non potest ténebris hujus mundi abscóndi; sed fulgens candóre Solis ætérni, luce nos spiritális Grátiæ illúminat.

head: Cap. 21.
lessons.la: E sústulit me in spíritu in montem magnum, et altum, et osténdit mihi civitátem sanctam Jerúsalem descendéntem de cælo a Deo, habéntem claritátem Dei: et lumen ejus símile lápidi pretióso tamquam lápidi jáspidis, sicut crystállum. Et habébat murum magnum, et altum, habéntem portas duódecim: et in portis ángelos duódecim, et nómina inscrípta, qua sunt nómina duódecim tríbuum filiórum Israël.
lessons.en: And he took me up in spirit to a great and high mountain: and he shewed me the holy city Jerusalem coming down out of heaven from God, Having the glory of God, and the light thereof was like to a precious stone, as to the jasper stone, even as crystal. And it had a wall great and high, having twelve gates, and in the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.

resp.a: In dedicatióne templi decantábat pópulus laudem
resp.b: Et in ore eórum dulcis resonábat sonus.
v: Obtulérunt sacrificium super altáre Dómini: et cecidérunt in fácies suas et adoravérunt eum.

lessons.la: T erat structúra muri ejus ex lápide jáspide: ipsa vero cívitas aurum mundum símile vitro mundo. Et fundaménta muri civitátis omni lápide pretióso ornáta. Fundaméntum primum, jaspis: secúndum, sapphírus: tértium, chalcedónius: quartum, smarágdus: quintum, sardónyx: sextum, sárdius: séptimum, chrysólithus: octávum, berýllus: nonum, topázius: décimum, chrysóprasus: undécimum, hyacínthus: duodécimum, amethýstus. HN. ii Fundáta est, domus Dómini super vérticem móntium, et exaltáta est super omnes colles Et vénient ad eam omnes gentes, * et dicent: Glória tibi Dómine, Veniéntes autem vénient cum exsultatióne, portántes manípulos suos, — Et dicent: Glória tibi Dómine.
lessons.en: And the building of the wall thereof was of jasper stone: but the city itself pure gold, like to clear glass. And the foundations of the wall of the city were adorned with all manner of precious stones. The first foundation was jasper: the second, sapphire: the third, a chalcedony: the fourth, an emerald: The fifth, sardonyx: the sixth, sardius: the seventh, chrysolite: the eighth, beryl: the ninth, a topaz: the tenth, a chrysoprasus: the eleventh, a jacinth: the twelfth, an amethyst. And I saw no temple therein. For the Lord God Almighty is the temple thereof, and the Lamb. And the city hath no need of the sun, nor of the moon, to shine in it. For the glory of God hath enlightened it, and the Lamb is the lamp thereof. And the nations shall walk in the light of it: and the kings of the earth shall bring their glory and honour into it. There shall not enter into it any thing defiled, or that worketh abomination or maketh a lie, but they that are written in the book of life of the Lamb. And he shewed me a river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding from the throne of God and of the Lamb.

lessons.la: I gwenem Portæ, duódecim margarítæ sunt, per síngulas: et síngulæ portæ erant ex síngulis margarítis: et plátea civitátis aurum mundum, tamquam vitrum perlúcidum. Et templum non vidi in ea: Dóminus enim Deus omnípotens templum illíus est, et Agnus. Et cívitas non eget sole, neque luna ut lúceant in ea: nam cláritas Dei illuminávit eam, et lucérna ejus est Agnus. ky dio Mane surgens Jacob erigébat lápidem in títulum, fundens óleum désuper votum vovit Dómino * Vere locus iste sanctus est, et ego nesciébam. Vidit Jacob scalam, súmmitas ejus cælos tangébat, Et descendéntes Angelos, et ait, — Vere locus iste sanctus est et ego nesciébam. Glória. Et ego nesciébam.
lessons.en: And the twelve gates are twelve pearls, one to each: and every several gate was of one several pearl. And the street of the city was pure gold, as it were transparent glass. And I saw no temple therein. For the Lord God Almighty is the temple thereof, and the Lamb. And the city hath no need of the sun, nor of the moon, to shine in it. For the glory of God hath enlightened it, and the Lamb is the lamp thereof. And the nations shall walk in the light of it: and the kings of the earth shall bring their glory and honour into it. And the gates thereof shall not be shut by day: for there shall be no night there. And they shall bring the glory and honour of the nations into it. There shall not enter into it any thing defiled, or that worketh abomination or maketh a lie, but they that are written in the book of life of the Lamb. And he shewed me a river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding from the throne of God and of the Lamb.

lessons.la: ITUS, quos in consecrándis ecclésiis et altáribus Romána servat Ecclésia, beátus Silvéster Papa primus instítuit. Nam, etsi jam ab Apostolórum témpore loca fuérunt Deo dicáta, quæ a quibúsdam oratória, ab áliis Ecclésia gi. cebántur, ubi colléctæ fiébant per unam sábbati, et christiánus pópulus oráre, Dei verbum audíre et Eucharístiam si. mere sólitus erat; non tamen illa ádeo solémni ritu consecrabántur, nec in eis adhuc in títulum eréctum erat altáre, quod chrísmate delibútum, Dómini nostri Jesu Christi, qui altáre, hóstia et sacérdos no. ster est, figúram exprímeret.
lessons.en: The Rites whereof the Church of Rome maketh use for the hallowing of Churches and Altars were first instituted by the blessed Pope Sylvester. From the very time of the Apostles there had been places set apart for God, where assemblies took place upon the first day of every week, and where the Christians were used to pray, to hear the word of God, and to receive the Eucharist, which places were by some called Oratories and by others Churches. But these places were not dedicated with so solemn a form, nor did they set up therein an Altar for a pillar, and pour chrism thereon, (Gen. xxviii. 18,) for a figure of our Lord Jesus Christ, Who is Himself our Altar, our Victim, and our Priest.

resp.a: Bénedic, Dómine, do. mum istam, quam ædificávi nómini tuo: veniéntium in locum istum— Exáudi preces in excélso sólio glóriæ tuæ
v: Dómine, si convérsus fúerit pópulus tuus, et oráverit ad sanctuárium tuum. — Exáudi preces.

lessons.la: Ed ubi Constantínus imperátor per baptísmi sacraméntum sanitátem salutémque consecútus est, tum primum lege ah eo lata concéssum est toto orbe terrárum, Christiáni ut ecclésias ædificárent; quos ille, non solum edícto, sed étiam exémplo ad sacram ædificatiónem est cohortátus. Nam, et in suo Lateranénsi palátio ecclésiam Salvatóri dedicávit, et ei continéntem basílicam nómine sancti Joánnis Baptístæ cóndidit, eo loco quo ipse, baptizátus a sancto Silvéstro, a lepra mundátus est; quam idem — Póntifex — consecrávit quinto idus novémbris. Cujus consecratiónis memória celebrátur hodiérno die, quo primum Romæ públice ecclésia consecráta est, et imágo Salvatóris, in paríete depícta, pópulo Románo appáruit.
lessons.en: But when the Emperor Constantine had by the Sacrament of Baptism received health both of body and soul, then first in a law by him published was it allowed to the Christians throughout the whole world to build Churches, to the which holy building he exhorted them by his example as well as by his decree. He dedicated in his own Lateran Palace a Church to the Saviour, and built hard by it a Cathedral in the name of St. John the Baptist, upon the place where he had been baptized by holy Sylvester and cleansed from his leprosy. This Cathedral was hallowed by the said Pope upon the 9th day of November. It is this consecration, the memory whereof is still celebrated upon this day, the first whereon the public consecration of a Church ever took place in Rome, and the image of the Saviour was seen by the Roman people painted upon the wall.

lessons.la: vop si beátus Silvéster póstea in consecratióne altáris Príncipis Apostolórum decrévit ut deínceps nisi ex lápide altária non ædificaréntur; tamen basílicæ Lateranénsis altáre fuit e ligno eréctum. Quod mirum non est; nam, cum a sancto Petro usque ad Silvéstrum, propter persecutiónes, Pontífices certo loco consístere non possent, quocúmque eos necéssitas compulísset, sive in cryptas, sive in cœmetéria, sive in ædes piórum, super illo altári lígneo ad arcæ similitúdinem cóncavo, sacra faciébant. Quo altári sanctus Silvéster, réddita Ecclésiæ pace, honóris causa Príncipis Apostolórum, qui in illo sacrificásse dícitur, et reliquórum Pontíficum, qui usque ad id tempus ad mystéria conficiénda eo usi fúerant, in Lateranénsi prima ecclésia collocáto, sancívit ne quisquam in eo, præter Románum Pontíficem, Missam deínceps celebráret. Eámdem Ecclésiam incéndiis, vastatiónibus, terræ ínsuper mótibus disjéctam cversámque, ac sédula Summórum Pontificum cura reparátam, nova póstmodum molitióne restitútam, Benedíctus Décimus tértius Póntifex Máximus, Ordinis Praedicatorum, die vigésima octáva Aprílis anni millésimi: septingentésimi vigésimi sexti, ritu solémni consecrávit, ejúsque celebritá tis memériam hac die recoléndam státuit.

lessons.la: DENS Hispanus, ex Óppi do sancti Nicolai de Portu diœcesis Hispalénsis, ab ineunte ætate, pii sub sacerdotis disciplína, sanctioris vitas solitaria in ecclésia, tirocinium exercuit. Deínde, ut firmius Deo se conjungeret, in convéntu de Arizzáfa fratrum Minórum quos Observántes vocant sancti Francisci regulam in statu laicali proféssus est. Magna ibi alacritate húmilis obediéntiæ et regularis observantiæ jugum subiens, contemplatióni in primis déditus, mira Dei luce perfundebátur, adeo ut de rebus cæléstibus, litterárum expers, mirándum in modum et plane divinitus loquerétur.
lessons.en: Diego was a Spaniard, and was born at the little town of San Nicola-del-Porto, in the diocese of Seville. From his childhood he learnt the more holy life under a godly Priest, (who lived hermit) in a lonely Church, and so served his apprenticeship. Afterwards, being fain to be more utterly God's only, he professed himself as a lay brother under the Rule of St. Francis in the convent of the Friars Minor, called Observant, of Arrizafa. There he cheerfully bore the yoke of the lowliest obedience and the strictest observance. He was much given to contemplation, and a wonderful light from God shone in him, so that, though he was untaught, he could speak touching heavenly things strangely and as it were supernaturally.

lessons.la: Canariis in insulis, ubi frátribus sui ordinis præfuit, multa perpéssus, martyrii æstuans desidério, plures infidéles verbo et exemplo ad Christi fidem convértit. Romam veniens anno jubilæi, Nicolao quinto Pontifice, ægrotórum curæ in convéntu Arecmli destinátus, eo caritátis afféctu munus hoc exercuit, ut, Urbe annonæ inópia laborante, ægrotis tamen, quorum aliquándo úlcera étiam lambéndo abstergebat, nihil pénitus necessarii defécerit. Eximia quoque fides et grátia curatiónum n eo eluxit, cum imáginem Die Xiv. Novémbris. Hu, Joánnis Lincii. lámpadis, quæ collucebat ante Die Xiv. Novémbris, beatíssime— Dei B. Joánnis Lincii Genitrícis, quam summa devo Conf. Ord. PRJED. tióne colebat, oleo ægros inún Duplex. Oratio. gens, signo crucis impresso, multórum morbos mirabíliter sanaverit.

Demum, Complúti finem sibi D vitæ adesse intélligens, lácera et obsoleta indútus tú: nica, conjectis in crucem óculis, singulari devotióne illis verbis ex sacro hymno pronuntiátis: Dulce lignum, dulces clavos, dulcia ferens póndera, quæ fuísti digna portare Regem cælórum et Dóminum, ánimam Deo réddidit pridie y Idus Novembris, anno Dómini supra millesimum quadringentésimo sexagesimo tertio. Ejus corpus, cum menses non paucos ut pio confluéntium desidério fieret satis insepúltum mansísset, quasi jam incorruptiónem indúerit, odórem suavíssimum efflávit. Illum, multis et illustribus miraculis clarum, Sixtus quintus, Pontifex maximus, Sanctórum número adscripsit.
lessons.en: He was at Alcala when he understood that the end of his life was at hand. Clothed in a ragged cast-away habit, he fixed his eyes upon the Cross, and said with extraordinary earnestness 'Sweet the nails, and sweet the iron, Sweet the Weight That hung on thee,' thou that wast chosen to up-bear the Lord, the King of heaven, and so he gave up his soul to God, upon the 12th day of November, in the year of our Lord 1463. To satisfy the godly wishes of the multitude, his body was kept unburied for not a few months, and lay in a right sweet savour, as though the corruptible had already put on incorruption. He was famous for many and great miracles, and Pope Sixtus V. enrolled him in the number of the Saints.

lessons.la: Jannes Líccius Cáccabi, quod est Sicíliæ óppidum in ^anormitána dicecési húmili génere natus est. Seméstrem infántulum matre orbátum, ac nutríce ob patris inópiam destitútum, cum solo mali punici succo alerétur, inédia fere conféctum, pia múlier lactándum suscépit : dum autem viro suo, diutúrna membrórum contractióne in lecto jacénti, admovisset, is repénte conváluit. A púero, jugi oratióne, crebris Jejúniis et carnis maceratióne sese impénse exercébat, Pubertátem vero egréssus, Panórmum dedúctus est, ubi, suadénte Petro Jeremía sanctitáte claro, Przedicatórum Órdinem, quem ille profitebátur, ampléxus est, positóque virtútum ómnium tirocínio, solémnibus votis árctius sese Deo conjúnxit, Sacris mox lítteris. diligentíssime excúltus, apostólico múneri designátus est; quod tanta súbiit eloquénti; divínæ vi, ut vel e sáxeis ,córdibus lácrimas pisi compunctiónis eliceret.

FFUSUS in ómnia erga próximos caritátis offícia, ómnium ánimos ad se rapiébat, Kem divínam non sine ingénti lacrimárum vi fervideeque devotiónis astu faciébat. Præcípua in Deíparam Vírginem pietáte ac religióne fuit : ejúsque Rosárii cultum insigniter auxit ac propagávit. Cáccabi ccenóbium sui Ordinis loco sibi cǽlitus indicáto molítus, matériam óperi perficiéndo parátam divínitus hábuit. Calcáriam fornácem bíduo accénsam, et jamjam ruitúram, quo ejus casum reparáret, ingréssus, inde exívitillzesus. Aquam vero, eo loci scaténtem atque exundántem, oratióne exsiccávit, absolutóque zedifício, rursum edúxit, przesentiíssimum deínceps áccolis advérsus quoscúmque morbos remédium.

lessons.gospel: *ENOBIO a se constrúcto diu præfuit Superiórum nutu ac voluntáte, Siculámque Praedicatórum provínciam severióris disciplínas zelo, cum summa prudéntia et caritáte conjúncto, sanctíssime administrávit. Dénique, provécta ad annos fere úndecim supra centum zetáte, millésimo quingeutésimo undécimo, mense Novémbri, inter Crucifíxi ampléxus ferventísque caritátis actus, placidíssime excéssit. Ad ejus corpus tríduo insepúltum incredíbilis fuit hóminum concúrsus, ob sancti Viri famam celebritatémque, novis multísque miráculis auctam. Religiósum jam tum eídem adhíbitum cultum, ad hæc usque témpora constánter propagátum,sacraRituum Congregátio probávit : ejúsque Officium et Missam ab univérso Praedicatórum Ordine et Panormitánz Ecclésize Clero Benedíctus Décimus quartus Póntifex Máximus celebrári concéssit, In Ii. Nocturno.

head: Cap. 39.
lessons.la: Sapiéntiam ómnium antiquórum exquíret sápiens, t in prophétis vacábit. Narratiónem virórum nominatórum conservábit, et in versútias parabolárum simul introíbit. OccáHa proverbiórum exquíret, et in abscónditis parabolárum conversábitur. In médio magnatórum ministrábit, et in conspéctu prǽsidis apparébit. In terram alienigenárum géntium pertránsiet: bona enim et mala in homínibus tentábit.
lessons.en: The wise men will seek out the wisdom of all the ancients, and will be occupied in the prophets. He will keep the sayings of renowned men, and will enter withal into the subtilties of parables. He will search out the hidden meanings of proverbs, and will be conversant in the secrets of parables. He shall serve among great men, and: appear before the governor. He shall pass into strange countries: for he shall try good and evil among men.

lessons.la: or suum tradet ad vigilánC dum dilúculo ad Dóminum, qui fecit illum, et in conspéctu Altíssimi deprecábitur. Apériet os suum in oratióne, et pro delíctis suis deprecábitur. Si enim Dóminus magnus volúerit, spíritu intelligéntiæ replébit illum: et ipse tamquam imbres mittet elóquia sapiéntiæ suæ, et in oratióne confitébitur Dómino: et ipse díriget consílium ejus, et disciplínam, et in abscónditis suis consiliábitur.
lessons.en: He will give his heart to resort early to the Lord that made him, and he will pray in the sight of the most High. He will open his mouth in prayer, and will make supplication for his sins. For if it shall please the great Lord, he will fill him with the spirit of understanding: And he will pour forth the words of his wisdom as showers, and in his prayer he will confess to the Lord. And he shall direct his counsel, and his knowledge, and in his secrets shall he meditate.

lessons.la: I. Palam fáciet disciplínam doctrínæ suæ, et in lege testaménti Dómini gloriábitur. Collaudábunt multi sapiéntiam ejus, et usque in sǽculum non delébitur. Non recédet memória ejus, et nomen ejus requirétur a generatióne in generatiónem. Sapiéntiam ejus enarrábunt gentes, et laudem ejus enuntiábit ecclésia. Si permánserit, nomen derelínquet plus quam mille: et si requiéverit, próderit illi.
lessons.en: He shall shew forth the discipline he hath learned, and shall glory in the law of the covenant of the Lord. Many shall praise his wisdom, and it shall never be forgotten. The memory of him shall not depart away, and his name shall be in request from generation to generation. Nations shall declare his wisdom, and the church shall shew forth his praise. If he continue, he shall leave a name above a thousand: and if he rest, it shall be to his advantage.

lessons.la: LUERTUS, ob singulárem eruditiónem cognoménto Magnus, natióne Suévus, ab infántia Deíparze Vírgini devoUssimus fuit, ex cujus étiam consílio Órdinem ' Fratrum Preedicatérum intráre constítuit, Verum ob várias dzemohi5 artes mutáto deínceps propósito, illud idem venerábilis Patris Jordáni mónitis adhorlationibúsque resúmpsit. Missus deínde Colóniam Agrippínam, ut philosophiae óperam daret, cum ob ingénii hebetúdinem condiscípulis suis esset inférior, id moléste ferens, Órdinem, quem nondum proféssus erat, desérere constítuit. At calésti visióne confirmátus, impetratáque | Deíparæ Vírginis ope, philosophiae sciéntia ádeo brevi témpore , profécit, ut vulgo Philósophus appellarétur.

N'TEREA assiduis précibus Dei Matrem obsecrábat, ut ,in fide confirmarétur : ne forte captiósis philosophórum ratiónibus illaqueátus, de divínis mystériis dubitáret. Votis ánnuit benigníssima Patróna. Ei quippe conspícuam se przbens : Sapiéntize, inquit, stú- | dio incúmbe : at ne te in fide vacilláre contíngat, ars omnis syllogística ante mortem a te auferétur. Signo autem erit id brevi esse futúrum, quod ,in lectióne pública memoáóriz 'Lapsum aliquándo —patiérc. Parísios póstea missus, tanto auditórum conceúrsu libros Sententiárum expósuit, ut discípulos schola non cáperet. Quare in platéa pública docére compúlsus est, quæ ob id Magístri Albérti platéa etiám- : num hódie nuncupátur.

OLONIAM inde revérsus, sanctum Thomam Aquinátem discípulum hábuit, cujus futúram doctrínam exímiam prophético spíritu prædíxit. Humilitáte 4c paupertáte potíssimum excélluit. Ab Urbánao Quarto Romam vocátus, Ratisbonénsi Ecclésie Epíscopus datus est. Guillélmum — Religiósi status impugnatórem fudit : erróres vários in concílio Lugdunénsi confutávit, Post dimissum Épiscopátum, dum annum áágeret octogésimum tértium, Colónize in pública lectióne memóriaze lapsum passus est : unde immincéntem óbitus sui diem przenóvit. Ac tandem compléto octogésimo séptimo, migrávit ad Dóminum, anno Salútis millésimo ducentésimo octogésimo.

EVERAN prióris vitzeratiónem matrimónio juncta neque emólliit neque intermísit. Oratiónibus, jejúniis, vigíliis aliísque afllictatiónibus carnem miblandiéntem mundum etúdere, | réfice súbigens, jugi Comme et persequéntem superáre fe-;niónis eucharísticæ usu spiricisti : da ut ejus intercessióne tum reficiébat. Sǽculi luxum et exémplo nec terrénis vin-; vanitatésque perósa, pretiósis cámur illécebris, nec ullis aran- ; véstibus in páuperes, quos exigáámur advérsis. Per eúmdem. In I. Nocturno. Lectiones De virgínibus. de Communi uníus Vírginis non Mártyris, pag. 98*. In Il. Nocturno.

Ulla Narniénsis, nóbili &énére orta, prophetíæ donum pietatémque cum lacte suxisse visa est. Nam adhuc: mia caritáte complectebátur, distribútis, vilióribus utebátur, ad ínfima abjectiónis offícia ultro libénsque sese demittens. Diutúrnas ac gravesdsemonum moléstias patientíssime tulit ac fregit. Ab ipso sponso dúrius hábita arctóque cárccere aliquándo reclúsa, vitæ innocéntia atque constántia id demum obtínuit, ut ab Pe Sejungerétur, Quare hábitu Tértit Ordinis Praedicatorum devóte suscépto, Romam profécta, inde Vitérbium a Superióribus missa, sacris ibídem Stigmátibus, iisdémque conspicuis ac cruéntis, a Christo Dómino mirabíliter insigníta est. A a.

lessons.homily_head: Homilía in Evangelium Símíle erit regnum czelórum decem virgínibus.
lessons.gospel: ESTAURATA Vitérbii apud Be Ordinis sanctimoniáles regulári disciplína, adniténte Hércule Primo Ferrárize duce, ad eam civitátem Summi Pontíficis jussu migrávit : ubi constrúcto sub invocatióne sanctæ Catharínæ Senénsis ampliíssimo monastério, instituéndis nobílibus puéllis dirigendísque sacris virgínibus, summa caritáte, prudéntia ac virilántia diu przefécta est, Hóminum calúmniis, injúriis, contuméliis ac derisiónibus per annos trigínta et octo, variisque morbórum cruciátibus probáta, sepius tamen cléstibus recreáta visiónibus, migrávit ad Sponsum,anno milléstmo quingentésimo quadragésimo quarto, cetátis vero suze sexagésimo. Ejus corpus Ferráriz, adhuc incorrúptum sacrorúmque Stígmatum cicatrícibus in to Copspícuis, anno millésimo septingentésimo décimo repértum est, cúm ex eo decisum crus ad civitátem Narniénsem translátum est, ubi magnífico sacéllo excéptum, religiosíssime cólitur. Beátae Luciae cultum Clemens Undécimus approbávit : ejus vero festum cum Offício et Missa uníus Vírginis in univérso Praedicatórum Ordine atque a Clero Narniénsi, Viterbiénsi et Ferrariénsi Benedíctus Décimus tértius celebrári concéssit. In Iii. Nocturno.

lessons.la: REGORIUS, Neocasárese G Ponti epíscopus, sanctitáte doctrinaque — illustris, signis vero ac miraculis multo illustrior, quorum multitúdine atque præstántia Thaumatúrgus appellátus esl, et sancti Basilíi testimonio cum Móyse, Prophetis et Apóstolis comparátus; montem, qui ecclésiæ edificatiónemimpediébat, oratióne álio tránstulit. Item palúdem, inter fratres causam discordiárum, exsiccávit. Lycum fluvium, perniciose agros inundántem, defixo ad ripam quo sustentabátur baculo, qui statim virentem crevit in árborem, coércuit, ut póstea ultra eum terminum non efflúxerit.
lessons.en: Gregory, Archbishop of Neo-Caesarea, in Pontus, is famous indeed for his holiness and doctrine, but much more so on account of the signs and wonders which he wrought, the number and character of which were so extraordinary that they have gotten him the name of Thaumatourgos, (which is, being interpreted from the Greek, the Wonderworker.) Holy Basil compareth him with Moses, with the Prophets, and with the Apostles, and testifieth that by his prayers he moved a mountain that stood in the way of the building of a Church. Moreover, he dried up a marsh, which was a cause of strife between brothers. Also, when the River Lycus overflowed and wasted the fields, he set his walking-stick on the bank, ~(which stick forthwith grew into a green tree,) and confined the stream within its bed, so that it never more passed that place again.

lessons.la: Sæpíssime dæmones ex idolórum simulacris atque ex hóminum corpóribus ejécit, múltaque alia mirabíliter effécit, quibus innumerábiles hómines traxit ad Jesu Christi fidem, cum étiam prophetico spíritu futura prædiceret. Qui, migratúrus e vita, cum quæsísset quot in civitáte Neocæsariénsi réliqui essent infidéles, responsumque esset tantum esse septemdecim; Deo grátias agens, Tótidem, inquit, erant fidéles, cum cepi episcopátum. Plura scripsit, quibus etiam, non solum miraculis, Dei Ecclésiam illustrávit.
lessons.en: He oftentimes cast out devils either from heathen idols or from the bodies of men, and did many other marvelous things, whereby he drew countless numbers to believe in Jesus Christ. Also he had the spirit of prophecy, and foretold things to come. When he was at the point of death, he asked how many unbelievers were left in the city of Neo-Caesarea? and when they answered Seventeen, he gave God thanks, and said: Just so many were the faithful when I took the Bishopric. He wrote a great deal, whereby, as well as by his wonders, he hath enlightened the Church of God.

lessons.la: EATI Patris Gregórii merita jam in tuto posita secúri magnificémus; qui, gubernaculum fidei viríliter tenens, ánchoram spei tranquilla jam in statióne compósuit, et plenam cæléstibus divítiis et ætérnis mercibus navem optáta in litore collocávit. Qui, contra omnes adversarios, scutum timoris Dei tamdiu, infatigabíliter ténuit, donec ad victoriam perveníret. Quid enim fuit totus vitæ illíus cursus, nisi uníus cum vígili hoste conflictus?
lessons.en: From the Sermons of St. Maximus, Bishop (of Turin.) Our blessed Father Gregory is safe now, and we may safely praise his great deeds. He that kept such a manful hand upon the tiller of faith, hath now cast the anchor of hope in moorings of great calm, and brought his ship, heavy laden with heavenly riches and everlasting merchandise, safe into the haven where he would be. Thus fareth it now with him who never fainted, but for so long time held up ever the shield of the fear of God against all that did beset him. What was his whole life but one long fight against an enemy that never slept?

head: Cap. ll.
lessons.homily_head: Homilía venerábilis Bedæ Presbýteri, (Lib.
lessons.gospel: In illo témpore: Respóndens Jesus discípulis suis ait illis: Habéte fidem Dei. Amen dico vobis quia quicúmque díxerit huic monti: Tóllere et míttere in mare, et non hæsitáverit in corde suo, sed credíderit quia quodcúmque díxerit fiat, fiet ei. Et réliqua.
lessons.la: s. Comm. in Marc, cap. ll. Olent Gentiles qui contra Ecclésiam maledicta scri. psére, improperare nostris quod non habúerint plenam fidem Dei, quia nunquam montes transferre potúerint. Qui. bus respondéndum est non ómnia scripta esse, Qua in Ecclésia sunt gesta, sicut étiam de factis ipsíus Christi ct Dómini nostri Scriptúra testátur. Unde et hoc quoque fíeri potuísset, ut mons ablátus de terra mitterétur in mare, si necessitas id fíeri poposcísset. Quómodo légimus factum precibus beáti Patris Gregórii, Neocæsaréæ Ponti antístitis, viri meritis et virtútibus exímii, ut mons in terra tantum loco cederet quantum íncolæ civitátis opus habebant.

Um enim, volens ædificáre ecclésiam in loco apto, vidéret eum angustiórem esse quam res exigébat, eo quod ex una parte, rupe maris, ex alia, monte próximo coarctarétur; venit nocte ad locum, et, genibus flexis, admonuit Dóminum promissiónis suæ, ut montem longius juxta fidem petentis ágeret. Et, mane facto, reversus invénit montem tantum spatii reliquisse structóribus ecclési: e quantum opus habuerant. Poterat ergo hic, poterat alius quis ejusdem meriti vir, si opportunitas exégit set, impetrare a Dómino, mérito fidei, ut étiam mons tollerétur et mitterétur in mare.
lessons.en: Gregory was wishful to build a Church in a meet place, but the site was too narrow, being wedged in between a mountain on the one side and a precipice going down into the sea on the other. He came therefore by night to the place, kneeling down, and reminding the Lord of His promise, and calling upon Him to remove the mountain. And in the morning, when he came thither again, he found that the mountain had been removed back, and as much room left for the builders of the Church as they needed. This man therefore would have been able, and any other man of like grace would have been able, if need were, to obtain of the Lord, by the force of his faith, that even a mountain should be removed, and be cast into the sea.

lessons.la: ERUM quia montis nómine nonnúnquam diabolus significátur, videlicet propter supérbiam, qua se contra Deum erigit, et esse vult símilis Altíssimo; mons ad præcéptum eórum qui fortes fide sunt, tollitur de terra et in mare projícitur, cum, preedi cántibus verbum doctóribus sanctis, immundus spíritus ab eórum corde repéllitur qui ad vitam sunt præordináti, et in turbulentis amarisque infidelium méntibus ve.
lessons.en: Mystically, however, by a mountain is sometimes signified the devil, on account of the pride whereby he lifteth himself up against God, and would fain be like unto the Most High. And when holy teachers, strong in faith, do preach the Word, this mountain is removed, and cast into the sea, that is to say, the unclean spirit is removed out of the hearts of such as are foreordained unto eternal life, and sent free to exercise the wild rage of his tyranny in the riotous and embittered minds of the unfaithful.

lessons.la: zi ORRO Vaticanam basilicam, vetustáte jampridem collabentem, ac proptérea multórum Pontificum pietáte latius ac magnificentius a fundamentis erectam, Urbanus octavus, hac eádem recurrénte die anni millesimi sexcentésimi vigesimi sexti, solemni ritu consecrávit. Basilicam — vero Ostiensem, cum dira incendii vis anno millesimo octingentésimo vigesimo tertio penitus consumpsísset, indefessa quatuor Pontificum cura splendidius quam antea erectam, et ab intéritu véluti vindicátum, Pius nonus, auspicatíssimam nactus occasiónem qua dogma de immaculáta beátæ Maríæ Vírginis Conceptióne, nuper ab ipso proclamátum, ingentem cardinalium et episcopórum númerum ex dissitis étiam catholici orbis regiónibus Romam attraxerat; die décima Decembris anni — millesimi octingentésimi quinquagesimi quarti, tanta circúmdatus purpuratórum patrum et antistitum coróna, solemniter dedicávit, ejusque celebritátis memóriam hac die recoléndam decrevit.
lessons.en: The Church of St. Peter upon the Vatican fell in course of time to ruins, and having been rebuilt from the foundations, enlarged and garnished, by the zeal of many Popes, was solemnly consecrated anew by Urban VIII, upon the same day, in the year 1628. The Church of St. Paul upon the road to Ostia was almost entirely consumed by fire in the year 1823, but was rebuilt in a more splendid form and, as it were, raised from the dead, by the unwearied zeal of four successive Popes. In the year 1854 Pius IX seized the happy occasion when the doctrine concerning the Immaculate Conception of the Virgin Mary, which he had just set forth, had drawn together to Rome a great multitude of Cardinals and Bishops from all quarters of the Catholic world, solemnly to dedicate this new Church in their presence upon the 10th day of December in the year aforesaid; but he decreed that the yearly Feast in honour of that dedication should be kept upon this day, being the same as that of the Dedication of the Church of St. Peter.

lessons.la: Et cap. o. pigro vos fíliæ Jerúsalem si invenéritis diléctum meum, ut nuntiétis ei quia amóre lángueo. Qualis est diléctus tuus ex dilécto, o pulchérrima mulíerum? qualis est diléctus tuus ex dilécto, quia sic adjurásti nos? Diléctus meus cándidus et rubicúndus: eléctus ex míllibus. Caput ejus aurum óptimum: comæ ejus sicut elátæ palmárum, nigræ quasi corvus. Oculi ejus sicut colúmbæ super rívulos aquárum, qua lacte sunt lotæ, et résident juxta fluénta pleníssima. Genæ illíus sicut aréolæ arómatum, cónsitæ a pigmentáriis. Lábia ejus lília, distillántia myrrham primam.
lessons.en: I sleep, and my heart watcheth; the voice of my beloved knocking: Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is full of dew, and my locks of the drops of the nights. I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if you find my beloved, that you tell him that I languish with love. What manner of one is thy beloved of the beloved, O thou most beautiful among women? what manner of one is thy beloved of the beloved, that thou hast so adjured us? My beloved is white and ruddy, chosen out of thousands. His head is as the finest gold: his locks as branches of palm trees, black as a raven. His eyes as doves upon brooks of waters, which are washed with milk, and sit beside the plentiful streams. His cheeks are as beds of aromatical spices set by the perfumers. His lips are as lilies dropping choice myrrh.

lessons.en: His hands are turned and as of gold, full of hyacinths. His belly as of ivory, set with sapphires. His legs as pillars of marble, that are set upon bases of gold. His form as of Libanus, excellent as the cedars. His throat most sweet, and he is all lovely: such is my beloved, and he is my friend, O ye daughters of Jerusalem. Whither is thy beloved gone, O thou most beautiful among women? whither is thy beloved turned aside, and we will seek him with thee? My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the bed of aromatical spices, to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.

lessons.la: Clemens, Románus, Faustíni fílius, de regióne Cǽlii montis, discípulus beáti Petri, cujus méminit Paulus scribens ad Philippénses: Etiam rogo et te, germáne compar, ádjuva illas quæ mecum laboravérunt in Evangélio, cum Cleménte et céteris adjutóribus meis, quorum nómina sunt in libro vitæ. Hic septem Urbis regiónes divísit septem notáriis, síngulas síngulis attríbuens, qui passiónes Mártyrum et res ab eis gestas, diligentíssime conquisítas, lítteris mandárent. Multa scripsit et ipse accuráte et salutáriter, quibus christiánam religiónem illustrávit.
lessons.en: Clement, the son of Faustinus, was a Roman, from the quarter of the Coelian Mount. He was a disciple of the blessed Peter, and is the same concerning whom Paul saith, writing to the Philippians And I entreat thee also, true yokefellow, help those women which laboured with me in the Gospel, with Clement also, and with other my fellow-labourers, whose names are written in the book of life. ~(iv. 3.) (He succeeded Cletus as Bishop of Rome.) He it was who divided the seven quarters of the city among seven scribes, one to each, whose duty it was to search out most carefully, and record in writing the sufferings and acts of the Martyrs. He himself also wrote much, and that most orthodox and healthy, whereby he clearly explained the Christian Religion.

lessons.la: Um autem doctrína ac vitæ sanctitáte multos ad Christi fidem convérteret, a Trajáno imperatóre relegátus est trans mare Pónticum in solitúdinem urbis Chersónæ; in qua duo míllia Christianórum réperit, qui ab eódem Trajáno condemnáti fúerant. Qui cum in eruéndis et secándis marmóribus aquæ penúria laborárent, Clemens, facta oratióne, in vicínum collem ascéndit, in cujus jugo vidit Agnum déxtero pede fontem aquæ dulcis, qui inde scatébat, attingéntem; ubi omnes sitívi explevérunt. Eóque miráculo multi infidéles, ad Christi fidem convérsi, Cleméntis étiam sanctitátem venerári cœpérunt.
lessons.en: His teaching and the holiness of his life brought many to believe in Christ, and he was therefore exiled by the Emperor Trajan to Kherson, in the Crimea, where he found two thousand Christians, who had been condemned by the same Trajan. There they all worked in the marble quarries. During their labour they suffered for want of water, and Clement prayed, and then went up an hill hard by, on the top whereof he saw a Lamb standing, touching with its right foot a flowing spring of sweet waters. Therewith they all quenched their thirst, and by this miracle many unbelievers were brought to believe in Christ, and began to honour the holiness of Clement.

Furem enim esse osténdit Zábulum, ad detrahénda ex nobis spólia pervígilem, et córporum nostrórum dómibus insidiántem : ut ea incuriósis nobis et somno déditis, consiliórum suórum atque illecebrárum jáculis perfódiat. d E. vii Stolam jucunditátis índuit eum Dóminus, * Et corónam pulchritádinis pósuit Super caput ejus. ℣. Cibávil illum Dóminus pane vite et intelléctus, et aqua sapiéntize salutáris potávit eum. — Et corónam.

resp.a: S. Cleméntis PAPJE Et Mart, prudens, quem constítuit dóminus super famíliam. suam? Quamquam in commune nos ad indeféssam vigilántiae curam adhortétur; speciálem tamen pópuli princípibus, id est Epíscopis, in exspectatióne adventúque suo soallicitúdinem mandat. i R. viii Coróna áurea super caput ejus, expréssa Signo sanctitátis, glória honóris
resp.b: Et opus fortitúdinis.
v: Quóniam prævenísti eum in benedictiónibus dulcédinis: posuísti in cápite ejus corónam de lápide pretióso. — Et opus fortitúdinis.

lessons.la: NC enim servum fidélem atque prudéntem, praepósitum famíilize signíficat, cómmoda atque utilitátes commíssi sibi pópuli curántem. Qui si dicto áudiens, et przecéptis obédiens erit, id est, si doctrínæ opportunitáte et veritáte, infírma confírmet, disrúpta consólidet, depraváta convértat, ct verbum vitze in ceternitátis cibum aléndze famíliæ dispéndat, atque hæc agens hisque ímmorans deprehendátur; glóriam a Dómino tanquam dispensátor fidélis et víllicus útilis consequétur, et super ómnia bona constituétur, id est, in Dei glória collocábitur : qua nihil sit ultra, quod mélius sit.

resp.b: Ut enárrent mirabília tua.
